findings.title: A `partial union` is reported as not partial, and the code fix duplicates the modifier
findings.what_happens_today: `IsPartial` reads the modifiers only when the primary declaration satisfies `SyntaxKind.IsTypeDeclaration`, which lists class, struct, interface, record and record struct. `UnionDeclaration` (kind name from `eng/src/GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter/Syntax-5.10.0.xml:1954-1978`, where `UnionDeclarationSyntax` derives from `TypeDeclarationSyntax`) is not in the list, so the `_ => default` arm returns an empty token list and `IsPartial` is `false` for `public partial union U(...)`. `ProcessTransformationsOnType` then reports `GeneralDiagnosticDescriptors.TypeNotPartial` (LAMA0048) at line 161 and returns without generating a file; `IsInNonPartialSourceType` gives the same answer for types nested in the union. `TheCodeFixProvider` registers LAMA0048 as fixable (line 57), finds the declaration through `BaseTypeDeclarationSyntax` (line 190, which does match a union) and appends a `partial` token (line 173), so applying the fix to a union that is already partial produces `public partial partial union U`, which is CS1004. The C# 15 proposal (`proposals/csharp-15.0/unions.md`, fetched 2026-09-03) permits `partial` on a union declaration and permits members in its body, so this scenario is a supported one: an aspect that introduces a member into a partial union.
findings.consequence_class: Diagnostic reported (a wrong LAMA0048), and silent wrong output (no generated partial file, so introduced members are invisible in the editor).
findings.proposed_change: Make `SyntaxKindExtensions.IsTypeDeclaration` and `IsBaseTypeDeclaration` (line 41) recognise the union kind. The 5.0.0 variant compiles the same source against Roslyn 5.0, which has no `SyntaxKind.UnionDeclaration`, and the repository forbids production branches on a variant constant (`Metalama.Framework/docs/testing.md:58`; FACTS: zero `#if ROSLYN_*` in production). Resolve the kind once at start-up with `Enum.TryParse<SyntaxKind>("UnionDeclaration", out var kind)` into a static field, in the manner of the numeric casts of `Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/Utilities/AllLanguageVersions.cs:14-18`, rather than hard-coding the value 9082 recorded in FACTS, because a preview value may move before the stable release. Add a design-time aspect test (see the test plan under DT-7) and a unit test for `IsPartial` on a union.
findings.confidence: Verified for the code path. That a union symbol reaches this code as an ordinary `INamedType` is verified on Roslyn main (`src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/Symbols/EnumConversions.cs` maps `DeclarationKind.Union` to `TypeKind.Struct`, so `SourceNamedTypeImpl.cs:69-79` returns `TypeKind.Struct` and does not throw) and is plausible for the July build.
open_questions: Whether the stable Roslyn 5.10 keeps `UnionDeclarationSyntax` as a `TypeDeclarationSyntax` (the July grammar says so).
Whether the code model should expose `INamedType.IsUnion`, which is a code-model theme; Roslyn main exposes `ITypeSymbol.IsUnion` (`src/Compilers/Core/Portable/Symbols/ITypeSymbol.cs`).

findings.title: The generated partial part of a union is emitted as `partial struct`, which conflicts with the union declaration
findings.what_happens_today: `CreatePartialType` switches on `INamedType.TypeKind` and `IsRecord`. A union symbol has `TypeKind.Struct` (Roslyn `EnumConversions.cs`) and `IsRecord == false` (the proposal states that a union is a plain struct and that `record union` is not supported), so the `TypeKind.Struct when !type.IsRecord` arm at line 749 emits `partial struct U { ... }`. Roslyn reports `ERR_PartialTypeKindConflict` (CS0261) when two partial parts of one type have different declaration kinds (`src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/Symbols/Source/SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs` on main, `if (t.IsPartial && other.IsPartial) diagnostics.Add(ErrorCode.ERR_PartialTypeKindConflict, ...)`), so the generated file breaks the compilation in the editor as soon as DT-1 lets it be generated. `AddHeader` also matches concrete syntax types (class, struct, record, interface, namespace) and would not put the generated-code header on a `UnionDeclarationSyntax`. The `_ => throw new AssertionFailedException` arm at line 788 is not reached for unions, and if it were, the failure would be contained per group and reported as LAMA0049 (lines 86-105), not as a crash.
findings.consequence_class: Diagnostic reported (CS0261 from the generated document), and the introduced members remain unusable at design time.
findings.proposed_change: Detect a union in `CreatePartialType` (either from the primary declaration syntax kind resolved as in DT-1, or from a new `INamedType.IsUnion` fed by `ITypeSymbol.IsUnion`) and emit a `UnionDeclarationSyntax` part. `SyntaxFactory.UnionDeclaration` does not exist in Roslyn 5.0 and is marked experimental in the July 5.10 build, so build the part from text with `SyntaxFactory.ParseMemberDeclaration` using the parse options of the compilation (the generator already reuses them at lines 54-57), or route through the generated syntax factory of `eng/src/GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter` once the stable grammar no longer strips the node. Extend `AddHeader` to `TypeDeclarationSyntax`. Add a `@TestScenario(DesignTime)` test whose expected `0.i.cs` shows the union part.
findings.confidence: Verified for the generator; plausible for the exact Roslyn behaviour of a generated union part.
open_questions: Whether a partial union part may omit the case-type list. The proposal grammar makes `'(' case_types ')'` mandatory and says nothing about parts, whereas the grammar file declares `ParameterList` as optional on `UnionDeclarationSyntax` (`Syntax-5.10.0.xml:1965`). If every part must repeat the case types, the generator needs the case types, which the code model does not expose; Roslyn main exposes them on `ITypeSymbol` next to `IsUnion`.

findings.title: The design-time diff hashers do not see C# 15 nodes until the grammar is refreshed from the stable Roslyn 5.10
findings.what_happens_today: `RunTimeCodeHasher` and `CompileTimeCodeHasher` are generated with one `Visit<Node>` override per grammar node, and the generator strips every node and field that carries `ExperimentalUrl` (FACTS: `UnionDeclarationSyntax`, `WithElementSyntax`, `UnsafeExpressionSyntax`, and the `Name` field of `BreakStatementSyntax` and `ContinueStatementSyntax`). Two consequences follow. First, `UnionDeclarationSyntax` has no override, so `CSharpSyntaxWalker.DefaultVisit` runs; the walker is constructed with `SyntaxWalkerDepth.Node` (`SafeSyntaxWalker.cs:39`), which visits child nodes and skips tokens, so the union identifier, its modifiers and the `union` keyword contribute nothing to the hash, while the case types, base list and members still do. Second, the generated `VisitBreakStatement` and `VisitContinueStatement` hash only the keyword and the semicolon, because the `Name` field was removed before generation, so the label of a labeled `break` or `continue` is never hashed even by `CompileTimeCodeHasher`, which otherwise hashes bodies. `DiffStrategy.IsDifferent` treats an equal hash as no change (lines 80-85), so the pipeline is not re-run. Observable effects: renaming a union, or adding `partial` to it in response to LAMA0048, in a file with no other change does not trigger re-analysis, so the stale result and the stale LAMA0048 persist until an unrelated edit; changing the target label of `break` or `continue` inside a template does not rebuild the compile-time project, so the template keeps its previous behaviour at design time. Separately, `PartialTypesVisitor` and `PartialTypesHasher` override only class, struct and record, so a partial union is never listed in `SyntaxTreeVersion.PartialTypes` and the partial-type invalidation of `SyntaxTreeChange.cs:111` and `DiffStrategy.cs:97-150` does not cover unions, whereas `DependencyCollector.cs:63-64` does register unions because it tests `BaseTypeDeclarationSyntax`.
findings.consequence_class: Silent wrong output.
findings.proposed_change: As part of the update to the stable Roslyn 5.10 (`Metalama.Framework/docs/updating-roslyn.md:10-12`), copy the stable `Syntax.xml` over `Syntax-5.10.0.xml` and regenerate; the union node and the break and continue `Name` field lose their `ExperimentalUrl` when the features ship in C# 15, so the generator will emit the missing overrides and hash the missing field. Add `VisitUnionDeclaration` overrides to `PartialTypesVisitor` and `PartialTypesHasher` under the same variant constraint as DT-1 (a walker override cannot be resolved by name, so these two classes need a `DefaultVisit` that tests the resolved kind, or the override must live in a file compiled for the 5.10 variant only, which is a policy exception to record). Add a `DiffStrategy` unit test that renames a union and changes a `break` label and asserts that the hash changes, skipped at run time when `LanguageVersionFacts.TryParse("15.0")` fails.
findings.size: S for the regeneration, M with the tests and the partial-type visitors.
findings.confidence: Verified for the generator and the walker depth; the exact token behaviour of `CSharpSyntaxWalker.DefaultVisit` is standard Roslyn behaviour and was not executed here.
open_questions: Whether the stable Roslyn 5.10 grammar still marks any of these nodes experimental. If it does, the repository policy that experimental features are unsupported (`updating-roslyn.md:11`) leaves the gap open, and the DT-1 and DT-2 work would be pointless for that release.

findings.title: The design-time pipeline verifies no language version, so a C# 15 project is silently processed at C# 14 while the build reports an error
findings.what_happens_today: `VerifyLanguageVersion` exists only in `CompileTimeAspectPipeline`, and its comment (lines 64-65) states that Roslyn does not set the language version properly at design time, so the other pipelines do not check it. No file under `Metalama.Framework.DesignTime` or `Engine/Pipeline/DesignTime` reads `LanguageVersion`, `AllowPreviewLanguageFeatures` or `SupportedCSharpVersions` (grep). At design time the compile-time project is compiled with `LanguageVersionProvider`, which caps the project version at C# 14 for any SDK major of 10 or more (line 56, FACTS), and `MSBuildProjectOptions.LanguageVersion` returns `SupportedCSharpVersions.Latest` (C# 14) whenever `LangVersion` does not parse (lines 173-178), which is the case for `15.0` on the consumed July build (see DT-7 for the dating). A project at `LangVersion=15.0` or `preview` therefore analyses without any LAMA diagnostic in the editor, templates that use C# 15 syntax fail in the compile-time compilation with the ordinary "feature is not available in C# 14.0" errors, and the same project fails the build with `CSharpVersionNotSupported`, whose formatting throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` for the value 1500 (`LanguageVersionExtensions.cs:39`, FACTS). The `preview` opt-in `MetalamaAllowPreviewLanguageFeatures` is likewise consulted at compile time only (`CompileTimeAspectPipeline.cs:72`). The generated design-time syntax trees reuse the parse options of the compilation (lines 54-57), so they follow the project language version and need no change.
findings.consequence_class: Diagnostic reported at build only; no impact at design time beyond the inconsistency.
findings.proposed_change: No design-time change once the compile-time analysts add `AllLanguageVersions.CSharp15 = (LanguageVersion) 1500`, extend `SupportedCSharpVersions.All`, `Latest`, `GetMaxLanguageVersion` and `ToDisplayStringSafe`, and extend `LanguageVersionProvider` for SDK major 11. Keep the design-time pipeline free of the version check, because the design-time host may present a Roslyn that maps `Default` differently from the build (the 5.0 variant under Rider maps it to C# 14), and a check there would report against the wrong version.

findings.title: The attribute-adding helper of code actions returns null for unions, and already does so for records and extension blocks
findings.what_happens_today: `AddAttribute` switches on `SyntaxKind` and casts to the concrete syntax type for method, destructor, constructor, interface, delegate, enum, class, struct, parameter, property, event, accessors, operators, indexer, field, event field and compilation unit. `RecordDeclaration`, `RecordStructDeclaration`, `ExtensionBlockDeclaration` and `UnionDeclaration` fall to `default: return null` (line 189-190). The Premium "add aspect attribute" code action then returns `CodeActionResult.Empty` (line 97) and the user sees no change and no message. The unit tests cover classes and methods only (no test mentions records).
findings.consequence_class: Silent wrong output (the code action does nothing).
findings.proposed_change: Replace the per-kind cases for member declarations with a single `MemberDeclarationSyntax.AddAttributeLists` call, which the abstract base type defines and which covers every type declaration kind including unions, and keep the special cases for `Parameter`, accessors and `CompilationUnit`. Add unit tests for a record, an extension block and, under the 5.10 variant, a union.

findings.title: Design-time suppressions are not applied to diagnostics located on a union header
findings.what_happens_today: The suppressor locates the declaring member of each reported diagnostic with `FindSymbolDeclaringNode`, whose kind list names class, struct, interface, record, record struct, enum and delegate but not union (nor extension block). For a diagnostic whose location is on the union header (the identifier, a modifier or a case type), the walk passes over the union node and stops at the namespace, and the loop at lines 202-212 then resolves symbols from the namespace upwards, so a suppression registered on the union type is never matched. Diagnostics located inside a member of the union still match, because the member is found and the walk up from it reaches the union node, on which `GetDeclaredSymbol` succeeds. `FindMemberDeclaringNode` and `GetDeclaringType` have the same omission and are used by other design-time and engine callers.
findings.consequence_class: Diagnostic reported (a suppression that should apply does not).
findings.proposed_change: Base these three helpers on `BaseTypeDeclarationSyntax` and `MemberDeclarationSyntax` type tests instead of enumerated kinds, or add the resolved union kind of DT-1 to each list. Add a suppression test on a union in the design-time test suite.
findings.confidence: Verified for the code; the run-time effect was reasoned from the code and not executed.

findings.title: C# 15 cannot be requested by a test today, and a `@LanguageVersion(15.0)` test is skipped without any failure
findings.what_happens_today: `@LanguageVersion(v)` is parsed with `LanguageVersionFacts.TryParse`; when that fails for an integral value of 10 or more, the test is marked skipped with the reason "not recognized by the current version of Roslyn" (lines 687-691) rather than failed. The Roslyn build consumed by the 5.10 variant is `5.10.0-1.26365.3`; the Arcade date stamp `26365` decodes as year 2026, month 7, day 15 (`yy * 1000 + mm * 50 + dd`), and the Roslyn commit that added `LanguageVersion.CSharp15` ("Add C# 15 language version (#84799)") is dated 2026-08-11 on the GitHub history of `src/Compilers/CSharp/Portable/LanguageVersion.cs` (fetched 2026-09-03). The consumed build therefore has no C# 15 language version; its C# 15 syntax is reachable only under `LanguageVersion.Preview`, which agrees with the `ExperimentalUrl` markers in `Syntax-5.10.0.xml`. Consequently a `@LanguageVersion(15.0)` test is skipped on both variants and the suite reports success with zero C# 15 tests executed. A `@LanguageVersion(preview)` test parses, but the default scenario runs `CompileTimeAspectPipeline`, which rejects `Preview` unless `AllowPreviewLanguageFeatures` is set, and neither `TestOptions` nor `TestProjectOptions` exposes that option (the grep for `AllowPreviewLanguageFeatures` under the two testing projects returns nothing; `DefaultProjectOptions.cs:77` returns `false`). Independently of the directive, the compile-time project of every test is compiled at `SupportedCSharpVersions.Latest` (C# 14) by `TestLanguageVersionProvider`, so a template using C# 15 syntax cannot compile; `TestContext.GetCompilationParseOptions` gives unit tests `DefaultParseOptions` (C# 14) with no way to pass a version; and every aspect test file is also compiled into the test project itself at the project language version (default of the .NET 10 SDK: C# 14), unless its name starts with `__`, in which case it is excluded from compilation (csproj lines 53-55), excluded from discovery (`TestDiscoverer.cs:139`, any leading underscore) and pulled in by a `@Include` directive of another test (`TestOptions.cs:545-549`). `RequiredConstant` and `ForbiddenConstant` work as documented: the constants come from the `DefineConstants` assembly metadata (`Metalama.Testing.AspectTesting.targets:58-61`), and `ROSLYN_5_10_0_OR_GREATER` is defined by the latest variant only (`Roslyn.5.10.0.props:10`); the two existing uses are `Tests/Aspects/DesignTimeInvalidCode/UnknownAccessorInTemplate.cs:7` and its `_Roslyn5_0` counterpart.
findings.consequence_class: Silent wrong output (the suite passes with the C# 15 tests skipped).
findings.proposed_change: Proposed change, as the plan for C# 15 tests: 1. Gate: consume the stable Roslyn 5.10 first (DT-8); until then `15.0` cannot be requested on any variant. 2. Engine: add `AllLanguageVersions.CSharp15`, raise `SupportedCSharpVersions.Latest` and `All` (compile-time analysts). This also raises `DefaultParseOptions` and `TestLanguageVersionProvider`, so templates and unit tests get C# 15 without a further change. 3. Aspect tests: write each C# 15 test with `// @LanguageVersion(15.0)` and `// @RequiredConstant(ROSLYN_5_10_0_OR_GREATER)`, so that the 5.0 variant skips it with a named reason. Because every test file is compiled into the test project, either set `LangVersionOverride=15.0` for the aspect test project (csproj line 22, valid on both variants since Metalama.Compiler compiles both) or put the C# 15 source in a `__Name.cs` companion included with `@Include`. Design-time scenarios (`@TestScenario(DesignTime)`) produce the `0.i.cs` files through `DesignTimeTestRunner.cs:47-67`, and the generated trees carry the project parse options, so union partial parts are testable there; commit the `.t.cs` and `.i.cs` baselines after reading them. 4. Guard against silent skipping: add a unit test that asserts `LanguageVersionFacts.TryParse("15.0")` succeeds when `typeof(SyntaxNode).Assembly.GetName().Version` is 5.10 or above, so that a future Roslyn bump that loses the version fails visibly. 5. Unit tests: add a `LanguageVersion` parameter to `TestContext.GetCompilationParseOptions` and `CreateCSharpCompilation`, or a `TestContextOptions.LanguageVersion` next to `TemplateLanguageVersion` (`TestContextOptions.cs:167`). 6. Preview: add a `@AllowPreviewLanguageFeatures` directive mapped to `TestProjectOptions.AllowPreviewLanguageFeatures` only if tests must run against a preview feature; C# 15 itself does not need it after step 1. 7. HTML: `@WriteInputHtml` and `@WriteOutputHtml` require the `METALAMA_HTML_WRITER` constant, defined for the latest variant only (csproj lines 66-70), and resolve the writer through `IHtmlCodeWriterFactory` (`Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Testing.AspectTesting/TestContextExtensions.cs:19`); `Metalama.Extensions.HtmlWriter` contains no `SyntaxKind` switch (grep), so no change is needed.
findings.size: M for the framework changes, plus the tests themselves.
findings.confidence: Verified for the code paths and for the dating of the consumed build; the claim that the July build lacks `CSharp15` is inferred from the two dates, not from inspecting the build.
open_questions: Whether the stable Roslyn 5.10 maps `Default` to C# 15 (main does, per FACTS), which decides whether tests without `@LanguageVersion` see C# 15 once `DefaultParseOptions` moves.

findings.title: Workspaces, AspectTesting and the LinqPad driver reference a Roslyn version that nuget.org does not serve

findings.title: A .NET 10 host of Workspaces or LinqPad cannot use a machine that has only the .NET 11 SDK
findings.what_happens_today: `MSBuildInitializer` lists the SDKs with `dotnet --list-sdks` and keeps only those whose major version is at most `Environment.Version.Major`, then registers the highest one. The filter is correct, because the MSBuild assemblies of an SDK target the runtime of that SDK and cannot load into an older runtime. The Workspaces package is `net10.0` only (the comment at lines 5-8 explains why), and the LinqPad driver is `net10.0-windows`; the samples state that LINQPad 9 is required, and third-party queries found on GitHub describe LINQPad 9 as running on .NET 10 (`wcrowe/LINQPad-Queries`, header "LINQPad 9 / .NET 10"), which is the only evidence available here since nuget.org carries no `LINQPad.Runtime` 9.x package and linqpad.net is blocked. Under PB-2027.0 the .NET 11 SDK is in the supported set, and a developer who installs Visual Studio 2027 alone has the .NET 11 SDK and not necessarily the .NET 10 SDK. For such a machine, a .NET 10 host throws `MSBuildInitializationException` with the message at lines 91-94, which already names the cause. A .NET 11 host (a `net11.0` application referencing the `net10.0` asset) selects the .NET 11 SDK and loads its MSBuild against the `Microsoft.Build` 18.0.2 compile-time reference; that works as long as MSBuild keeps its frozen assembly version (`Directory.Packages.md:309`), and the pin must not rise because the .NET 10 SDK remains the lowest host (`Directory.Packages.props:35-52`).
findings.consequence_class: Assertion or crash (an exception at workspace load), on a plausible but unverified environment.
findings.proposed_change: Document in the Workspaces and LinqPad READMEs that the host runtime major decides which SDK is usable and that a .NET 10 host needs a .NET 10 SDK; consider a `net11.0` target for the LinqPad driver only if a LINQPad release hosts .NET 11, which is unknown. No code change is proposed for the filter.
findings.confidence: Plausible (the code is verified; the LINQPad host runtime and the Visual Studio 2027 default SDK set are not).
open_questions: The runtime of LINQPad 9 and of any later LINQPad.

Whether the Roslyn 5.10 build host process (`net10.0` and `net472` only, csproj lines 5-8) rolls forward to .NET 11 on a machine without a .NET 10 runtime (the comment in Roslyn's `src/Workspaces/MSBuild/Core/Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Workspaces.MSBuild.csproj` on main says the deployed build host is used so that it can "rollforward to a runtime that supports the SDK version", which suggests that it does).

non_findings: Analyzer shim and variant selection. `RoslynVariantPolicy.TryGetVariantName` (`Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.CompilerExtensions/RoslynVariantPolicy.cs:30-54`) returns `5.10.0` for every host at 5.10 or above, so a Visual Studio 2027 update presenting Roslyn 5.11 or 6.0 is served by the latest variant; `RoslynVariantPolicyTests.cs:36-45` pins 5.10, 5.10.0, 5.11.0 and 6.0.0. `ResourceExtractor.GetHostRoslynVersion` (`ResourceExtractor.cs:633-656`) reads the assembly version of `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis` and handles the JetBrains build. `AssemblyResolutionPolicy.SelectAlreadyLoadedAssembly` (`AssemblyResolutionPolicy.cs:61-80`) accepts a same-or-higher version for non-embedded assemblies, so a host Roslyn above the compile-time reference binds. A host below 5.0 gets no variant and a report file (`ResourceExtractor.cs:157-211`), and the compiler entry point reports LAMA0087 (`MetalamaSourceTransformer.cs:23-31`, `:48-63`). Every other entry point routes through `TryCreateInstance` and holds no version literal (`MetalamaSourceGenerator.cs:25-59`, `MetalamaDiagnosticAnalyzer.cs:35-51`, `MetalamaDiagnosticSuppressor.cs:27-44`, `MetalamaGeneratedCodeAnalyzer.cs:28`, `AdditionalDiagnosticAnalyzer.cs:24`). The embedded resource lists (`Metalama.Framework.CompilerExtensions.csproj:53-70`) name the `net472` and `net10.0` outputs of `Metalama.Framework.CompilerExtensions.Resources.csproj:6`, and `platform-support.md:141-160` records that the Visual Studio private runtime is .NET 10 on the Roslyn 5.10 branch, so no flavour changes. The residual risk is binary: the 5.10.0 variant is compiled against the July preview and loads into the stable Roslyn 5.10 of Visual Studio 2027 with no version check other than the major and minor; an API that changed between the two would surface as a load or missing-method exception written to the crash-report directory (`ResourceExtractor.cs:259-307`) and as nothing in the editor. DT-8 closes this by consuming the stable build before release.

RPC and cross-version contracts. The only kind on the wire is `AspectExplorerDeclarationKind` with the values `Default` and `ReturnParameter` (`Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.DesignTime.Contracts/AspectExplorer/AspectExplorerAspectInstance.cs:60-66`). No file under `DesignTime.Rpc`, `DesignTime.Contracts` or `DesignTime/VisualStudio` mentions `TypeKind`, `SyntaxKind` or `LanguageVersion` (grep). `ProjectKey` carries the assembly name, a preprocessor-symbol hash and a Metalama flag (`ProjectKey.cs:21-25`). Declarations cross the pipe as `SerializableDeclarationId` strings resolved through `SerializableDeclarationIdProvider.ToSymbol.cs:21-39`, and a union is an ordinary named type symbol to that resolution. `RpcContractMessagePackOptions` (`RpcContractMessagePackOptions.cs:37-78`) constrains typeless deserialization to `[RpcContract]` types and `SymbolKey`; nothing there depends on the language version.

Preview and code-action transport. `SerializableSyntaxTree` carries text and annotations; `ToSyntaxTree` re-parses with the caller's options (`Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/DesignTime/JsonSerializationHelper.cs:41-49`, used by `PreviewTestRunner.cs:83` with the original tree options), and `ToSyntaxNode` uses `CSharpParseOptions.Default` (line 52) when a code action is applied in the user process (`CodeActionResult.cs:75`). With a stable Roslyn 5.10 whose `Default` is C# 15, C# 15 text parses; under the 5.0 variant a project cannot be at C# 15 in the first place. The omission of the project's preprocessor symbols in that call is pre-existing and unrelated to this release.

Code lens and refactorings. `CodeLensServiceImpl` reasons on symbols and prints `symbol.Kind` (`CodeLensServiceImpl.cs:189`); `TheCodeRefactoringProvider` resolves `GetDeclaredSymbol(node)` for whatever node is under the caret (`TheCodeRefactoringProvider.cs:104-132`); neither switches on a declaration kind. The live template test runner locates its target by attribute (`LiveTemplateTestRunner.cs:51-56`).

Design-time diff for `with(...)` elements. `WithElementSyntax` is stripped from the grammar, so it has no hasher override, but `DefaultVisit` still visits its `ArgumentList` child, whose arguments are hashed; only the `with` keyword token is lost, which cannot change without the argument list changing shape.

Dependency collection. `DependencyCollector.AddDependency` tests `BaseTypeDeclarationSyntax` and the `partial` token (`DependencyCollector.cs:63-64`), so partial unions register partial-type dependencies.

Generated syntax trees at design time. The generator reuses the compilation's parse options (`DesignTimeSyntaxTreeGenerator.cs:54-57`), so generated documents share the project language version and preprocessor symbols, and `DesignTimeTestRunner` adds them to the input compilation unchanged (`DesignTimeTestRunner.cs:58-66`).

Workspaces packaging under PB-2027.0. The single `net10.0` target (`Metalama.Framework.Workspaces.csproj:18`) is what the baseline requires; a `net11.0` consumer resolves the `net10.0` asset. The `_WorkspacesMSBuildAssetTargetFramework` fallback to `net9.0` (lines 96-98) is dead once the package ships a `net10.0` folder, and the `Error` at lines 117-118 guards the packing. The `build/Metalama.Framework.Workspaces.targets` file imports `../buildTransitive/Metalama.Framework.Workspace.targets`, a path that does not exist (the real file is `Workspaces.targets`, plural); this has been so since the first public commit 046f2e18. It has no effect, because NuGet drops from the `build` asset list every file whose name also appears under `buildTransitive` (`LockFileUtils.AddMSBuildAssets` in NuGet.Client, fetched 2026-09-03), so only the `buildTransitive` file is ever imported. The file can be deleted or corrected at leisure.

Workspaces MSBuild versions. `MicrosoftBuildVersion` is `18.0.2` with the rationale at `Directory.Packages.props:35-52`; the lowest host stays the .NET 10 SDK under PB-2027.0 (`Directory.Packages.md:18-20`), so the pin is unchanged by .NET 11. `Microsoft.Build.Locator` 1.7.8 and `Microsoft.VisualStudio.SolutionPersistence` 1.0.52 (`Directory.Packages.props:151-152`) have no dependency on the SDK major.

LinqPad literals. The only framework literal is the `net10.0-windows` target (`Metalama.LinqPad.csproj:6`); `TargetFramework` strings elsewhere in the driver are project properties read at run time (`Permalink.cs:49`, `SchemaFactory.cs:52-55`). The driver compiles its typed data context with LINQPad's own Roslyn (`MetalamaScratchpadDriver.cs:167-180`), which is independent of the Metalama language version. `LINQPad.Reference` 1.4.0-preview.1 ships `netcoreapp3.0` and `net46` assets (nuspec on nuget.org), so it constrains nothing. The eng build packs `Metalama.LinqPad` alongside Workspaces (`eng/src/Program.cs:108`, `:123`, `:132`).

Observation outside the .NET 11 scope: `Workspace.LoadProjectSetCoreAsync` accepts `.csproj`, `.sln` and `.slnf` only (`Workspace.cs:311-340`), and no file under Workspaces or LinqPad mentions `.slnx`, although `Microsoft.VisualStudio.SolutionPersistence` is referenced. Visual Studio 2026 and 2027 create `.slnx` solutions, so this is worth a separate issue.

Test directives. `RequiredConstant` and `ForbiddenConstant` are evaluated against the `DefineConstants` metadata of the test assembly (`TestInput.cs:74-95`, `Metalama.Testing.AspectTesting.targets:58-61`); `@LanguageFeature` maps to `CSharpParseOptions.WithFeatures` (`TestOptions.cs:720-737`, `BaseTestRunner.cs:226-229`); `@DependencyLanguageVersion` shapes the dependency project (`BaseTestRunner.cs:421-424`). All three behave as documented in `Metalama.Framework/docs/testing.md:147-154`.

Cross-version contracts and the `Metalama.Framework.DesignTime.Contracts.v2` assembly need no change for this release; nothing in the union, closed-class, labeled-break, collection-expression-argument, extension-indexer or static-interface-member features crosses a Metalama version boundary.

findings.title: The build container carries no .NET 11 SDK
findings.what_happens_today: `eng/src/Program.cs:26` sets `dotNetSdkVersion = "10.0.400"` and `eng/src/Program.cs:35-37` holds the only `DotNetComponent`; `eng/docker/build.Dockerfile:43-44`, the two `NonStandardDotNetRoot` Dockerfiles (`DOTNET_VERSION=10.0.302`) and `ReferenceAssemblyArchitectureMismatch/Dockerfile:18` (`SDK_X64=10.0.302`) pin .NET 10 SDKs. `global.json` is generated from the same constant (`platform-support.md:199-201`), so every build and every test runs under SDK 10.0.400. The .NET 11 SDK, which `platform-support.md:195-197` and `Metalama.Framework.props:33,39` declare supported, is never exercised, and no targeting pack for `net11.0` exists on the agent.
findings.consequence_class: Build or restore error for any project that adds `net11.0` before the SDK is added (`NETSDK1045`); no impact until then.
findings.proposed_change: Add a second `DotNetComponent` for the .NET 11 SDK (or the `Microsoft.NetCore.Component.SDK` of Visual Studio 2027 Build Tools, which requires a new `VisualStudioBuildToolsComponentVersion` in PostSharp.Engineering). Decide what `global.json` pins: keeping 10.0.400 keeps parity with Visual Studio 2026 and leaves `LangVersion` defaults at C# 14; pinning 11.0.x makes the default `LangVersion` C# 15 and triggers the `LangVersion` rewrite of `Metalama.Framework.targets:118-120` (see FACTS, line 22) in every standalone scenario that does not set `LangVersion`. Add an `11.0.x` variant of the two docker scenarios that pin `10.0.302`. Read the `MSBuildExtensionsPath` note of `CLAUDE.md` first: two feature bands in one image were the cause of `MSB4062`.
open_questions: Which SDK `global.json` pins.
Whether PostSharp.Engineering 2023.2.420 exposes a Visual Studio 2027 Build Tools component version.

findings.title: `MaximumSdkVersion=11.0` reports LAMA0601 for every .NET 11 SDK
findings.what_happens_today: `Metalama.Framework.props:33` sets `<MaximumSdkVersion>11.0</MaximumSdkVersion>`; `Metalama.Framework.targets:399` computes `_MetalamaSdkVersion` as `NETCoreSdkVersion` with the prerelease suffix removed (for example `11.0.100`); `Metalama.Framework.targets:410-413` evaluates `$([MSBuild]::VersionGreaterThan($(_MetalamaSdkVersion), %(_MetalamaPlatformRequirement.MaximumSdkVersion)))`. With SDK 10.0.400 the comparison `10.0.400 > 11.0` is false and nothing is reported. With SDK 11.0.100 the comparison is `11.0.100 > 11.0`. MSBuild's `VersionGreaterThan` parses through `SimpleVersion`, which treats missing components as zero, so `11.0` is `11.0.0.0` and `11.0.100` is greater. The target framework rule does not have this problem, because `$(TargetFrameworkVersion)` is `v11.0` (`Metalama.Framework.targets:321-322`), which compares equal to `11.0`. The minimum rules are safe for the same reason (`10.0.400 < 10.0` is false).
findings.consequence_class: Diagnostic reported. Every user building with the .NET 11 SDK, which is in the supported set, gets `LAMA0601 'Metalama.Framework' does not support the .NET SDK 11.0.100, which is newer than 11.0`.
findings.proposed_change: Compare the SDK on major.minor only, for example by computing `_MetalamaSdkVersion` as the first two components of `NETCoreSdkVersion`, or document that `MaximumSdkVersion` names the last supported feature band and write `11.0.99999`. Add a scenario `SupportedPlatform.SdkAtMaximum` to `Metalama.Framework/src/tests/Standalone/` with a contributed requirement whose `MaximumSdkVersion` equals the major.minor of the SDK of the build agent and which forbids `LAMA0601`; the existing `Test.LegacySdk` (`SupportedPlatform.ContributedRequirements.csproj:41-43`) uses `1.0` and cannot catch the boundary.
findings.confidence: plausible. The targets were read end to end; the `SimpleVersion` semantics of MSBuild were not executed here and must be checked with one `dotnet build` under an 11.0.100 SDK before anything else in this report.
open_questions: None beyond the verification.

findings.title: The nested compile-time reference project still targets `net8.0`
findings.what_happens_today: `CompileTimeAssemblyLocator.cs:43` sets `_defaultCompileTimeTargetFrameworks = "netstandard2.0;net8.0;net48"`, used at `:209-212` when `MetalamaCompileTimeTargetFrameworks` is empty; at `:415-417`, on a .NET host, the first framework matching `net1*` or `net6`..`net9` is taken as the directory of the additional compile-time assemblies. `Issue1789.csproj:13` and its `README.md` document the scenario as "the same target frameworks as the default"; `CompileTimeTargetFrameworksTests.cs:23-31,52-56` and `IProjectOptions.cs:203` also carry the value. Every build restores a temporary project with a `net8.0` target that PB-2027.0 has dropped (`platform-support.md:297`). Under the .NET 11 SDK, `net8.0` is an end-of-life target framework, so the nested restore emits `NETSDK1138` into a log that is not published (`testing.md:216-217`), and it needs `Microsoft.NETCore.App.Ref` 8.0 from NuGet because the SDK no longer bundles it. A `MetalamaCompileTimePackage` whose package ships only `net10.0` or later assets cannot be restored for `net8.0` (`NU1202`), and the failure surfaces as the reference-assembly build error `LAMA0082`. The `AdditionalCompileTimePackage` scenario (`AzureFunctionTriggerAspect.csproj:14`) passes only because `Microsoft.Azure.Functions.Worker.Extensions.Http` ships a `netstandard2.0` asset.
findings.consequence_class: Build or restore error for packages without `net8.0`-compatible assets; otherwise no impact.
findings.proposed_change: Change the default to `netstandard2.0;net10.0;net48`, which the selection at line 417 already accepts (`net1...`), and update `Issue1789.csproj:13`, its `README.md`, the unit test data and the `IProjectOptions` comment. The cache key of the temporary project includes the framework list (`:213-216`), so existing caches are invalidated once, which is harmless.
open_questions: Whether the documented value of `MetalamaCompileTimeTargetFrameworks` in `Metalama.Documentation` also names `net8.0`.

findings.title: Tests observe `Project.TargetFramework == "net8.0"` whatever the test assembly targets
findings.what_happens_today: `DefaultProjectOptions.cs:56` declares `public virtual string? TargetFramework => "net8.0";` and `TestProjectOptions.cs:129` overrides only `AllTargetFrameworks`; the expected output of `DeclarativeAdviceWithTemplateInitialization.t.cs:17` contains `"net8.0"`. `meta.Target.Project.TargetFramework` and `IProjectOptions.TargetFramework` are `"net8.0"` in every unit, aspect, template and linker test, on the `net48` leg as well as on the `net10.0` leg, although the test framework knows the real value (`TestProjectProperties.cs:32` receives `$(TargetFramework)` from `Metalama.Testing.AspectTesting.targets:108-111`). `ProjectModel.ProjectFeaturesImpl.TargetFrameworkSupportsCovariantReturn` (`ProjectModel.ProjectFeaturesImpl.cs:55-83`) is therefore evaluated on `"net8.0"` in tests. A `net11.0` test leg would keep reporting `net8.0`.
findings.consequence_class: Silent wrong output, confined to tests.
findings.proposed_change: Route `TestProjectProperties.TargetFramework` into `TestContextOptions` and override `TargetFramework` in `TestProjectOptions`; failing that, change the default to `net10.0`. Re-accept `DeclarativeAdviceWithTemplateInitialization.t.cs` and any other snapshot that prints the value. Tests that must be independent of the leg can pin the value through `TestContextOptions`.

findings.title: No test project has a `net11.0` leg
findings.what_happens_today: The five Framework test projects (`AspectTests.csproj:14`, `UnitTests.csproj:7`, `TemplateTests.csproj:14`, `LinkerTests.csproj:14`, `UnitTestHelpers.csproj:8`) target `net48;net10.0`; `Workspaces.csproj:7`, `Engine.Analyzers.Tests.csproj:7`, `Analyzers.Tests.csproj:7` and `Benchmarks.csproj:6` target `net10.0`; `Metalama.Backstage.Tests.csproj:4`, `Metalama.Backstage.Testing.csproj:4` and `Metalama.Testing.Hooks.Tests.csproj:4` target `netframework4.7.2;net10.0`; `Metalama.Backstage.Commands.Tests.csproj:4` and `Metalama.Backstage.Worker.Tests.csproj:4` target `net10.0`; every `Metalama.Patterns/src/tests/*` and `Metalama.Extensions/src/tests/*` project targets `net472;net10.0`, `net10.0` or `net10.0-windows` (full list in the `TargetFramework` survey of this analysis); `Metalama.LinqPad.Tests.csproj:5` targets `net10.0-windows`. `net11.0` is a supported user target framework (`platform-support.md:211-213`) that no automated test executes. The mechanisms that a new leg needs already exist: the `.5.0.0` shims inherit the target frameworks of the base project (`testing.md:43-56`); the aspect test discovery records `TargetFramework` and `TargetFrameworks` per leg (`Metalama.Testing.AspectTesting.targets:108-115`); `@TargetFrameworks` skips a test outside its list (`TestInput.cs:97-117`); extension assemblies are selected with `IsTargetFrameworkCompatible` (`Metalama.Testing.AspectTesting.targets:136`), so the `net10.0` assets of `Metalama.Extensions.HtmlWriter` and `Metalama.Extensions.DiffEngine` (`MetalamaExtensionAssemblies.props:6-11`) serve a `net11.0` leg; program execution is gated by `NET5_0_OR_GREATER` (`AspectTestRunner.cs:239`); every `@RequiredConstant(NET*_OR_GREATER)` gate (139 uses) is satisfied on `net11.0` because the SDK defines the lower `_OR_GREATER` symbols. Three details need attention: the expected `.t.cs` and `.t.txt` files are shared by all legs and are compared per leg under `obj/transformed/<tfm>` (`testing.md:121`), so any output that depends on the .NET 11 base class library (for example overload resolution of `global::System.Console.WriteLine` with a new overload, or a changed `ToString` format printed by `Program.Main`) must be split with `@TargetFrameworks`; `Metalama.Backstage.Tests.csproj:34` conditions the `Microsoft.AspNetCore.App` framework reference on `'$(TargetFramework)'=='net10.0'` and needs a `net11.0` branch; `Metalama.Framework/Directory.Build.props:31` and `Metalama.LinqPad/Directory.Build.props:11` disable code quality analyzers on every leg other than `net10.0`, which is acceptable for a second Core leg. `Metalama.AspectWorkbench/ViewModels/MainViewModel.cs:43-47` hard-codes the preprocessor symbols up to `NET10_0_OR_GREATER`.
findings.consequence_class: No impact today; coverage gap for a supported platform.
findings.proposed_change: After UT-1, add `net11.0` to the five Framework test projects, to the Patterns and Extensions aspect and unit tests, and to `Metalama.Backstage.Tests` (with the framework reference condition widened), run once, and split the snapshots that differ with `@TargetFrameworks`. Keep `Metalama.Framework.Tests.Workspaces` and the benchmarks on `net10.0` unless UT-13 is settled. Add `NET11_0_OR_GREATER` to the AspectWorkbench list. Expect the Core leg of the CI run to double in duration; the `Roslyn.5.0.0` variants double as well because the shims inherit the list.
findings.size: M for the projects, L if many snapshots diverge.
findings.confidence: verified for the mechanisms; the number of diverging snapshots cannot be known without a run.
open_questions: Whether both Core legs, or only `net11.0`, should run in the `.5.0.0` variants.

findings.title: `SupportedPlatform.TestedTargetFrameworks` deliberately omits `net11.0`
findings.what_happens_today: The project comment at `SupportedPlatform.TestedTargetFrameworks.csproj:8-9,14` says that `net481`, `net11.0` and `net11.0-windows` are also in the tested matrix but are not listed here, because the build agents do not have their targeting packs. The scenario proves that `net10.0` and `net10.0-windows` report no `LAMA0600`; the `MaximumNETCoreAppVersion=11.0` boundary (`Metalama.Framework.props:31`, `Metalama.Framework.targets:349-352`) is not exercised.
findings.consequence_class: No impact; coverage gap.
findings.proposed_change: Add `net11.0;net11.0-windows` to `TargetFrameworks` once UT-1 is done; the rest of the scenario, including `test.json`, is already correct.

findings.title: Standalone scenarios run on `net10.0` only, except the two that follow the SDK
where: Metalama.Framework/src/tests/Standalone (92 `<TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>` occurrences across Standalone and DesignTimeStandalone; 69 and 7 scenario directories)
findings.what_happens_today: There are 92 `<TargetFramework>net10.0</TargetFramework>` occurrences across `Metalama.Framework/src/tests/Standalone` and `DesignTimeStandalone` (69 and 7 scenario directories); `BlazorApp.csproj:8` and `Issue1741.csproj:10` use `net$(NETCoreAppMaximumVersion)`; `DefaultLanguageVersion/DotNet/DotNet.csproj:6` (comment still says ".Net 8 project", targets `net10.0`, resets `LangVersion`); `TemplateLanguageVersion14.csproj:4,10`. With the .NET 11 SDK, the two `NETCoreAppMaximumVersion` scenarios switch to `net11.0` by themselves and the remaining 92 keep `net10.0`. `DefaultLanguageVersion/DotNet` is the scenario that will observe the `LangVersion` rewrite to `12.0` described in FACTS line 22 once the implicit language version is 15.0, because it clears `LangVersion` on purpose. The `test.json` `Matrix` and `Properties` entries (`testing.md:230-232`) can build one scenario per target framework by passing `TargetFramework` as a global property, which overrides the value of a single-target project.
findings.consequence_class: No impact today; coverage gap, and `DefaultLanguageVersion/DotNet` becomes an early detector of the C# 15 default.
findings.proposed_change: Choose a subset that exercises runtime behaviour (`CodeCoverage`, `SingleFile`, `CompileTimeContract`, `TestWeaver`, `WriteHtml`, `CompiledBindingsWpf`, `Issue1749*`) and add a two-entry `Matrix` with `Properties: { TargetFramework: net10.0 }` and `net11.0`; leave regression scenarios on `net10.0`. Update the comment of `DefaultLanguageVersion/DotNet.csproj:3`.
findings.confidence: verified for the two self-adjusting scenarios and for the `Matrix` schema; plausible for overriding `TargetFramework` through `Properties` in multi-project scenarios.
open_questions: Whether `ManySolutions` passes `Properties` to `dotnet test` as well as to `dotnet build`.

findings.title: The design-time host simulator and the workspace loader select the SDK by the runtime major version
findings.what_happens_today: `eng/src/DesignTimeSolution.cs:42` sets `_simulatorTargetFramework = "net10.0"`; `Metalama.DesignTime.HostSimulator.csproj:6` targets `net10.0`; `MSBuildEnvironment.cs:48-51` selects the highest SDK with `Version.Major <= Environment.Version.Major`, and `MSBuildInitializer.cs:83-86` applies the same rule; `Metalama.Framework.Workspaces.csproj:5-8,18` is `net10.0` only because `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Workspaces.MSBuild` 5.10 ships `net10.0` and `net472` assets only. The simulator runs on the .NET 10 runtime and therefore never selects the .NET 11 SDK even when it is installed, so no design-time scenario can contain a `net11.0` project (MSBuild of SDK 11 cannot run on .NET 10). The same rule makes `Metalama.Framework.Workspaces`, `Metalama.LinqPad` and `Metalama.Tool` select SDK 11 only when their process runs on .NET 11, which happens for a user application targeting `net11.0` (it receives the `net10.0` asset) and for the tools through `RollForward=Major`.
findings.consequence_class: No impact; coverage gap for design-time scenarios on `net11.0`.
findings.proposed_change: Give `Metalama.DesignTime.HostSimulator` a `net11.0` target and make `_simulatorTargetFramework` follow the SDK of the build (for example the highest installed), then add a `DesignTimeStandalone` scenario with a `net11.0` project. Consider `RollForward=Major` on the simulator instead if a single target is preferred.
open_questions: See UT-13 for the MSBuild version that SDK 11 loads into a process compiled against `Microsoft.Build` 18.0.2.

findings.title: `DoubleTests` in the Contracts unit tests never compiles
findings.what_happens_today: `DoubleTests.cs:5,13` uses `#if NET6_0` (exact symbol) while the project targets `net472;net10.0` (`Metalama.Patterns.Contracts.UnitTests.csproj:4`). `NET6_0` is defined only when targeting `net6.0`, which the project has not done since .NET 6 was dropped; the `StrictlyLessThan` and related facts are compiled out on every leg and nothing reports it.
findings.consequence_class: Silent wrong output (a test that reports nothing).
findings.proposed_change: Replace `NET6_0` with `NET6_0_OR_GREATER` or remove the guard; run the tests.

findings.title: Two aspect tests are gated on a preprocessor symbol that no variant defines
findings.what_happens_today: `Operator.cs:7,10` and `Operator_Explicit.cs:7,10` use `@RequiredConstant(ROSLYN4_4_OR_GREATER)` and `#if NET8_0_OR_GREATER && ROSLYN4_4_OR_GREATER`; the variant symbols in use are listed in `Directory.Packages.md:211-221` and only `ROSLYN_5_10_0_OR_GREATER` exists (`eng/RoslynVersions/Roslyn.5.10.0.props:10`). The symbol name is misspelled relative to the former `ROSLYN_4_4_0_OR_GREATER`, so both tests have been skipped in every variant, and the removal campaign of `Directory.Packages.md:219` did not catch them because the spelling did not match.
findings.consequence_class: Silent wrong output (two tests that never run).
findings.proposed_change: Remove the gates, run the tests, accept the output. This belongs with the test conventions of UT-19 because a C# 15 test suite will add new `@RequiredConstant(ROSLYN_5_10_0_OR_GREATER)` gates, and a misspelled gate is invisible.

findings.title: Runtime dependency pins for the self-hosted bucket and the design-time cap
findings.what_happens_today: Where: `Directory.Packages.props:52-70` (`MicrosoftVisualStudioThreadingLatestVersion` 17.14.15, `MessagePackLatestVersion` 2.5.198, `SystemTextJsonLatestVersion` 10.0.11, `MicrosoftBclAsyncInterfacesLatestVersion` 10.0.11, `SystemTextJsonVersion` fallback 8.0.6, `SystemTextJsonMinVersion` 8.0.6, `SystemNetHttpLatestVersion` 4.3.4, `SystemTextRegularExpressionsLatestVersion` 4.3.1, `SystemFormatsAsn1LatestVersion` 9.0.10, `SystemIOPipelinesLatestVersion` 10.0.11, `SystemBuffersLatestVersion` 4.6.1); `eng/RoslynVersions/Roslyn.5.0.0.props:11-12` (`SystemTextJsonVersion` 9.0.0, required by `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp.Features` 5.0) and `Roslyn.5.10.0.props:11-12` (10.0.11, required by Features 5.10); consumers of the `*LatestVersion` values: `Metalama.Testing.AspectTesting.csproj:25,28-29`, `Metalama.Testing.UnitTesting.csproj:36-38`, `Metalama.Framework.Tests.AspectTests.csproj:43,47`, `TemplateTests.csproj:43,47`, `LinkerTests.csproj:41`, `UnitTests.csproj:57`; user-surfacing pins on the 8.0 line: `Directory.Packages.props:88-94,99,104,108,127,133-134` (`Microsoft.Extensions.*` 8.0.x, `System.Drawing.Common` 8.0.26, `System.DirectoryServices` 8.0.0, `System.IO.Packaging` 8.0.1, `System.Threading.AccessControl` 8.0.0, `System.Collections.Immutable` 8.0.0, `System.Reflection.Metadata` 8.0.0), consumed by `Metalama.Patterns.Caching.csproj:24-27`, `Metalama.Patterns.Caching.Backend.csproj:23-26`, `Flashtrace.csproj:15-17`, `Metalama.Backstage.csproj:21-31`. What happens today, and what .NET 11 changes: (a) nothing has to move to 11.x. For a `net10.0` or `net11.0` consumer the .NET SDK prunes the in-box packages (`System.Text.Json`, `System.Collections.Immutable`, `Microsoft.Bcl.AsyncInterfaces`, `System.IO.Pipelines`, the `Microsoft.Extensions.*` abstractions that ship in the shared framework) from the graph, and the shared framework of .NET 11 provides them; only the `netstandard2.0` and `net472` assets keep the pinned packages, and those assets never run on .NET 11 in a supported configuration. (b) The `SystemTextJsonVersion` per variant is a design-time cap, not a runtime choice: the `Roslyn.5.10.0` payload loads into hosts whose private runtime is .NET 10 (`platform-support.md:144-157`), so it must stay on the 10.0 line; the `Roslyn.5.0.0` payload stays at 9.0.0. Neither may move to 11.x for 2027.0. (c) The `*LatestVersion` values feed only test and self-hosted projects, whose `net10.0` legs prune them anyway; they can stay at 10.0.x and run on .NET 11. (d) The user-surfacing 8.0.x line is already recorded as unjustified by `Directory.Packages.md:44-46` and tracked by #1903; .NET 11 adds no new constraint to it. Vulnerability warnings: what can be verified offline is the set of suppressions and pins, not the advisory database, which NuGet fetches from the package source at restore time and which does not depend on the SDK. The .NET 11 SDK changes three things only: pruning removes in-box packages from the audited graph of `net10.0` and `net11.0` projects; `NuGetAuditMode` was already `all` from SDK 9.0.100 on (the `Metalama.Patterns/src/tests/Directory.Build.props:19` override to `direct` and its comment are stale); `net8.0` becomes an end-of-life target and `NETSDK1138` appears in the nested compile-time restore (UT-3). The recorded suppressions are: `GHSA-8g4q-xg66-9fp4` (System.Text.Json 8.0.4 through `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Features`) in `Metalama.Framework.Package.csproj:30`, `Metalama.Patterns.Immutability.csproj:35` and `Metalama.Patterns.Observability.csproj:35`, whose comments still name "Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Features 4.12.0" and "8.0.4"; with `RoslynApiMinVersion` at 5.0.0 the transitive System.Text.Json is at least 9.0.0 (`Roslyn.5.0.0.props:11`), so these suppressions are probably dead; `GHSA-7jgj-8wvc-jh57` and `GHSA-cmhx-cq75-c4mj` in `Metalama.Framework.DesignTime.Contracts.csproj:42-43` (System.Net.Http 4.3.0 and System.Text.RegularExpressions 4.3.0 through `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.Workspaces.Common` 4.0.1, deliberately pinned). `NU1903` is silenced per reference in `Metalama.Backstage.csproj:26`, `Metalama.Backstage.Tools.csproj:22`, `Metalama.Framework.Engine.csproj:65,68`, `Metalama.Framework.ConfigurationFiles.csproj:10`, `Metalama.Framework.Implementation.Package.csproj:52`, `DesignTime.Contracts.csproj:36` and globally in `Metalama.Backstage/src/tests/Directory.Build.props:7`, `Metalama.AspectWorkbench.csproj:10` and `eng/src/BuildMetalama.csproj:13`; `NuGetAudit` is off in seven analyzer and package projects. None of this changes with the SDK.
findings.consequence_class: No impact.
findings.proposed_change: No version bump for .NET 11. Run `dotnet list package --vulnerable --include-transitive` on each top-level solution under the .NET 11 SDK once it is in the container, remove the three `GHSA-8g4q-xg66-9fp4` suppressions if the report confirms they are dead, rewrite the stale comments (`Directory.Packages.props:6-7,15,62-66,168`, `Immutability.csproj:31-34`, `Observability.csproj:31-34`, `Patterns/src/tests/Directory.Build.props:17-19`), and record in `Directory.Packages.md` that the `SystemTextJsonVersion` of a variant follows the private runtime of the hosts it serves.

findings.title: A union declaration is a struct for every pattern (preamble to UT-14a through UT-14d)
findings.what_happens_today: Roslyn maps `DeclarationKind.Union` to `TypeKind.Struct` (`scratchpad/roslyn/EnumConversions.cs:35-38`), forbids the `ref` modifier on it (`scratchpad/roslyn/SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:341-346`), allows `readonly` without implying it (same lines), forbids instance fields other than the backing field of the synthesized `Value` property and public one-parameter constructors other than the synthesized case constructors (`:2084-2101`), and exposes `ITypeSymbol.IsUnion` and `UnionCaseTypes` (`scratchpad/api/main_Core_Unshipped.txt:31-32`). Metalama maps Roslyn's `Struct` to `TypeKind.Struct` and reads `IsRecord` from the symbol (`SourceNamedTypeImpl.cs:69-79,173`), so, until theme 03 adds anything, a union is an ordinary non-record struct to every aspect. There is no "union case" declaration: the case types are existing types listed in the union's parameter list (`Syntax-5.10.0.xml`, `UnionDeclarationSyntax.ParameterList`), so an aspect on a union case is an aspect on that ordinary type.
findings.consequence_class: See the sub-findings UT-14a to UT-14d.
findings.proposed_change: See the sub-findings UT-14a to UT-14d.
findings.size: See the sub-findings UT-14a to UT-14d.
findings.confidence: See the sub-findings UT-14a to UT-14d.

findings.title: `[Observable]` rejects unions with its existing message
findings.what_happens_today: `ObservableAttribute.cs:52` has `MustSatisfy( x => x.TypeKind is TypeKind.Class, x => $"{x} must be a class or a record class" )`. A union is ineligible, and the eligibility diagnostic is reported. This is the right outcome for a value type whose only state is the synthesized `Value`.
findings.consequence_class: Diagnostic reported (intended).
findings.proposed_change: None in code; one aspect test in `Metalama.Patterns.Observability.AspectTests` asserting the diagnostic on a union.

findings.title: Immutability classifies a union as mutable, which produces Observability warnings
findings.what_happens_today: `ImmutabilityExtensions.cs:55-56` returns deep for delegates, enums, pointers and primitives; `:78-91` classifies a non-`System` value type as `Shallow` only when `namedType.IsReadOnly`, else `None`; `GraphBuildingContext.cs:74-83` (`IsDeeplyImmutable` delegates to `GetImmutabilityKind`); `DependencyGraphBuilder.Visitor.cs:117-127` reports warning `WarningChildrenOfNonInpcFieldsOrPropertiesAreNotObservable` for a stem whose type is neither deeply immutable nor INPC. A union declared without `readonly` is `ImmutabilityKind.None`. In an `[Observable]` class, a computed property that reads `this.Shape.Value` (a union-typed property followed by a member access) reports the warning as if the union could change behind the reference. The compiler guarantees that a union has no instance state beyond `Value`, so `Shallow` (or `Deep` when all case types are deeply immutable) is the accurate classification.
findings.consequence_class: Diagnostic reported (spurious warning).
findings.proposed_change: In `GetImmutabilityKind`, return at least `Shallow` for union types; `Deep` when every case type is deeply immutable. This needs a code model surface for `IsUnion` and the case types (theme 03), because production source may not branch on a Roslyn variant symbol and the Roslyn 5.0 API has no `IsUnion`. Add a unit test in `Metalama.Patterns.Observability.CompileTimeTests`.
open_questions: Whether the compiler will imply `readonly` on unions in the stable Roslyn 5.10.

findings.title: Caching keys and serializes a union as an opaque struct
findings.what_happens_today: Cache keys are built by Flashtrace formatters: `FormatterRepository.cs:141-153` (a struct without a registered formatter gets `DefaultFormatter<T>`), `DefaultFormatterHelper.cs:14-20` (`HasCustomToStringMethod` is true only when `ToString()` is declared below `object`), `DefaultFormatter.cs:57-63,144-148` (without a custom `ToString`, the formatted key is the type name inside braces); serialization: `JsonCachingSerializer.cs:39-56,70,73-89` (`JsonSerializer.Serialize( value )` on the runtime type, then `JsonSerializer.Deserialize( json, type )`). For any struct that does not override `ToString`, all values share the cache key `{Namespace.Type}`. The Roslyn sources in the scratchpad synthesize a `Value` property and case constructors for a union declaration and nothing else (`SourceMemberContainerSymbol.cs:4977-5060`), so a `[Cache]` method with a union parameter returns the entry of the first value for every other value, and `[InvalidateCache]` invalidates by the same collapsed key. The same holds for a union declared with `[CacheKey]` members in another type. For serializing backends, `Value` is get-only and typed `object`, so `Deserialize` returns `default(Union)` with a null `Value` (System.Text.Json does not set get-only properties and has no parameterless-constructor requirement for structs).
findings.consequence_class: Silent wrong output.
findings.proposed_change: Register a formatter for union types in the caching formatter repository that formats `Value` through the repository (needs the runtime `Type` to be recognizable as a union: the compiler emits a marker that `ITypeSymbol.IsUnion` also honours through `HasUnionAttribute`, `SourceNamedTypeSymbol.cs:1463-1467`; the runtime attribute name must be read from the stable Roslyn), and a `JsonConverter` for unions in `Metalama.Patterns.Caching.Backend` that writes the case type and the value. Alternatively, report a build-time warning from `CacheAttribute.BuildAspect` when a parameter type is a union without `ToString`. Add tests with the in-memory backend (key collision) and with `JsonCachingSerializer` (round-trip).
findings.confidence: plausible (rests on the union not synthesizing `ToString`, which the July 2026 sources show and the stable compiler may change).
open_questions: The name of the runtime marker attribute of unions.

findings.title: Multicast treats unions as structs
findings.what_happens_today: `MulticastImplementation.cs:166-178` (`MatchesTypeKind`: `TypeKind.Struct => MulticastTargets.Struct`), `:225-236` (eligibility for `MulticastTargets.Struct`), `:270,291,304,317` (`MustBeExplicitlyDeclared` on members and parameters), `MulticastTargetsHelper.cs:20-40`. An assembly-level multicast aspect with `MulticastTargets.Struct` or `AnyType` selects union declarations, and its member rules select the union's explicitly declared members only, provided the code model reports the synthesized `Value` property and case constructors as implicitly declared (they are `SynthesizedUnionValuePropertySymbol` and `SynthesizedUnionCtor` in Roslyn). This matches PostSharp semantics for structs.
findings.consequence_class: No impact expected.
findings.proposed_change: One aspect test in `Metalama.Extensions.Multicast.AspectTests` with a union and `MulticastTargets.Struct | Method`; adjust the diagnostic wording "is not a struct or record struct" (`:235`) if unions should be named.
findings.confidence: plausible (depends on `IsImplicitlyDeclared` of the synthesized members in the code model, theme 03).

findings.title: Closed classes reach no pattern-specific code
findings.what_happens_today: `IsSealed` decisions: `ClassicObservabilityStrategyImpl.cs:89,223,317,347,415`, `ClassicDesignTimeObservabilityStrategyImpl.cs:70,86,105,140`, `ImplementFormattableAspect.cs:77` (`IsVirtual = !builder.Target.IsSealed`); `IsAbstract`: `MulticastAttributeInfo.cs:288`; type-kind rules of UT-14. Roslyn exposes `ITypeSymbol.IsClosed` and `GetClosedDerivedTypeInfo` (`scratchpad/api/main_Core_Unshipped.txt:14-19`); no Metalama source references either (grep for `IsClosed`, `closed class`: no result). `closed` is a modifier, the type is not sealed, so the patterns introduce virtual members exactly as for an open class, which is valid because a closed class may be derived within its assembly. Inheritable contracts propagate to the derived classes of the hierarchy as usual. No pattern introduces a derived type.
findings.consequence_class: No impact.
findings.proposed_change: None; one aspect test per pattern that introduces virtual members (`[Observable]`, `[CacheKey]`) on a closed class, to keep the expected output under observation when the linker learns the modifier (theme 04).

findings.title: Extension indexers: contracts and the not-null fabric depend on the code model shape
findings.what_happens_today: `EligibilityRuleFactory.Contracts.cs:31-77` holds rules for `IFieldOrPropertyOrIndexer` (writable or readable, explicitly declared, run-time-only declaring type, non-abstract) and `:100-115` the receiver-parameter rules for extension blocks; `ContractExtensions.cs:93-96,104-106` (`VerifyNotNullableDeclarations` adds `[NotNull]` to `t.Indexers` and to the parameters of `t.Indexers`); `NotNullAttribute.cs:41-58`; C# 14 extension member tests exist only in the Framework (`Tests/Aspects/CSharp14/ExtensionMembers/*`, receiver contracts at `ExtensionMembers_Contract_OnReceiver_Property.cs:14-21`), none in `Metalama.Patterns/src/tests` or `Metalama.Extensions/src/tests` (grep for `extension(`: no result). An extension indexer reuses `IndexerDeclarationSyntax` inside an extension block (FACTS, line 28). If the code model lists it in `INamedType.Indexers` of the static class, the Caching fabric (`Metalama.Patterns.Caching/Fabric.cs:14` calls `VerifyNotNullableDeclarations`) and any user fabric will add `[NotNull]` to its reference-typed parameters and the contract advice must be applied to an extension member, which is the C# 14 work of #1159 and #1160 extended to indexers. If the code model does not list it, nothing happens and nothing is reported.
findings.consequence_class: No impact, or a diagnostic or crash inherited from theme 03 and 04.
findings.proposed_change: After theme 03 decides, add `ExtensionIndexer_Contract` and `ExtensionIndexer_Contract_OnReceiver` tests in the Framework suite and a `[NotNull]` test on an extension indexer parameter in `Metalama.Patterns.Contracts.AspectTests`; no Patterns source change is expected.

findings.title: Labeled `break`/`continue` and `with(...)` elements in bodies analysed by patterns
findings.what_happens_today: Metrics: `SyntaxMetricProvider.cs:78,94-108` (`BaseVisitor : CSharpSyntaxVisitor<T>` whose `DefaultVisit` aggregates child nodes), `StatementsCountMetricProvider.Visitor.cs:19-34` (counts `StatementSyntax` nodes), `SyntaxNodesCountMetricProvider.Visitor.cs:18-28` (counts every node), `Metalama.Extensions.Metrics.csproj:13-14` (built against `Metalama.Framework.Sdk`, whose Roslyn is `RoslynApiMinVersion` 5.0.0). Observability: `DependencyGraphBuilder.Visitor.cs:54` (`CSharpSyntaxWalker`), `:280-291` (`Visit` override that only tracks depth), `:305-311` (`VisitArgument` opens a root context), `:409-437` (`VisitIdentifierName` binds the symbol and adds it to the chain), `:205-260` (`ProcessAndResetIfApplicable`: a chain whose first symbol is not a property or private field is `Unsupported`), `:99-105` (`ValidatePathElement` returns null for an unsupported non-field, non-property symbol and its `switch` has no `Label` case), `RoslynHelper.cs:24-77` (`GetAccessKind` returns `Read` for an identifier whose parent is a statement). A `break outer;` inside a computed property getter adds an `IdentifierNameSyntax` that binds to a label symbol; the walker adds it to a chain, the chain is classified `Unsupported`, and no diagnostic and no exception result. This is the path that `goto label;` already takes today, because `GotoStatementSyntax.Expression` is the same identifier shape. A `with(...)` element contributes `ArgumentSyntax` children, which `VisitArgument` analyses like method-call arguments, so property references inside `with(capacity: this.Count)` are recorded as dependencies. For Metrics, `SyntaxNodesCount` grows by one for the label identifier and by the argument nodes of `with(...)`; `StatementsCount` is unchanged because `BreakStatementSyntax` remains one statement. The visitors are compiled against Roslyn 5.0.0 and rely on the Roslyn 5.10 base class dispatching `VisitWithElement` and `VisitUnionDeclaration` to `DefaultVisit`, which is how every generated `Accept` behaves.
findings.consequence_class: No impact.
findings.proposed_change: Add metric unit tests for both constructs in `Metalama.Extensions.Metrics.UnitTests` and one Observability aspect test with a labeled loop in a getter, gated with `@RequiredConstant(ROSLYN_5_10_0_OR_GREATER)`.
findings.confidence: verified by reading the walkers; plausible for `GetSymbolInfo` on a break label, which is not observable offline.
