findings.title: The `LangVersion` clamp rewrites the SDK-implied 15.0 to 12.0 and warns with the wrong explanation
findings.what_happens_today: The condition at line 118 accepts only `12.0`, `13.0`, `14.0`, `default`, `latest`, `latestMajor` and `preview`. A `net11.0` project whose `LangVersion` the SDK sets to `15.0` (A1) and that Metalama.Compiler marks as implicitly set (A1) is rewritten to `12.0` at line 120. The warning at line 245 then states that the version was updated "because 12.0 is the lowest version supported by Metalama Framework", which is false in this direction. The comment at line 115-117 shows that the rewrite was written for target frameworks whose implied version is below C# 12, and the whitelist enumerates the versions known at the time instead of comparing. The same evaluation happens in the design-time build, so the IDE sees C# 12 as well. (Behaviour matrix, scenario (a) SDK-implied 15.0: `15.0` is not in the accepted list, so `LangVersion` is rewritten to `12.0`; the whole compilation is C# 12; `MetalamaCheckLangVersion` at `:243-247` warns without a code, text says `12.0` is "the lowest version supported by Metalama Framework"; `MSBuildProjectOptions.LanguageVersion` (`:167-182`) parses `12.0`; `LanguageVersionProvider.GetLanguageVersionFromDotNetSdk` (`:54-71`) yields `min(C# 14, C# 12)` = C# 12; `VerifyLanguageVersion` passes because C# 12 is in `All`; `EMBED_SYSTEM_TYPES` is not defined for C# 12 (`CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.cs:425-428`); the manifest is serialized as `1200` (`CompileTimeProjectManifest.LanguageVersion` `:96-97`, written at `CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.cs:1282`); `TemplateExpansionContext.CheckTemplateLanguageVersion` (`:861-878`) reports `LAMA0282` for an aspect library built with C# 13 or C# 14 syntax against the C# 12 target; `LinkerAnalysisStep.cs:553` (`< CSharp14`) emits typed lambda parameters (C# 12 branch). Scenario (b) explicit 15.0: `LangVersionImplicitlySet` is not set (A1), no rewrite, warning silent. Scenario (c) preview: `preview` is in the list, no rewrite, warning silent.)
findings.consequence_class: Build or restore error when user code or aspect code uses any feature of C# 13, 14 or 15 (the compiler reports the "feature is not available in C# 12.0" family of errors). Diagnostic reported, with a misleading text and no warning code, when the code happens to fit C# 12. The `Warning` task at line 244 has no `Code` attribute, so `NoWarn` cannot address it.
findings.proposed_change: Replace the enumeration by a comparison. Keep the rewrite only when the implied value is numeric and lower than `12.0`, for example a condition on `$([MSBuild]::VersionLessThan('$(LangVersion)', '12.0'))` guarded by a numeric test, and leave every named value and every version at or above `12.0` untouched. Give the warning a code (the `LAMA06xx` range is used by the platform checks at lines 329-369). Rewrite the text so that it says what happened. Add a standalone scenario `Standalone/DefaultLanguageVersion/DotNet11` that targets `net11.0`, leaves `LangVersion` empty, and uses a C# 14 feature, mirroring `DefaultLanguageVersion/DotNet/DotNet.csproj:5-11` and `Test.cs:24-27`, which target `net10.0` and use a C# 12 feature and therefore cannot detect this defect. That scenario needs the `net11.0` targeting pack on the agents (see LV-9).
findings.size: S for the targets, M including the container change of LV-9.
findings.confidence: Verified for the targets logic; plausible for the value `15.0` and for `LangVersionImplicitlySet` (A1).
open_questions: Whether Metalama.Compiler computes the implied version from its own target-framework table (the comment at line 115 says "according to the current target framework") or copies the SDK value; if it has its own table, `net11.0` may not be marked at all and the rewrite would not fire, which would leave a C# 15 compilation to reach LV-2 instead.

findings.title: `VerifyLanguageVersion` throws instead of reporting `LAMA0052` for C# 15
findings.what_happens_today: With an explicit `15.0` (case b), or with `default`, `latest` or `latestMajor` once the compiler maps them to C# 15 (A3), the first syntax tree carries language version `1500`. It is not in `SupportedCSharpVersions.All`, so line 87 evaluates `languageVersion.ToDisplayStringSafe()` to build the `LAMA0052` arguments, and that call throws (`LanguageVersionExtensions.cs:33-39` has no case for `1500` and throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException`). `SourceTransformer` catches the exception, `CompileTimeExceptionHandler` writes a crash report and reports `LAMA0001` ("Unexpected exception occurred in Metalama"), and `isHandled` is true, so the build fails with an error that asks the user to open a support ticket. The same helper is used by `RoslynVersionSyntaxVerifier.cs:37` and `TemplateExpansionContext.cs:874-875`, which cannot receive `1500` today but will as soon as LV-3 is applied. (Behaviour matrix: `CompileTimeAspectPipeline.VerifyLanguageVersion` (`:62-93`) in scenario (b): `1500` is not in `All`; `ToDisplayStringSafe(1500)` throws before `LAMA0052` is created (`:87`, `LanguageVersionExtensions.cs:39`); in scenario (c) preview: `LAMA0051` unless `MetalamaAllowPreviewLanguageFeatures` (`:70-81`); not a function of the SDK.)
findings.consequence_class: Assertion or crash, surfaced as a `LAMA0001` error. The build does fail, so no wrong output is produced, but the designed diagnostic is not the one the user sees.
findings.proposed_change: Add `(LanguageVersion) 1500 => "15.0"` to `ToDisplayStringSafe`, and replace the throwing default arm by a formatted fallback such as `$"{(int) version / 100}.{(int) version % 100}"` for any value of at least `700`, so that a future version can never turn a diagnostic into a crash again. Add a unit test for values `1300`, `1400`, `1500` and `1600` in `Metalama.Framework.Tests.UnitTests`.
findings.confidence: Verified. The prerelease Roslyn 5.10 must accept `15.0` in `LanguageVersionFacts.TryParse` for the value to reach this site (A3); on the stable 5.10 it will.

findings.title: Every language version table stops at C# 14, and `Latest` cannot simply move to C# 15 because it is shared by the Roslyn 5.0 variant
findings.what_happens_today: Case (b) reaches LV-2. Case (d): `GetLanguageVersionFromDotNetSdk` returns C# 14 for the .NET 11 SDK (SDK major 11 maps to C# 14 at `LanguageVersionProvider.cs:56`), so the compile-time syntax trees are parsed at C# 14 (`CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.cs:351`) and `TemplateLanguageVersion` is C# 14 (`TemplateCompiler.cs:51`); compile-time code that uses C# 15 syntax fails in the compile-time compilation with the compiler's own language-version errors, which are reported through the compile-time diagnostics. The run-time compilation is unaffected. Under `msbuild.exe` the cap comes from `GetMaxLanguageVersion` (`LanguageVersionProvider.cs:111`), which returns C# 14 for the Roslyn of any Visual Studio 2026 or 2027 MSBuild. Sites: `SupportedCSharpVersions.cs:31-32` (`Latest`), `:38-43` (`All`), `:52-62` (`ToLanguageVersion`, both `V5_0_0` and `V5_10_0` map to C# 14), `:149-159` (`GetMaxLanguageVersion`, every Roslyn 5.x maps to C# 14); `AllLanguageVersions.cs:14-18` (no `CSharp15`); `LanguageVersionProvider.cs:54-60` (SDK major 10 or more maps to C# 14). Consumers of `Latest`: `SupportedCSharpVersions.cs:50` (`DefaultParseOptions`), `Options/DefaultProjectOptions.cs:127`, `Options/MSBuildProjectOptions.cs:173-177` (fallback when `LangVersion` does not parse), `Services/CompilationContext.cs:181`, `CompileTime/CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.cs:1355`, `CompileTime/CompileTimeProjectRepository.Builder.cs:596`, `Metalama.Testing.UnitTesting/TestLanguageVersionProvider.cs:12`, `Metalama.Testing.AspectTesting/BaseTestRunner.cs:218`, `CompileTimeAspectPipeline.cs:68`. (Behaviour matrix: `MSBuildProjectOptions.LanguageVersion` (`:167-182`) parses `15.0` in the 5.10 variant (A3); in the 5.0 variant `TryParse` fails and the value silently falls back to `Latest`, that is C# 14; `GetLanguageVersionFromDotNetSdk` (`:54-71`) yields `min(C# 14, C# 15)` = C# 14 for explicit 15.0 and `min(C# 14, Preview)` = C# 14 for preview; `TemplateCompiler.TryReadProjectOptions` (`:56-79`): `MetalamaTemplateLanguageVersion` `15.0` would be rejected with `LAMA0052` because it is not in `All` (`:62-63`); `14.0` passes; `EMBED_SYSTEM_TYPES` is defined (C# 14) in scenarios (b), (c), (d); manifest serialized as `1400` in scenarios (b), (c), (d).)
findings.consequence_class: Diagnostic reported (compiler errors in the compile-time project for C# 15 syntax); no wrong output.
findings.proposed_change: Add `CSharp15 = (LanguageVersion) 1500` to `AllLanguageVersions`; add `CSharp15` to `All`; map the version of the latest variant (`V5_12_0` after LV-13, `V5_10_0` until then) to `CSharp15` in `ToLanguageVersion` and keep `V5_0_0` at `CSharp14`; make `GetMaxLanguageVersion` return `CSharp15` for `(5, >= 10)` and `CSharp14` for other 5.x; map SDK major 11 or more to `CSharp15` in `LanguageVersionProvider`. Define `Latest` as `RoslynApiVersion.Current.ToLanguageVersion()` instead of a constant: the 5.0.0 variant is compiled against Roslyn 5.0, whose parser rejects a `CSharpParseOptions` with language version `1500` through its option validation, and `Latest` feeds `DefaultParseOptions` (`:50`), the unit-test provider and every fallback listed above. `All` can stay a shared constant, because it is only used for membership and for the `LAMA0051`/`LAMA0052` text, which keeps the aspect-test baselines identical in both variants. Sort `FormatSupportedVersions` (`:45`) explicitly, because `All` is an `ImmutableHashSet` and the baselines `Tests/Aspects/Misc/LanguageVersion.t.cs:2` and `Tests/Aspects/LanguageVersion/LanguageVersionPreview.t.cs:2` pin the printed order; both baselines change to include `'15.0'`.
findings.size: M (the code is S; re-running both variants of the aspect suite and adjusting the two baselines and the standalone scenarios is the rest).
findings.confidence: Verified for the sites; plausible for the mapping of Roslyn 5.11 or later to C# 15 (A2).
open_questions: Whether `MetalamaTemplateLanguageVersion` may ever be `15.0` for a library that must also load in Rider (Roslyn 5.0); the answer today is no, and `Directory.Build.props:11-16` already documents that bound, so `TryReadProjectOptions` accepting `15.0` in both variants is correct only because the verifier (`RoslynVersionSyntaxVerifier.cs:41-52`) rejects the syntax at compile time in the 5.0 variant.

findings.title: `CompileTimeProjectManifest.ResolvedLanguageVersion` is dead code and disagrees with the two live fallbacks
findings.what_happens_today: `CompileTimeProjectManifest.cs:99-101` defaults to `CSharp13`; the fallbacks actually used are `CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.cs:1355` and `CompileTimeProjectRepository.Builder.cs:596`, both `manifest.LanguageVersion ?? SupportedCSharpVersions.Latest`. A search of the source finds no reader of `ResolvedLanguageVersion`. No effect. A manifest without a language version, which the comment at line 99 dates to versions whose maximum was C# 13, is re-parsed at `Latest`, that is C# 14, a superset, so nothing breaks.
findings.consequence_class: No impact today. After LV-3, if `Latest` became a constant `CSharp15`, the 5.0.0 variant would re-parse such manifests with an invalid version; the variant-aware `Latest` of LV-3 prevents this.
findings.proposed_change: Delete `ResolvedLanguageVersion`, or route both fallbacks through it with the value the comment documents (`CSharp13`), which is the version such manifests were actually compiled with.

findings.title: The manifest round-trips the language version as an integer and the API version as an enum name
findings.what_happens_today: `LanguageVersionJsonConverter.cs:18-43` serializes the language version as an integer (`CompileTimeProjectManifest.cs:94-97`); `TemplateSymbolManifest.cs:31,49` (`RoslynApiVersion? UsedApiVersion`) is serialized by `JsonStringEnumConverter` (`Serialization/ManifestJsonContext.cs:73`). Tests: `CompileTimeProjectManifestTests.cs:15-68` (including an unknown value `9999`), `ManifestSerializationTests.cs:44,63`. A manifest written by the 5.10 variant with language version `1500` is read by the 5.0 variant as `(LanguageVersion) 1500` without error, because the converter does not validate. The 5.0 variant then creates parse options with that value at `CompileTimeProjectRepository.Builder.cs:596` and `CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.cs:1355`, which Roslyn 5.0 rejects when the compilation is validated. This can only happen once C# 15 is accepted (LV-3), for an aspect library built with C# 15 templates and consumed in Rider.
findings.consequence_class: No impact today; after LV-3, assertion or crash in the Rider variant for that configuration, unless clamped.
findings.proposed_change: When reading a manifest, clamp the language version to `RoslynApiVersion.Current.ToLanguageVersion()` at the two fallback sites, and report a warning that names the versions, so that a library compiled with a newer language than the host understands degrades with a message rather than an exception. The `UsedApiVersion` string form matters for LV-13.
findings.confidence: Verified for the serialization; plausible for the exact Roslyn 5.0 behaviour on an out-of-range version (it reports an error diagnostic on the compilation rather than throwing at construction, which still fails the compile-time build).

findings.title: `OperatorData` is not affected by C# 15, and its `MinimumLangVersion` is not compared to anything
findings.what_happens_today: `OperatorData.cs:151-267` lists the C# 14 compound assignment operators; `:276` is the only use of `MinimumLangVersion`, a null filter. The C# 15 feature list (unions, closed hierarchies, labeled `break` and `continue`, collection expression arguments, extension indexers, static members in interfaces) adds no user-definable operator, so the table is complete. `MinimumLangVersion` is never compared to a language version, so even a wrong value would be silent.
findings.consequence_class: No impact.
findings.proposed_change: None for 2027.0. Optionally use `MinimumLangVersion` to report an introduction of a compound assignment operator into a C# 12 or 13 target, which is a separate defect outside this analysis.

findings.title: The repository's own language ceiling stays at C# 14 and this is correct
findings.what_happens_today: `Metalama.Framework/Directory.Build.props:43-46` sets `LangMaxVersion` `14.0`, exported to other repositories by `eng/src/Program.cs:151`; `Metalama.Extensions/Directory.Build.props:23`, `Metalama.Patterns/Directory.Build.props:26`, `Metalama.Migration/Directory.Build.props:18`, `Metalama.Framework.Tests.UnitTests.csproj:12-16`, `Directory.Build.props:11-16` (`MetalamaTemplateLanguageVersion` `14.0`), `Standalone/TemplateLanguageVersion14/README.md`. Every project of the five solutions compiles with C# 14, including the `.5.0.0` shims that recompile the same source against Roslyn 5.0 (`docs/testing.md:41-58`). Raising `LangMaxVersion` to `15.0` would break the 5.0.0 variant, and raising `MetalamaTemplateLanguageVersion` would break every template in Rider.
findings.consequence_class: No impact.
findings.proposed_change: None. Record in `Metalama.Framework/Directory.Build.props:43-45` that the ceiling is bounded by `RoslynApiMinVersion`, as `Directory.Build.props:11-15` already does for the template version, so that nobody raises it with the release.

findings.title: Test infrastructure already skips C# 15 tests in the Roslyn 5.0 variant
findings.what_happens_today: `TestOptions.cs:681-697` and `:702-718` (`@LanguageVersion` and `@DependencyLanguageVersion` set `SkipReason` when Roslyn does not recognize a numeric version of at least 10), `BaseTestRunner.cs:218-224`. A test marked `// @LanguageVersion(15.0)` runs in the 5.10 variant and is skipped in the 5.0 variant with a reason, which is the behaviour the C# 15 test suites of the other themes need. The default parse options of the aspect suite are `SupportedCSharpVersions.DefaultParseOptions` (`BaseTestRunner.cs:218`), so they follow `Latest` and inherit the variant-aware definition proposed in LV-3.
findings.consequence_class: No impact.
findings.proposed_change: None.

findings.title: Nothing in the repository builds or tests under the .NET 11 SDK or against `net11.0`
findings.what_happens_today: `eng/src/Program.cs:26` (`dotNetSdkVersion` `10.0.400`), `:35-37` (the only `DotNetComponent` of the container), `:61` (the same value generates `global.json`, which `.gitignore:65` excludes), `SupportedPlatform.TestedTargetFrameworks.csproj:8-14` (`net11.0` and `net11.0-windows` are named in the comment and excluded from `TargetFrameworks` because the agents have no targeting pack), `Metalama.Framework.props:30-33` (`MaximumNETCoreAppVersion` and `MaximumSdkVersion` `11.0`, that is, the platform check already admits both). The container carries one SDK feature band on purpose (`Program.cs:19-25` explains the `MSBuildExtensionsPath` conflict between two bands). Consequently the platform test that would have caught LV-1 cannot include `net11.0`, no standalone scenario runs `dotnet build` with the .NET 11 SDK, and the statement of `platform-support.md:338-339` that the `net10.0` toolset rolls forward to .NET 11 is not exercised by continuous integration. The `platform-support.md:196-197` states that the .NET 11 SDK is in the supported set, so the gap is between the doctrine and the test matrix, not inside the doctrine. (Behaviour matrix: `MetalamaCheckSupportedToolchain` (`:391-419`) with `MaximumSdkVersion` `11.0` (`Metalama.Framework.props:33`): no warning in scenarios (a), (b), (c); in scenario (d) `11.0.100` against `11.0`: no `LAMA0601`, on the reading that `[MSBuild]::VersionGreaterThan` pads missing components with zero (plausible, see non-findings).)
findings.consequence_class: No impact on shipped behaviour; coverage gap that hides LV-1 and any .NET 11 SDK regression.
findings.proposed_change: After the `MSBuildExtensionsPath` mitigation described in `CLAUDE.md` ("Changing the build container is riskier than it looks") is in PostSharp.Engineering, add a second `DotNetComponent` for the .NET 11 SDK to `Program.cs:33-59`, keep `global.json` on 10.0.400 for the product build, and add `net11.0` and `net11.0-windows` to `SupportedPlatform.TestedTargetFrameworks.csproj:13` and a `DefaultLanguageVersion/DotNet11` scenario (LV-1). Until the container change lands, an interim scenario can pin the .NET 11 SDK through its own `global.json` only if the SDK is installed, so it has to wait for the component.
findings.size: M, and it consumes at least one continuous integration cycle per the experience recorded in `CLAUDE.md`.
findings.confidence: Verified for the repository; plausible for the PostSharp.Engineering side.
open_questions: Whether the generated `global.json` carries a `rollForward` policy (decided in PostSharp.Engineering, not visible here); without one, a developer machine that has only the .NET 11 SDK cannot run `Build.ps1`, which is the intended pin and not a defect.

findings.title: `net10.0` literals name our own outputs, not the SDK, and are consistent
findings.what_happens_today: `eng/src/BuildMetalama.csproj:5-6` (with a comment pointing at the next site), `Metalama.Framework.CompilerExtensions.csproj:53-54,63-64,88-89` (`bin/$(Configuration)/net10.0` of the Resources project and `eng/src/bin/Debug/net10.0` of the build tool), `Metalama.Framework.CompilerExtensions.Resources.csproj:6` (`net10.0;net472`, "the two frameworks for which csc.exe is built"), `eng/src/DesignTimeSolution.cs:42` and `Metalama.DesignTime.HostSimulator.csproj:6`, `TargetedAssemblyReference.cs:19-20` and `Extensibility/ExtensionLoaderBase.cs:31` (any .NET Core host selects the `net10.0` flavour of an extension assembly), the extension props of DiffEngine and HtmlWriter, `Metalama.Framework/Directory.Build.props:31`, `Metalama.LinqPad/Directory.Build.props:11`, `Directory.Packages.props:35-50` (`MicrosoftBuildVersion` `18.0.2`, bound by `Microsoft.Build.Locator` at run time). findings.consequence_class: No impact.
findings.proposed_change: None for 2027.0. If the Core flavour ever moves, these sites move together; `BuildMetalama.csproj:5` already cross-references one of them.

findings.title: `MSBuildVersion` and the Build Tools component pin Visual Studio 18.9
findings.what_happens_today: `eng/src/Program.cs:40-41` (`VisualStudioBuildToolsComponentVersion.v18_9_2`), `:63` (`MSBuildVersion = new Version(18, 9)`), `:96-99` (the `MsbuildSolution` test that uses `MSBuild.exe`), `Metalama.Framework.props:34-37` (`MinimumVisualStudioVersion` `18.0`, with a comment that the LTSC feature band is measured after 2026-11-10). findings.title: The consumed Roslyn 5.10 prerelease has no stable counterpart, so the stable transition is a renumbering of the latest variant to 5.12.0
findings.what_happens_today: `Directory.Packages.props:25-30` (`RoslynApiMaxVersion` and `RoslynMaxVersion` at `5.10.0-1.26365.3`), `SupportedCSharpVersions.cs:85` (`ToNuGetVersionString` for `V5_10_0`), `updating-roslyn.md:15-17` (the rule that decides between renumbering and adding a variant), `platform-support.md:233-236` ("Roslyn 5.11 or thereabouts") and `:253` (a `5.10` row), `Directory.Packages.md:172,201` (the `5.10+` row and the "about 5.11" cell). The coordinator verified on 2026-09-03 that nuget.org serves the stable `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp` versions 5.0.0, 5.3.0, 5.6.0 and 5.9.0 only, that `eng/Versions.props` on `dotnet/roslyn` `main` reads major 5 and minor 12, that the only release branches are `release/dev18.0` and `release/dev18.3`, and that Roslyn ships a stable every third minor in step with the Visual Studio 2026 quarterly releases. The build `5.10.0-1.26365.3` is therefore a July 2026 build of `main` that will never have a stable counterpart, and the Visual Studio baseline of November 2026 carries Roslyn 5.12, not 5.11. The variant identity `5.10.0` then serves no host in PB-2027.0, which is exactly the renumbering case of `updating-roslyn.md:16`: rename the latest variant rather than add one. Under the rule of `Directory.Packages.md:174-186`, the variant identity must not understate the Roslyn version the payload binds against, so the identity has to become `5.12.0` once the payload references a 5.12 build, and it must not become `5.12.0` before that.
findings.consequence_class: Build or restore error on every user machine if `ToNuGetVersionString` names a package that its source does not serve (`SupportedCSharpVersions.cs:124-129`); silent wrong output if the identity understates the bound version, because `RoslynVariantPolicy` would hand a 5.10 or 5.11 host a payload it cannot load (`Directory.Packages.md:184`).
findings.proposed_change: In two steps that both go through the renumbering procedure of LV-13. Step 1, as soon as Metalama.Compiler builds on a 5.12 prerelease (A2): renumber the latest variant to `5.12.0` and set `RoslynApiMaxVersion`, `RoslynMaxVersion` and `ToNuGetVersionString(V5_12_0)` to that prerelease string, for example `5.12.0-<n>.<build>`; the hyphen keeps the `roslyn-consolidated` source declared (`SupportedCSharpVersions.cs:117-132`), and `Roslyn.5.12.0.props:3` keeps reading `$(RoslynApiMaxVersion)`. Step 2, within three weeks of the stable 5.12 (`platform-support.md:274-276`): edit the same three strings to `5.12.0`, which turns the prerelease source off, and re-derive `SystemTextJsonVersion` in the variant props (`Roslyn.5.10.0.props:11-12` today) from the stable `Features` package. Replace `Syntax-5.10.0.xml` by the 5.12 grammar at step 1 and again at step 2 (`updating-roslyn.md:12`); the experimental attributes that disappear make the generator emit the C# 15 nodes, which is theme 02. Correct `platform-support.md:235` and `Directory.Packages.md:201` from 5.11 to 5.12.
findings.size: S for the strings in each step; the renumbering itself is LV-13.
findings.confidence: Verified for the repository; the Roslyn facts are the coordinator's, verified on 2026-09-03.
open_questions: Whether the stable 5.12 `Features` package raises the `System.Text.Json` floor beyond `10.0.11`.

findings.title: Every site that the renumbering of the latest variant from 5.10.0 to 5.12.0 touches, and its two silent failure modes
findings.what_happens_today: Nothing; both failure modes below are consequences of the renumbering, and `RoslynVariantPolicy` maps a host presenting Roslyn 5.12 to the `5.10.0` variant correctly (see the non-findings). The procedure is `updating-roslyn.md:18-22` (step 8) followed by step 10 (`:29-35`). The sites were found by searching the repository for `5.10.0`, `V5_10_0`, `ROSLYN_5_10_0_OR_GREATER` and `ThisRoslynVersion`, excluding `bin`, `obj` and the grammar files. Sites that follow a property and need no edit: the assembly names (`Metalama.Framework.Engine.csproj:12`, `Metalama.Framework.DesignTime.csproj:9`, every test project, for example `Metalama.Framework.Tests.UnitTests.csproj:10`), the package identity `Metalama.Framework.Implementation.$(ThisRoslynVersionNoPreview)` (`Metalama.Framework.Implementation.Package.csproj:12,84-112`) and its artifact pattern (`eng/src/Program.cs:121`, a wildcard), the Roslyn package overrides (`Metalama.Framework.Engine.csproj:53-55`, `Metalama.Framework.Implementation.Package.csproj:46-48`), the ten `.5.0.0` shim projects under `Metalama.Framework/src` and `src/tests`, `Metalama.Framework.sln` and `Metalama.Framework.LatestRoslyn.slnf` (no version literal), `Metalama.Framework.CompilerExtensions.Resources.csproj:25-26` (it references the latest `DesignTime` project without a suffix and the `5.0.0` shim by name, so a renumbering of the latest variant changes nothing there; `updating-roslyn.md:34` describes the add-a-variant case), and the exported properties of `eng/src/Program.cs:149-152`, through which Metalama.Premium receives the new `RoslynApiMaxVersion` but must still rename its own `Metalama.Framework.Implementation.5.10.0` references and any `TargetRoslynVersion="5.10.0"` metadata (theme 07). Sites named in the procedure that do not exist: `ResourceExtractor.GetRoslynVersion` and `JsonSerializationBinder` (LV-14). The Roslyn version of the host is read by `ResourceExtractor.GetHostRoslynVersion` (`ResourceExtractor.cs:633-661`), which needs no edit, and mapped by `RoslynVariantPolicy.TryGetVariantName` (site 5). The constant `ROSLYN_5_10_0_OR_GREATER` (`Roslyn.5.10.0.props:8-10`) and its two tests (`Tests/Aspects/DesignTimeInvalidCode/UnknownAccessorInTemplate.cs:7`, `UnknownAccessorInTemplate_Roslyn5_0.cs:7`): keep the name. `Directory.Packages.md:215` names a symbol after the Roslyn version at which the distinction appears so that a renumbering does not rewrite its sites, and the distinction (the location of `CS1014`) appeared between 5.0 and the 5.10 build. The renamed props file continues to define it, and the test that requires it keeps running only in the latest variant. If the stable 5.12 moves the diagnostic again, the two baselines change, not the symbol. Silent failure mode 1, extension assemblies: `TargetedAssemblyReference.cs:22-24` accepts an extension assembly only when its declared `TargetRoslynVersion` equals `RoslynApiVersion.Current.ToVersion()` exactly, and `ExtensionLoaderBase.cs:35-37` drops the others without a diagnostic. An extension package that declares `TargetRoslynVersion="5.10.0"` (the pattern of `docs/extensibility.md:128-132`, used by Metalama.Premium) is no longer loaded after the renumbering, and the user sees neither the aspects of that extension nor a message. Consequence class: silent wrong output. Silent failure mode 2, compile-time manifests: `TemplateSymbolManifest.UsedApiVersion` (`:31,49`) is written as the enum name by `JsonStringEnumConverter` (`ManifestJsonContext.cs:73`), so an aspect library built by a 2027.0 preview carries `"V5_10_0"` in its embedded manifest. If the enum loses that member, `System.Text.Json` throws when the consumer reads the manifest. Consequence class: assertion or crash. Keeping `"5.10.0"` in `legacyVersionNames` (site 3) avoids it at no cost, which is what the legacy list at `GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter.cs:17` exists for.
findings.consequence_class: Nothing today. Silent failure mode 1 (extension assemblies): silent wrong output. Silent failure mode 2 (compile-time manifests): assertion or crash.
findings.proposed_change: The eight edit sites: 1. `eng/RoslynVersions/Roslyn.5.10.0.props`: rename to `Roslyn.5.12.0.props`; set `ThisRoslynVersionNoPreview` at line 5 to `5.12.0`; line 3 keeps `$(RoslynApiMaxVersion)`; line 7 keeps the empty suffix; lines 11-12 per LV-12. 2. `eng/RoslynVersions/Latest.props:2`: import the renamed file. 3. `eng/src/GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter/GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter.cs:17-18`: add `"5.12.0"` as the last entry of `versionNames`, and move `"5.10.0"` into `legacyVersionNames` rather than deleting it (see failure mode 2). `Model/SyntaxDocument.cs:22` derives the file name from the version name, so `Syntax-5.10.0.xml` stays and `Syntax-5.12.0.xml` is added. After `Build.ps1 prepare` the generated directory is `.generated/5.12.0` (`Metalama.Framework.Engine.csproj:37-38`, `Metalama.Framework.DesignTime.csproj:34`), and the generated `RoslynApiVersion` enum (`Generator.cs:64-100`) gains `V5_12_0` with `Current` and `Highest` pointing at it while `V5_10_0` remains a member. 4. `Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/Utilities/SupportedCSharpVersions.cs`: `ToLanguageVersion` (`:52-62`) gains `V5_12_0 => CSharp15` (LV-3) and keeps `V5_10_0`; `ToNuGetVersionString` (`:77-87`) gains `V5_12_0` with the string of LV-12; `ToVersion` (`:134-144`) gains `new Version( 5, 12, 0 )`. The `V5_10_0` arms may stay as they are, because the generator keeps the member and the switches must be exhaustive (`:61,86,143` throw on an unexpected value). 5. `Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.CompilerExtensions/RoslynVariantPolicy.cs:111-113`: threshold `new Version( 5, 12 )` and name `"5.12.0"`. `MSBuildProjectOptions.LanguageVersion` (`:167-182`) documents its fallback to `Latest` when the IDE runs a Roslyn older than the project requires; with C# 15 this is the Rider case and is the intended degradation.

`TemplateCompiler.TryReadProjectOptions` (`:56-79`) validates `MetalamaTemplateLanguageVersion` against `All`; `Standalone/Issue1757/OldAspects/OldAspects.csproj:11` pins `12.0` for a library built by 2025.1.18, and the README at `:70-73` explains why. No change for C# 15.

Assumption A1 (from the report's section 'Assumptions about Metalama.Compiler', not a non-finding): `LangVersionImplicitlySet`. `Metalama.Framework.targets:115-118` expects Metalama.Compiler to set `LangVersionImplicitlySet=True` when the project does not define `LangVersion`, with `LangVersion` holding the SDK's implied value at the time the rewrite is evaluated. The analysis assumes the .NET 11 SDK implies `15.0` for `net11.0`, following the `net8.0` to `12.0`, `net9.0` to `13.0`, `net10.0` to `14.0` sequence that the current list at line 118 encodes. If Metalama.Compiler derives the value from its own target-framework table, `net11.0` may be unmarked, and LV-1 does not fire while LV-2 does.

Assumption A2 (from the report's assumptions section, not a non-finding): Roslyn version, the prerequisite of the renumbering. `MetalamaCompilerVersion` is `2027.0.0` (`eng/AutoUpdatedVersions.props:3`) and Metalama.Compiler builds on the Roslyn named by `RoslynApiMaxVersion` (`Directory.Packages.props:25-28`, `docs/updating-roslyn.md:9-10`, whose first step is "Update Metalama.Compiler first"). The renumbering of LV-12 and LV-13 requires Metalama.Compiler to build on a Roslyn 5.12 build before this repository binds its latest variant against 5.12: a payload bound against `5.12.0.0` does not load in a compiler that hosts `5.10.0.0`, and `RoslynVariantPolicy` would then serve that compiler the `5.0.0` variant, which limits every build to C# 14 without any diagnostic. The analysis assumes that the 2027.0 compiler moves to a 5.12 prerelease first and to the stable 5.12 in November 2026, and that any Roslyn at or above 5.10 supports C# 15 (`FACTS.md`, C# 15 feature list). The compile-time compilation is compiled by the host's Roslyn, so the compiler's Roslyn is what `SupportedCSharpVersions.ToLanguageVersion` for `RoslynApiVersion.Current` must describe.

Assumption A3 (from the report's assumptions section, not a non-finding): Command-line language version. The analysis assumes that the compiler's `LanguageVersionFacts.TryParse` accepts `15.0` and that `MapSpecifiedToEffectiveVersion` maps `default`, `latest` and `latestMajor` to C# 15, as the `main` branch of Roslyn does per `FACTS.md`. Whether the consumed July 2026 prerelease already does so is not known; the stable will.

Assumption A4 (from the report's assumptions section, not a non-finding): Host runtime and toolset. `platform-support.md:338-339` records that the `net10.0` toolset and the `Metalama.Compiler.Sdk` tasks declare `rollForward=Major` and run on .NET 11, and `:345-349` records two places that drift when the SDK floor moves. Nothing in this repository contradicts either statement, and nothing tests them (LV-9).

Assumption A5 (from the report's assumptions section, not a non-finding): Properties consumed from the compiler. `Metalama.CompilerVisibleProperties.props:56` states that more properties are exported by Metalama.Compiler; the engine reads the names in `MSBuildPropertyNames.cs:64-102`, of which `MSBuildProjectFullPath`, `TargetFramework`, `NuGetTargetMoniker`, `Configuration`, `MetalamaDebugTransformedCode` and `MetalamaCompilerTransformedFilesOutputPath` are not in the props file of this repository and are therefore assumed to come from the compiler. A rename on the compiler side would be silent, because `MSBuildProjectOptions` returns null or the default for a missing option.

Assumption A6 (from the report's assumptions section, not a non-finding): API surface. The engine implements the compiler's `ISourceTransformer` contract through `Metalama.SourceTransformer/SourceTransformer.cs` and `Metalama.Framework.Engine/Pipeline/SourceTransformer.cs:100-170` (`TransformerContext.ReportDiagnostic`, `AddResources`, `AddSyntaxTreeTransformations`, `Compilation`, `Resources`, `ProjectOptions`), registers an `IExceptionReporter` from `Metalama.Compiler.Services` (`SourceTransformer.CompilerServiceProvider.cs:54-57`), and embeds `Metalama.Compiler.Interface.dll` from the `Metalama.Compiler.Sdk` package (`Metalama.Framework.Engine.csproj:29-33`). `UseMetalamaCompiler=Private` (`Metalama.Framework.Engine.csproj:11`, `Metalama.Framework.Tests.UnitTests.csproj:11`) and `MetalamaCompilerDisablePackCustomization` (`Metalama.Framework.Engine.csproj:10`) are compiler-side properties assumed to keep their names.

Assumption A7 (from the report's assumptions section, not a non-finding): `LAMA0622`. The host-runtime check `MetalamaCompilerCheckHostRuntime` named at `platform-support.md:340-342` lives in the compiler's targets and is assumed to exist as described; this repository's own check (`MetalamaCheckSupportedToolchain`) covers the SDK version and MSBuild version only.

Both ranges match the code, and the ProcessStatement range does support the claim that a compile-time statement is kept unchanged. The VisitIdentifierName range, however, shows that a non-transformed identifier is routed to the compile-time-only rewriter at line 2980 rather than simply returned by the base implementation. The property has nine call sites outside the test projects, the analyzers and its own file, of which two are named by the proposal itself, so the count of eight holds only if IsBaseTypeDeclaration is counted as a site of its own. clusters.title: Hand-written type-declaration kind lists that omit the union declaration
clusters.rationale: Four themes reported the same five places. Verified in the working tree: SyntaxKindExtensions.IsTypeDeclaration enumerates exactly class, struct, interface, record and record struct (Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/Utilities/Roslyn/SyntaxKindExtensions.cs:33-35), IsBaseTypeDeclaration derives from it at :41, and the same enumeration is repeated by hand in SyntaxExtensions at :34, :62 and :117. Every consequence the four findings describe follows from those places: SourceNamedTypeImpl.IsPartial matches on SyntaxKind.IsTypeDeclaration (SourceNamedTypeImpl.cs:344), so a partial union reports false and LAMA0048 is emitted wrongly, the design-time generator never produces a partial file, the suppression path does not reach a union header, and the linker sites of LK-3 fall through. One edit with one shared decision, therefore one work item and not four. The decision inside it is whether the predicate becomes a type test on TypeDeclarationSyntax or gains a union kind; a type test names no experimental member and compiles for both Roslyn variants today.

clusters.title: Syntax visitors and the design-time classifier with no union override
clusters.rationale: CM-7 is the inventory of visitors that inherit the Roslyn dispatch and therefore never see a union declaration, and LK-10 is one member of that inventory, Formatting/TextSpanClassifier.cs:113-119, whose VisitClassDeclaration, VisitStructDeclaration and VisitRecordDeclaration route to a shared helper that a union never reaches. LK-10 also shows that the classifier cannot be corrected alone, because TemplateAnnotator has no union dispatch either and its default path would classify a run-time union as compile-time. Both require an override of a virtual visitor method, which a numeric syntax kind cannot express, so both share the gating mechanism of CL-09.

clusters.title: The compile-time code finder and rewriter drop or copy a union verbatim
clusters.rationale: CM-9 and TP-6 name the same two visitors of CompileTimeCompilationBuilder: FindCompileTimeCodeVisitor, which classifies the declarations of a syntax tree, and ProduceCompileTimeCodeRewriter, whose four type-declaration overrides route to a private VisitTypeDeclaration. CM-9 describes the run-time union in a file that also contains an aspect, which breaks the compile-time compilation with a message about a language version or a missing framework type, and TP-6 describes the union nested in a compile-time class, which is copied verbatim. One override, or one type test that replaces the four overrides, closes both. Two of the three input plans kept them together and the third split them across two stories, which would produce conflicting edits to the same file.

clusters.title: The design-time generated partial part of a union is emitted as a struct
clusters.rationale: Three themes describe one arm of one factory. Verified: DesignTimeSyntaxTreeGenerator.CreatePartialType selects a struct declaration for any TypeKind.Struct that is not a record (DesignTimeSyntaxTreeGenerator.cs:749), and Roslyn reports a union as TypeKind.Struct, so the generated document declares a partial struct against a partial union and the compiler reports CS0261. The three findings agree on the remedy and disagree only on the discriminator and on whether the case list is repeated, which is one decision. LK-4 adds the verified negative statement that the closed modifier needs no counterpart, because the compiler merges the modifiers of partial parts.

clusters.title: Renumbering the latest Roslyn variant to the stable 5.12 and regenerating the syntax model
clusters.rationale: Five themes reported one release step. The consumed Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp is the prerelease 5.10.0-1.26365.3 and no stable 5.10 or 5.11 package exists, so leaving the prerelease feed is a renumbering of the latest variant to 5.12.0 rather than an edit of a label (FACTS.md:48-49). LV-12 decides the target version and the version strings, LV-13 enumerates the eight edit sites and the two silent failure modes of a mismatch, LV-14 corrects the procedure document that the renumbering follows, TP-1, TP-9 and DT-3 are the grammar file and the regeneration that stops stripping the experimental union, with-element and labeled-break nodes, and DT-8 is the same edit seen as a release gate for the three packages published on nuget.org. PR-1 is the mirror edit in Metalama.Premium and is delivered as a separate pull request, because a pull request cannot span two repositories.

clusters.title: Every C# language version table of the engine stops at C# 14
clusters.rationale: Four themes converge on one small set of files. Verified: SupportedCSharpVersions.Latest returns LanguageVersion.CSharp14 (SupportedCSharpVersions.cs:31-32), All lists C# 10 to C# 14 (:38-43), ToLanguageVersion maps both V5_0_0 and V5_10_0 to CSharp14 (:57-60), and GetMaxLanguageVersion returns CSharp14 for every Roslyn 5. LV-2 is the throwing display mapping, LV-3 the tables and the variant-awareness of Latest, TP-2 the same tables seen from the template verifier, TP-8 the template language constants, DT-4 the deliberate non-change at design time, LV-7 the comment that separates the repository ceiling from the product ceiling, and LV-6 the verified statement that the operator table needs nothing for C# 15. The cluster splits by deliverability: the non-throwing display mapping compiles today and is pulled forward, while every assignment of the value 1500 waits for the variant that carries LanguageVersion.CSharp15.

clusters.title: The language version of the compile-time project manifest
clusters.rationale: Both findings concern the same property and the same two reading sites. CompileTimeProjectManifest.ResolvedLanguageVersion documents CSharp13 and is not read, while CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.cs:1355 and CompileTimeProjectRepository.Builder.cs:596 apply their own fallback. LV-5 adds the clamp that a lower Roslyn variant needs when it reads a manifest written at a higher language version, which is the failure that issue #1185 already reported once as CS8192. The property and the clamp cannot be decided separately.

clusters.title: The test harness cannot request C# 15 and skips silently instead
clusters.rationale: Three themes describe the same behaviour of TestOptions: a language version that the running Roslyn does not recognise marks the test skipped with a reason and reports no failure. LV-8 records the tolerance as adequate while C# 15 does not exist, DT-7 records that it would hide a whole C# 15 suite once the suite exists, and UT-19 defines the directory and constant conventions that such a suite follows. One change to a shared harness plus one convention note.

clusters.title: The Roslyn variant gating strategy for the C# 15 API members
clusters.rationale: A single finding, recorded as a cluster because at least fourteen other findings state that their implementation depends on its outcome. Metalama.Framework.Engine.5.0.0 compiles the same source files against Roslyn 5.0, which has neither UnionDeclarationSyntax nor ITypeSymbol.IsUnion, production source carries no conditional compilation today, and the only variant constant exists for two aspect tests (FACTS.md:12). The three candidate mechanisms have different reach: a numeric syntax kind names no absent member but cannot override a virtual visitor method or call a syntax factory, a preprocessor block can but must be renamed with every variant renumbering, and a per-variant service repeats the reflection that issue #1215 deliberately removed.

clusters.title: The .NET 11 SDK is absent from the build container, and nothing runs on net11.0
clusters.rationale: Three themes reported one prerequisite and its dependants. Verified: eng/src/Program.cs:26 declares a single .NET SDK at 10.0.400 and the comment at :19-25 records that two feature bands under one dotnet directory already produced an MSB4062 restore failure. A .NET 10 SDK rejects a net11.0 target framework outright, so no test project, no standalone scenario, no design-time scenario and no Premium leg can name net11.0 until the container changes. The container is separated from the legs that consume it, because its feedback loop is one continuous integration cycle per attempt while the legs can then be added in parallel.

clusters.title: MSBuild platform checks that misreport under the .NET 11 SDK
clusters.rationale: Two defects in the same pair of package build files. Verified: Metalama.Framework.targets:117-120 rewrites an implicitly set LangVersion that is not one of 12.0, 13.0, 14.0, default, latest, latestMajor or preview down to 12.0, and the warning at :243 carries no Code attribute and explains the rewrite falsely. Verified separately: _MetalamaSdkVersion strips only the prerelease label (Metalama.Framework.targets:399) and is then compared with VersionGreaterThan against MaximumSdkVersion 11.0 (Metalama.Framework.props:33, targets:412), so every .NET 11 SDK, including 11.0.100, reports LAMA0601 although the same file declares .NET 11 supported. The second defect is live today and contradicts the matrix that issue #1884 declared.

clusters.title: The November 2026 platform measurement and the host-capped pins
clusters.rationale: Four findings from three themes wait on one calendar date. Verified: eng/src/Program.cs:40 pins VisualStudioBuildToolsComponentVersion.v18_9_2 and Metalama.Framework.props:34-37 states that the November 2026 long-term servicing feature band is measured after 2026-11-10. The Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk pin whose comment still names Visual Studio 2022, the Microsoft.Build pin that doctrine keeps at the lowest supported host, and the dependency audit re-run all read the same measurement. Grouping them avoids four separate reopenings of the same two documents.

clusters.title: Injection, linking, eligibility and the compiler-synthesized members of a union
clusters.rationale: One chain that cannot be broken safely. LinkerInjectionStep.Rewriter.cs:316-322 and LinkerLinkingStep.LinkingRewriter.cs:37-66 each dispatch on four concrete type declaration kinds, so a member injected into a union is never inserted and, once inserted, never linked; repairing only the first produces a worse state than repairing neither. LK-8 is the eligibility half: a union forbids instance fields, auto-properties and field-like events, forbids a public single-parameter constructor and requires every constructor to chain, so a repaired dispatch without eligibility rules turns a dropped injection into code the compiler rejects with the diagnostic on generated code. CM-8 belongs here because its remedy is the linker kind list and LinkerRecordHelper, and because it extends the substitution mechanism of the open pull request metalama/Metalama#1879 rather than duplicating it.

clusters.title: Closed hierarchies across the code model, type introduction and the template compiler
clusters.rationale: One feature with a reader half, a writer half and two verified negative statements. CM-4 and LK-5 propose the same member, INamedTypeBuilder.IsClosed with the emission of the closed token in ModifierHelper.GetTypeSyntaxModifierList instead of the abstract token that the compiler implies; CM-5 is the symmetrical read-only INamedType.IsClosed; TP-10 records that the template compiler and the syntax generator need nothing, with the caveat that a closed compile-time class would need two attributes that the reference set does not provide; UT-15 records that the pattern libraries need no product change and asks only for observation tests. Grouping them lets the product owner defer the whole feature without leaving a half-implemented modifier behind.

clusters.title: Extension indexers across advice, overriding and contracts
clusters.rationale: One advice surface. LK-6 lifts the deliberate rejection of indexers in extension blocks at AdviceFactory.cs:1406, which issue #1587 recorded in the documentation rather than fixed, and adds the eligibility rules the language requires instead; LK-7 is the overriding half and the non-inlined trampoline bounded by the pre-existing LAMA0699 of open issue #937; UT-16 is the contract advice and the not-null fabric over the same member shape. The three share one prerequisite, a compilation that accepts an extension indexer, so none of them can be validated separately.

clusters.title: Labeled break and continue in templates, in inlining and in the metrics
clusters.rationale: One language feature with two independent failure modes and one test set. TemplateAnnotator has no visit for a labeled statement, so the label is dropped and an emitted break targets the innermost loop; independently, the inlining substitution copies user labels verbatim, and labeled loops make a collision between a template label and a target label realistic for the first time. Both read BreakStatementSyntax.Name and ContinueStatementSyntax.Name, which only the regenerated latest variant exposes, so writing them apart would duplicate the gating work. UT-17 records that the metric providers count nodes generically and need no new case, so its value is the tests that pin it.

clusters.title: Switches over declaration kinds that fall through, in both repositories
clusters.rationale: The same shape of defect in four places, none of them caused by C# 15 and all of them reachable today. CSharpAttributeHelper enumerates declaration kinds and returns null for records, record structs and extension blocks, so the add-attribute code action reports success and does nothing; ChangeVisibilityCodeAction in Metalama.Premium skips interfaces and indexers the same way; the member switch of TransformCompileTimeType throws for an indexer and falls through for an extension block, so a template declared inside an extension block is copied verbatim; ReferenceValidationContext.GetInboundGranularity throws for a validated extension block and the exception is reported as an error diagnostic from inside the user validator. In every case the remedy is to test an abstract syntax base type or to add the missing arm, which admits unions later without naming an experimental member.

clusters.title: Pattern libraries, extension libraries and the reference graph on unions
clusters.rationale: UT-14 is the shared premise that a union is an ordinary struct with an opaque Value property for every library that reads the code model, and the four sub-findings are its consequences in Observability, Immutability, Caching and Multicast. PR-12 is the same premise in the architecture rules, and its only product change is one override in the core reference index walker, without which a reference from a union to its case types is never attributed and an architecture rule under-reports with no diagnostic. All six consume the same code model surface and share one test matrix.

clusters.title: Metalama.Premium residuals after Premium#85 and Premium#86
clusters.rationale: Eight findings describe one migration and what it left behind. PR-4 and PR-15 are fully covered by merged pull requests and must not be proposed again: Premium#85 dropped the Roslyn 4.12 variant, made 5.0.0 the lower variant, added the 5.10.0 latest variant with its package source and moved every target framework to net10.0, and Premium#86 retargeted the engineering project and moved the image to the Visual Studio 2026 build tools. The rest are small build-file items with no dependency on the Roslyn gate, apart from PR-2, which is the only Premium item of real size: the Roslyn 5.0.0 variant of the engines is compiled by the solution and executed by no test, and it is the variant that serves Rider and the C# Dev Kit.

clusters.title: Documentation that states the previous baseline
clusters.rationale: Five findings propose prose only, and four of them edit the same two documents, Metalama.Framework/docs/platform-support.md and Directory.Packages.md, even when the subject is in Metalama.Premium. UT-18 is the sweep of the locations that still name net8.0 or C# 14 as the latest, LV-10 is the statement that the remaining net10.0 literals name our own outputs and move only with the embedded Core flavour, DT-9 is the host runtime statement for the introspection packages, and PR-9 and PR-14 extend the drift-point list to the Premium build files. One pull request avoids five conflicting edits to one document.

clusters.title: Residue of the previous platform baseline in engine defaults and in test gates
clusters.rationale: Three leftovers of the move that dropped .NET 8 and .NET 9, sharing one property: each is invisible in a green build and none produces a failure. The default target frameworks of the nested compile-time reference project still name net8.0, so an additional compile-time package resolves its netstandard2.0 asset and an out-of-support target framework is restored on every build. Two facts of the Contracts unit tests are excluded on every leg because their guard names NET6_0 rather than NET6_0_OR_GREATER, and two aspect tests never run because their guard names ROSLYN4_4_OR_GREATER, which no variant defines because the naming convention uses underscores.

clusters.title: The with element and the experimental syntax guard in the template compiler
clusters.rationale: Two findings about the same two files, TemplateAnnotator and the generated meta-syntax rewriter. The with element in a collection expression crashes the template compiler in run-time scope before regeneration and needs only tests afterwards, because the regeneration produces its visitor. The unsafe expression keeps its experimental marker on the target Roslyn and is therefore still stripped, so it needs a name-free guard driven by the generator, which records that a node was removed as experimental, rather than a per-node override that would have to be written again for every future experimental node.

clusters.title: The union in the public code model
clusters.rationale: One finding, recorded separately because it is the surface that six other stories consume. A union is currently indistinguishable from a struct: the TypeKind mapping reports Struct, IsRecord is false, and nothing tells an aspect that instance fields are forbidden. The shape of the member is a product decision, because ITypeSymbol.IsUnion is also true for a hand-written type carrying the union attribute, and the design-time generator and the immutability classification each need the declaration form specifically.

stories.title: Move Metalama.Compiler to the stable Roslyn 5.12
stories.rationale: This story carries no finding, because Metalama.Compiler is not cloned in this session and nothing in it could be verified (FACTS.md:6, :50). It is nevertheless the head of the critical path and must be a tracked item: step 1 of Metalama.Framework/docs/updating-roslyn.md makes every other Roslyn move conditional on it, and the whole C# 15 plan depends on a date that is decided in that repository. The scope is the rebase onto the Roslyn version that Visual Studio 2027 and the .NET 11 SDK carry, expected to be 5.12, since dotnet/roslyn main reads MinorVersion 12 and no stable 5.10 or 5.11 package exists on nuget.org (FACTS.md:48-49). Until it is done, nothing downstream of S09 can start, so its schedule is the single most valuable piece of planning information for 2027.0.

stories.title: Decide and document how engine source names the Roslyn members that only the latest variant has
stories.rationale: CM-10, delivered as a written policy plus one worked example in the smallest consumer. It is the first item of the pre-gate lane and the prerequisite of every union and closed story, so it must be settled before any of them starts and under no time pressure. Metalama.Framework.Engine.5.0.0 compiles the same source files against Roslyn 5.0, whose public API has neither UnionDeclarationSyntax nor ITypeSymbol.IsUnion; issue #1881 removed all conditional compilation from production source and the only variant constant serves two aspect tests (FACTS.md:12). The three mechanisms are not interchangeable: a numeric syntax kind with a runtime guard names no absent member and covers every kind test but cannot override a virtual visitor method or call a syntax factory, a preprocessor block can do both but reverses part of issue #1881 and must be renamed when the variant is renumbered by S09, and a per-variant service repeats the reflection that issue #1215 deliberately removed. The realistic outcome is a documented mixture, and the value of the story is that the mixture is written down once instead of being decided differently at each of the fourteen sites that depend on it. The policy must also settle the RSEXPERIMENTAL006 suppression, which disappears when the latest variant reaches Roslyn 5.12, and what the 5.0 variant does when it meets a referenced union or closed type.

stories.title: Recognise any type declaration by type test instead of by enumerated syntax kind
stories.rationale: CL-01. This is the largest piece of union plumbing that can be delivered before the Roslyn gate, and therefore the highest-value item of the pre-gate lane. Verified: SyntaxKindExtensions.cs:33-35 and :41 and the three enumerations of SyntaxExtensions.cs at :34, :62 and :117 classify a declaration by listing kinds, and SourceNamedTypeImpl.cs:344 matches on SyntaxKind.IsTypeDeclaration, which is why CM-2 sees a wrong LAMA0048 on a partial union, DT-1 sees no generated partial file, DT-6 sees a suppression that does not reach a union header, and CM-6 and LK-3 see the linker consumers fall through. Replacing the enumeration with a test on TypeDeclarationSyntax or MemberDeclarationSyntax names no experimental member and compiles for both variants today, and it also repairs defects that exist now, since interfaces and extension blocks are already missing from several of these lists. Three cautions carry into the implementation: the story must choose between the narrow predicate that the documentation of SyntaxKindExtensions promises, which is a type declaration that can contain members, and the broad Roslyn helper, which also matches delegates, enums and extension blocks and would change shipped behaviour; the KindCheckOptimizationAnalyzer of issue #1307 enforces the kind-check doctrine; and the two consumers named in LK-3 need care rather than widening, because the parameter list of a union is a case list.

stories.title: Correct the LangVersion clamp and the .NET SDK ceiling comparison of the platform check
stories.rationale: CL-11, two MSBuild-only defects in the package build files, delivered before the gate so that the C# 15 enablement pull request does not have to carry them. LV-1: Metalama.Framework.targets:117-120 rewrites an implicitly set LangVersion that is not in its list down to 12.0, so on the day the compiler toolset raises the implied version for net11.0 a project loses C# 13, C# 14 and C# 15 at once, and the warning at :243 has no Code attribute, so it cannot be suppressed through MSBuildWarningsAsMessages, and its explanation is false in that direction. UT-2 is a separate one-line defect that is live today and was verified in this session: _MetalamaSdkVersion strips only the prerelease label (targets:399) and is compared with VersionGreaterThan against MaximumSdkVersion 11.0 (props:33, targets:412), so 11.0.100 reports LAMA0601 although the same file declares .NET 11 supported and the SDK description names 10.0 and 11.0. The repair is a second property holding the first two components, used by the maximum rule only, because the minimum rule legitimately keeps feature-band precision. The standalone scenarios that prove both need the .NET 11 SDK, so the code lands now and the scenarios land with S06.

stories.title: Add the .NET 11 SDK to the build container and decide what global.json pins
stories.rationale: The container half of CL-10, scheduled first among the platform work and in parallel with the Roslyn gate. Verified: eng/src/Program.cs:26 declares the single constant dotNetSdkVersion 10.0.400 and the comment at :19-25 records the MSB4062 restore failure that two feature bands under one dotnet directory produce through a stale MSBuildExtensionsPath. A .NET 10 SDK rejects a net11.0 target framework, so every net11.0 leg, every net11.0 standalone scenario and the two scenarios that prove S03 are blocked here. It is scheduled early because the feedback loop is one continuous integration cycle per attempt and because CLAUDE.md records that the last two container changes each cost one. The mitigation named in CLAUDE.md is incomplete by one entry, MSBuildExtensionsPath in ToolInvocationOptions.BlockedEnvironmentVariables and in MSBuildTool.cs, and that entry lives in PostSharp.Engineering, so it is an external prerequisite of this story rather than a deliverable of this repository.

stories.title: Re-derive the November 2026 baseline: Visual Studio build tools, MSBuild and the host-capped pins
stories.rationale: CL-12, a calendar-gated story rather than a dependency-gated one, kept separate so that it never competes with the critical path. LV-11 is the Visual Studio build tools component, verified at eng/src/Program.cs:40 as v18_9_2, which is a quarterly release below the November 2026 long-term servicing floor that PB-2027.0 names, together with MSBuildVersion; it cannot move until PostSharp.Engineering exposes the newer component version, which is the reason issue #1902 declined the previous attempt. UT-12 is the Microsoft.NET.Test.Sdk pin whose comment still names Visual Studio 2022, UT-13 is the Microsoft.Build pin that doctrine keeps at the lowest supported host and that needs verification rather than a bump once a .NET 11 SDK exists in the image, and UT-11 is the vulnerability audit re-run and the removal of the audit suppressions whose cause the Roslyn floor move removed. All four read the same measurement, which Metalama.Framework.props:34-37 and Directory.Packages.md already schedule after 2026-11-10, so one measurement session serves them all. The audience paragraph of Directory.Packages.md is excluded, because open issue #1903 owns it.

stories.title: Run the test matrix and the standalone scenarios on net11.0
stories.rationale: The coverage half of CL-10, separated from the container so that it can start the day the container lands and be split among several people. The declared support matrix names net11.0 and the .NET 11 SDK and nothing builds or runs on either. UT-5 adds the second Core leg to the test projects, UT-6 adds net11.0 and net11.0-windows to Standalone/SupportedPlatform.TestedTargetFrameworks and corrects the comment that currently records their deliberate absence, UT-7 adds the net11.0 siblings of the standalone scenarios, including one that clears LangVersion so that the implied version is observable and one at the SDK ceiling boundary that proves UT-2, and UT-8 raises the design-time host simulator so that its target framework follows the build SDK rather than a constant. UT-4 must land first inside the story, because DefaultProjectOptions reports a fixed net8.0 to every test, so no test can observe its own leg until that value follows the real target framework, and one aspect test snapshot that prints it has to be re-accepted. PR-8 is the same leg in Metalama.Premium and is the second pull request of this work item, applied to the solution and to the MSBuild-based standalone entries of the Premium eng project. The size is L because the number of expected-output files that diverge between the two legs is unknown until the first run, and each divergence must be read rather than adopted. It must not start before S03, or the SDK ceiling warning fails the scenarios that forbid warnings.

stories.title: Remove the residue of the previous platform baseline from the engine defaults and the test gates
stories.rationale: CL-21, hygiene that is independent of every gate and is scheduled before the C# 15 test suite is written, because that suite will add new constant gates of exactly this shape. UT-3: the default target frameworks of the nested compile-time reference project in CompileTimeAssemblyLocator still name net8.0, so an additional compile-time package resolves its netstandard2.0 asset instead of its net10.0 asset and an out-of-support target framework is restored on every build; the value moves to net10.0 and not to net11.0, because PB-2027.0 keeps a .NET 10 SDK as the build-time SDK, and the fixtures that pin it, including the Issue1789 standalone scenario and its unit test, are edited in the same change. UT-9 and UT-10 are two suites that never run and never fail: two facts of the Contracts unit tests are guarded on NET6_0 rather than NET6_0_OR_GREATER, and two aspect tests are guarded on ROSLYN4_4_OR_GREATER, a name that no variant defines and that the cleanup of issue #1881 missed because it does not follow the underscore convention. Both keep their target framework guard, because the excluded code genuinely does not compile on .NET Framework, and re-enabling them may expose real behaviour differences that have to be read and adopted.

stories.title: Make the language version display mapping non-throwing and settle the compile-time manifest fallbacks
stories.rationale: LV-2 plus CL-07, the part of the language version work that compiles today, pulled out of S11 so that the enablement pull request is smaller and so that no crash path survives it. LV-2: LanguageVersionExtensions.ToDisplayStringSafe maps 1300 and 1400 by numeric cast and has no arm for 1500, so it throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException and replaces the designed LAMA0051 and LAMA0052 diagnostics by a request to open a support ticket; the new arm is a numeric cast and compiles against the Roslyn 5.0 variant as well. LV-4: CompileTimeProjectManifest.ResolvedLanguageVersion documents CSharp13, is read by nothing and disagrees with the two live fallbacks at CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.cs:1355 and CompileTimeProjectRepository.Builder.cs:596, so the story either deletes it or routes both fallbacks through it. LV-5: the reading side gains the clamp and the warning that a library compiled at a higher language version needs when a lower variant reads it, which is the failure that issue #1185 already reported as CS8192. All three become dangerous only after S11 and all three are cheaper to fix now.

stories.title: Renumber the latest Roslyn variant to the stable 5.12 and regenerate the syntax model
stories.rationale: CL-05 without its Premium half, and the gate of the whole release. It is one pull request because the pieces cannot land separately without breaking the build: LV-12 and LV-13 carry the version strings of Directory.Packages.props, the variant property file whose ThisRoslynVersionNoPreview and DefineConstants are hardcoded, SupportedCSharpVersions.ToNuGetVersionString, the version list of the generator whose enum values are positional indices so that the retired name must be inserted in version order rather than appended, RoslynVariantPolicy with its tests, and the variant project names, together with the two silent failure modes of a mismatch, namely that TargetedAssemblyReference compares the declared version by equality and that ExtensionLoaderBase drops a non-matching extension assembly with no diagnostic. TP-1, TP-9 and DT-3 are the regeneration: TreeReader.RemoveExperimentalDeclarations strips every node carrying ExperimentalUrl, which is why no generated visitor, verifier or design-time hasher knows the union declaration, the with element or the Name field of break and continue (FACTS.md:26-27); adding Syntax-5.12.0.xml as a new file and regenerating produces the rewriter members, the version verifier arms and the hashers in one run, and the drift guard that TP-1 asks for must compare against the grammar of the exact consumed package rather than key on a prerelease label, because the unsafe expression keeps its marker. LV-14 rewrites step 10 of updating-roslyn.md, which names members that pull request #1911 renamed. DT-8 is the release gate: Metalama.Framework.Workspaces, Metalama.Testing.AspectTesting and Metalama.LinqPad must not ship a dependency on a Roslyn package that nuget.org does not serve, which already reached a user in issue #1106.

stories.title: Mirror the Roslyn 5.12 renumbering in Metalama.Premium
stories.rationale: PR-1, the Premium half of CL-05, separated only because a pull request cannot span two repositories. It follows Premium#85, which FACTS.md:59 records as open and green and which two of the three input analyses report as merged on 2026-09-03; that pull request left Premium with a latest variant named 5.10.0, two prerelease fallback literals in Directory.Packages.props and a nuget.base.config declaring the roslyn-consolidated feed, and the version string appears in eleven tracked files, including the InternalsVisibleTo entries, the packaging paths and the MetalamaExtensionAssembly items with their TargetRoslynVersion metadata. If the two repositories do not move in the same release, either Premium resolves a preview from a feed that the core has removed, or Premium ships variant assemblies whose names no longer match the variant the core loads, which the extension loader drops without a diagnostic.

stories.title: Enable C# 15 as a supported language version across the engine, the targets and the test framework
stories.rationale: CL-06 and CL-08, the second gate and the story that delivers the headline of the release: after it a 2027.0 preview accepts a C# 15 project instead of reporting LAMA0051. LV-3 raises SupportedCSharpVersions.Latest, which is verified as CSharp14 at :31-32, and All at :38-43, makes Latest variant-aware rather than a shared constant, maps only the renumbered latest variant in ToLanguageVersion, which today maps both V5_0_0 and V5_10_0 to CSharp14 at :57-60, adds the arm to GetMaxLanguageVersion at the version at which the toolset actually raises the implied version, adds CSharp15 to AllLanguageVersions as the numeric cast 1500 and extends LanguageVersionProvider for the .NET 11 SDK. TP-8 carries the MSBuild constants that follow the same decision, including the accepted-value list of the clamp whose warning S03 already corrected, and LV-7 the comment that separates the repository ceiling from the product ceiling. TP-2 is the same tables seen from the template verifier and CompileTimeAspectPipeline.VerifyLanguageVersion, which must report LAMA0052 rather than crash. LV-8, DT-7 and UT-19 make the harness able to request the version instead of skipping silently, and establish the conventions of a Tests/Aspects/CSharp15 directory whose metalamaTests.json names the constant of the renumbered variant. LV-6 and DT-4 close with no code: the operator table needs nothing for C# 15, and the design-time pipeline verifies no language version by design. The story cannot precede S09, because no Roslyn that Metalama consumes before the renumbering has LanguageVersion.CSharp15 and the 5.0 variant rejects the value 1500 (FACTS.md:54-56).

stories.title: Expose the union in the public code model and add the visitor overrides
stories.rationale: CL-23 and CL-02 in part, the first post-gate story and the surface that six later stories consume. CM-1 adds IsUnion and the case types to INamedType beside IsRecord, deliberately without a new TypeKind value, because TypeKind.RecordClass and TypeKind.RecordStruct are already obsolete for exactly that reason and a new value would need an arm in every switch, several of which throw in the default. CM-7 adds the overrides that a type test cannot replace, because CSharpSyntaxVisitor dispatches VisitUnionDeclaration and a numeric kind cannot override a virtual method; this is where the mechanism chosen in S01 is applied at scale. The public shape is a product decision, because ITypeSymbol.IsUnion is also true for a hand-written type carrying the union attribute, and the reads of the case types require the 5.12 baseline, since the public UnionCaseTypes member is absent from the consumed preview (FACTS.md:53).

stories.title: Give the compile-time path and the design-time classifier a union dispatch
stories.rationale: CL-03 plus the classifier half of CL-02, kept together because all three edit visitors that must agree. CM-9 and TP-6 are the same two visitors of CompileTimeCompilationBuilder: a run-time union in a file that also contains an aspect is copied into the compile-time compilation and fails with a message about a language version or a missing framework type, and a union nested in a compile-time class is copied verbatim while one nested in a run-time class is dropped; one override, or one type test that replaces the four overrides and excludes extension blocks, closes both, and the acceptance test is one aspect test that puts a run-time union and an aspect in one file, which is the case a user hits first. LK-10 belongs here rather than with the code model because its fix requires the same TemplateAnnotator dispatch: routing every unhandled type declaration in Formatting/TextSpanClassifier.cs:113-119 to the compile-time helper would classify a run-time union, a run-time interface and an extension block as compile-time and would require the Formatting baselines to be re-adopted.

stories.title: Inject, link and validate advice applied to a union, and read its synthesized members
stories.rationale: CL-13, the story that decides whether an aspect applied to a union produces correct code, wrong code or a clear diagnostic. LK-1 and LK-2 replace the per-kind dispatch of LinkerInjectionStep.Rewriter.cs:316-322 and LinkerLinkingStep.LinkingRewriter.cs:37-66 by a version-neutral one over TypeDeclarationSyntax, which avoids naming a syntax type the 5.0 variant lacks; the fallback must preserve ParameterList, because for a union that list holds the case types, and must not run through the record or struct paths, whose removed-primary-constructor branch would delete it. LK-8 is the defensive slice and is the recommended content of the first pull request: one blanket eligibility rule declaring a union an unsupported advice target covers the three compiler errors that instance fields, auto-properties, field-like events, a public single-parameter constructor and an unchained constructor produce, as well as the silent case where an initializer is injected into a constructor that has no syntax, and it reads the code model member added by S12 rather than the Roslyn flag, because the eligibility rules live in the public assembly, which does not reference Roslyn. CM-8 makes the synthesized Value property and the per-case constructors readable and reachable, and it must be rebased onto the open pull request metalama/Metalama#1879, whose mechanism it extends and whose gates are keyed on IsRecord.

stories.title: Emit a union partial part at design time instead of a struct partial part
stories.rationale: CL-04, the design-time half of union support and the part the user sees first, scheduled directly after the code model because it reads the member added there. Verified: DesignTimeSyntaxTreeGenerator.CreatePartialType selects a struct declaration for any TypeKind.Struct that is not a record (DesignTimeSyntaxTreeGenerator.cs:749), and Roslyn reports a union as TypeKind.Struct, so a union with introduced members shows CS0261 on the type in the editor. Two implementation points are settled here and nowhere else: the discriminator must be the kind of the primary declaration syntax rather than the Roslyn union flag, which is also true for a hand-written attributed type whose generated part must stay a class or a struct, and the generated part must omit the case list, because a second partial part carrying a parameter list is CS8863. LK-4 contributes the verified negative statement that the closed modifier needs no counterpart, because Roslyn merges the modifiers of partial parts.

stories.title: Guard experimental C# syntax in templates and add the with element tests
stories.rationale: CL-22. The template compiler needs less than the other layers, because the regeneration of S09 produces the visitors for the union, the with element and the labeled break automatically. TP-4 therefore reduces to tests after the regeneration, and the finding corrects their location: the file belongs beside the existing collection-expression test of the C# 12 aspect suite rather than in a syntax directory that does not exist. TP-5 is what survives the regeneration: the unsafe expression keeps its experimental marker on the target Roslyn and is therefore still stripped (FACTS.md:32), so the annotator does not reject it and it surfaces as a C# error on the generated compile-time file instead of as a template diagnostic. The remedy is a name-free guard driven by the generator, which records that a node was removed as experimental, so that the same protection applies to every future experimental node without naming one.

stories.title: Support labeled break and continue in templates and rename labels when inlining
stories.rationale: CL-16, one feature with two independent failure modes, both of which produce wrong code without a diagnostic. TP-3: TemplateAnnotator has no visit for a labeled statement, so the scope of the labeled loop is not propagated and the label is dropped, which silently retargets the break to the innermost loop; the fix records label to scope, annotates break and continue from the label, reports a new template diagnostic when a run-time break targets a compile-time loop, and respects that only the immediately nested statement is labeled and that a labeled continue may target only an iteration statement. LK-9: the inlining substitution copies user labels verbatim into a destination that may already declare them, and labeled loops make that collision realistic for the first time, so the fix allocates unique names through the existing lexical scope factory. Both read BreakStatementSyntax.Name and ContinueStatementSyntax.Name, which only the regenerated latest variant exposes, so writing them apart would duplicate the gating work. UT-17 records that the metric providers count nodes and statements generically and need no new case, so its content is two metric unit tests and one observability aspect test with a labeled loop in a getter.

stories.title: Model closed hierarchies in the code model and in type introduction
stories.rationale: CL-14, the cheapest of the C# 15 features and the one most easily deferred, which is why it is a story of its own. Nothing is broken today: a closed class is a class with a modifier that the compiler merges across partial parts and the derived-type model is already correct. CM-5 adds the read-only INamedType.IsClosed and documents that DirectOnly enumeration of derived types is exhaustive for a closed type declared in the current compilation; CM-4 and LK-5 add the settable INamedTypeBuilder.IsClosed with the validation that mirrors the compiler rules and emit the closed token in ModifierHelper.GetTypeSyntaxModifierList instead of the abstract token, which the compiler implies and which is an error if written explicitly. TP-10 is the verified negative statement that the template compiler and the syntax generator need nothing, with the caveat that a closed compile-time class would need two attributes that the compiler does not synthesize and the reference set does not provide. UT-15 adds the pattern library observation tests, which need no product change. The reads are gated by S01 because ITypeSymbol.IsClosed does not exist in the Roslyn 5.0 variant, and the emission needs a compilation at C# 15, hence S11. Union introduction stays out of scope and is a listed decision.

stories.title: Support extension indexers in advice, in overriding and in the contracts
stories.rationale: CL-15, a self-contained feature with no dependency on the union work, so it can run in parallel with S12 to S15 once C# 15 is requestable.
