If every part must repeat the case list, the generator must copy ParameterList from the primary syntax, which is available through type.GetPrimaryDeclarationSyntax().

findings.title: Introduced types cannot be closed, and an introduced closed class would be emitted as abstract
where: Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework/Code/DeclarationBuilders/IMemberOrNamedTypeBuilder.cs:64-95 (settable IsSealed, IsAbstract, IsStatic, IsPartial; no IsClosed)
Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/CodeModel/Helpers/ModifierHelper.cs:198-236 (GetTypeSyntaxModifierList emits abstract when IsAbstract and sealed when IsSealed)
Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/CodeModel/Introductions/Builders/NamedTypeBuilder.cs:52-53 (asserts class, struct, interface or extension and !isRecord)
findings.what_happens_today: The public API has IntroduceClass and IntroduceInterface; there is no IntroduceStruct, IntroduceRecord or IntroduceUnion, and NamedTypeBuilder rejects records by assertion. A closed class cannot be introduced because no builder property exists. If IsClosed is added by copying IsAbstract, ModifierHelper would emit `abstract closed class`, which Roslyn rejects with ERR_ClosedExplicitlyAbstract.
findings.consequence_class: No impact today (the feature is absent); assertion or crash only for the future implementation if ModifierHelper is not adapted.
findings.proposed_change: Add `bool IsClosed { get; set; }` to INamedTypeBuilder (closed applies to classes only, so not to IMemberOrNamedTypeBuilder), validate in the setter that TypeKind is Class, that IsSealed and IsStatic are false, and make IsAbstract read true when IsClosed is true, mirroring Roslyn. Store it in NamedTypeBuilderData, expose it in IntroducedNamedType, and in GetTypeSyntaxModifierList emit Token(SyntaxKind.ClosedKeyword) and skip `abstract` when the type is closed. Do not add union introduction for 2027.0: record introduction is not supported either, and a union declaration requires a case list that the builder has no model for.
open_questions: Whether the `closed` token should be placed before `partial` (Roslyn requires `partial` immediately before `class`, so the order is `closed partial class`).

findings.title: IsClosed is not exposed; the derived closedness is otherwise modelled correctly
findings.what_happens_today: Roslyn sets the Abstract flag on a closed class, so IsAbstract is true, IsSealed is false, CanBeInherited is true, HasDefaultConstructor is false and MustNotBeAbstract rejects the type. All of this is semantically right. Nothing tells an aspect that the set of direct subtypes is complete, so validators that use DerivedTypesOptions.IncludingExternalTypesDangerous cannot take the shortcut that closedness allows, and an aspect cannot exploit the exhaustiveness guarantee of the proposal.
findings.consequence_class: No impact.
findings.proposed_change: Add `bool IsClosed { get; }` to INamedType, read from ITypeSymbol.IsClosed in SourceNamedTypeImpl, false in builders and introduced types unless CM-4 is implemented, and mention in the DerivedTypesOptions documentation that for a closed type DirectOnly is exhaustive. Consider GetClosedDerivedTypeInfo as a faster source for GetDerivedTypes of a closed type only if the index cannot answer it already; the index already records every subtype in the current compilation, which is the whole set for a closed type.
findings.confidence: Verified for the current behaviour; plausible for the Roslyn member.
open_questions: Whether [CompilerFeatureRequired("ClosedClasses")], which the compiler synthesizes on every constructor of a closed class, appears in IConstructor.Attributes for constructors read from metadata, and whether any advice that copies constructor attributes (forwarding constructors, pulled parameters) would copy it. This is a linker and advice question (theme 04).

findings.title: Hand-written lists of type-declaration syntax kinds omit UnionDeclaration
findings.what_happens_today: For the code-model sites: ToInsertPosition(ISymbol) takes the primary declaration of the union type (a UnionDeclarationSyntax) and calls FindMemberDeclaration, which walks up the ancestors until it finds a kind in the list at SyntaxExtensions.cs:30-36. The union kind is not in the list, so the walk continues to the enclosing namespace declaration, which is in the list, and the insert position becomes After the namespace declaration rather than Within the union; members introduced into a union are therefore positioned outside the type. When the union is declared in the global namespace the walk reaches the compilation unit, returns null, and FindMemberDeclaration throws AssertionFailedException at :21. The same applies to a synthesized union member, whose position is computed from symbol.ContainingType.GetPrimaryDeclarationSyntax() at CodeModelExtensions.cs:86-88. GetDeclaringType returns the enclosing type of the union instead of the union. HasModifier returns false for every modifier of a union type (harmless: the type modifier list is built from IsStatic, IsAbstract and IsSealed, not from HasModifier). HasNewKeyword reaches the default MemberDeclarationSyntax arm and answers from the union modifiers, which is correct. The complete list, including the linker, compile-time and test-framework sites, is in the exhaustiveness table.
findings.consequence_class: Assertion or crash (global namespace) or silent wrong output (namespace) for any member introduced into a union; silent for the rest.
findings.proposed_change: Add SyntaxKind.UnionDeclaration to each list. Where a list is a hand-written copy of Roslyn's SyntaxFacts.IsTypeDeclaration, replace the copy by the Roslyn helper, which ReferenceIndexWalker.cs:211 already uses and which Roslyn updates for the new kind. Add a unit test in Metalama.Framework/src/tests/Metalama.Framework.Tests.UnitTests/CodeModel/ that resolves ToInsertPosition for a union in the global namespace and for one in a namespace.
findings.size: S for the code-model sites; the linker, templating and design-time sites are counted in their own themes.

findings.title: Syntax visitors have no VisitUnionDeclaration override
findings.what_happens_today: Roslyn's generated CSharpSyntaxVisitor.VisitUnionDeclaration calls DefaultVisit, which in a CSharpSyntaxWalker visits the children and in a CSharpSyntaxRewriter rewrites the children. The Metalama visitors therefore descend into the members of a union but skip the logic they run at the type level. For the two dependency visitors this means that a union declared in a file is not recorded as a declared type, so the design-time dependency graph does not know that the file declares it; a change to the union does not invalidate the aspects that depend on it (silent). The templating, compile-time, linker, reference-graph, formatting and design-time diff visitors are listed in the exhaustiveness table with a one-line consequence each and belong to themes 02, 04 and 05. The 20 files are listed in the exhaustiveness table; the code-model ones are the two DependencyAnalysisHelper visitors.
findings.consequence_class: Silent wrong output.
findings.proposed_change: Add VisitUnionDeclaration overrides that route to the same helper as VisitStructDeclaration. Because UnionDeclarationSyntax is marked experimental in the prerelease grammar, the overrides need the experimental diagnostic suppressed until the stable grammar drops the attribute (FACTS.md). Extend Find-KindOptimizationCandidates.ps1 or the KindCheckOptimizationAnalyzer with a rule that flags a visitor overriding VisitStructDeclaration without VisitUnionDeclaration, so that the omission cannot recur.
findings.size: S per visitor; M in total across themes.

findings.title: The synthesized union members reach the code model with syntax the model does not expect
where: Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/CodeModel/Helpers/DeclarationExtensions.cs:665 (the implicit-constructor predicate IsImplicitlyDeclared: true, IsPrimary: false, Parameters: [])
findings.what_happens_today: The synthesized constructors have no declaring syntax (plausible, from SynthesizedInstanceConstructor), so IsPrimary is false, GetBaseConstructor takes the `null => null` arm and resolves the implicit base constructor, and PrimarySyntaxTree falls back to the containing type. They have one parameter, so the predicate at DeclarationExtensions.cs:665 does not classify them as implicit constructors; advice that replaces the implicit constructor (IntroduceConstructorAdvice.cs:96) treats them as explicit ones, which matches their public signature. The Value property is declared with the union declaration as its syntax. GetPropertyKind finds a backing field and a non-empty DeclaringSyntaxReferences, then calls HasExplicitAccessorBody, which reads the syntax; whether it copes with a UnionDeclarationSyntax was not read. SourceProperty.cs:115 casts the syntax with `as PropertyDeclarationSyntax` and survives. Linking/SymbolExtensions.GetDeclarationFlags switches on the kind of the primary declaration and throws AssertionFailedException at :62 for a kind outside its list, so the first linker analysis of Value (an aspect that overrides it or references it) crashes, in the same way that LinkerRecordHelper.cs:45,65 had to special-case RecordDeclaration for the synthesized record members.
findings.consequence_class: Assertion or crash for an aspect that touches Value; no impact for the constructors.
findings.proposed_change: Treat Value like the synthesized record members: add UnionDeclaration to the kind list of GetDeclarationFlags, extend LinkerRecordHelper (theme 04), and add a code-model unit test that reads Constructors, Properties, IsAutoPropertyOrField and IsImplicitlyDeclared of a union.
findings.confidence: Plausible (depends on the syntax reference that SourcePropertySymbolBase reports for the synthesized property).
open_questions: The behaviour of HasExplicitAccessorBody on a UnionDeclarationSyntax.
Whether meta.Proceed() in an override of Value must be rejected as it is for synthesized record members (LinkerRecordHelper.cs:236).

findings.title: A run-time union in a file that also contains compile-time code breaks the compile-time compilation
findings.what_happens_today: FindCompileTimeCodeVisitor decides whether a syntax tree is fed to the compile-time rewriter; it never visits a union, which is correct because a union is run-time code. When the same file also declares an aspect, the tree is rewritten by ProduceCompileTimeCodeRewriter, whose VisitClassDeclaration, VisitStructDeclaration, VisitInterfaceDeclaration and VisitRecordDeclaration overrides return null for run-time types. A top-level union is not intercepted, so the base rewriter copies it into the compile-time compilation, which is compiled as C# 14 (FACTS.md, SupportedCSharpVersions), and the compile-time build fails with a "feature not available in C# 14" error on a declaration the user never wrote for compile-time. A union nested in a run-time type reaches PopulateNestedCompileTimeTypes at :356-370, whose default arm drops it, which is correct by accident.
findings.consequence_class: Build or restore error, with a misleading message.
findings.proposed_change: Override VisitUnionDeclaration in ProduceCompileTimeCodeRewriter and route it to VisitTypeDeclaration; add a compile-time unit test with a run-time union and an aspect in one file. This belongs to theme 02; it is recorded here because the crash originates in the missing visitor override of CM-7.

findings.title: Every engine reference to the new Roslyn members needs a variant strategy
where: eng/RoslynVersions/Roslyn.5.0.0.props:8-10 ("This variant defines no constant. No production source branches on the variant.")
findings.what_happens_today: Metalama.Framework.Engine is compiled once per Roslyn variant, and Roslyn 5.0 has neither UnionDeclarationSyntax, SyntaxKind.UnionDeclaration, SyntaxKind.ClosedKeyword, ITypeSymbol.IsUnion, UnionCaseTypes nor IsClosed. Any of CM-1 to CM-9 that names them fails to compile in the Roslyn.5.0.0 variant. The Roslyn.5.0.0 variant serves Rider and the C# Dev Kit (FACTS.md), whose compiler cannot produce a union or a closed class, so the members are needed only in the Roslyn.5.10.0 variant.
findings.consequence_class: Build or restore error of the engine itself, for every implementation of the findings above.
findings.proposed_change: Decide once, for all themes, between three mechanisms: `#if ROSLYN_5_10_0_OR_GREATER` blocks (which requires lifting the policy stated in the two .props files), numeric kind values ((SyntaxKind) 9082 for UnionDeclaration, 8452 for UnionKeyword, 8453 for ClosedKeyword, from FACTS.md) with a RoslynApiVersion guard, or a small IRoslynFeatureShim service registered per variant that answers IsUnion, UnionCaseTypes and IsClosed through reflection. The IsUnion, IsClosed and UnionCaseTypes reads fit the shim; the syntax factory call of CM-3 and the visitor overrides of CM-7 fit `#if`, because a numeric kind cannot override a virtual method.
findings.size: A decision, then S per site.
open_questions: The outcome of the policy decision.
Whether the public Metalama.Framework.Sdk surface (SyntaxKindExtensions is [PublicAPI]) may mention the new kinds.

non_findings: Identity: a union type receives the documentation id T:Ns.Pet through DocumentationCommentId (SerializableDeclarationIdProvider.FromSymbol.cs:97-105 goes to the default arm at :113-155; DocumentationIdHelper.GeneratorOfDeclarationIdFromDeclaration.cs:59-63), its synthesized constructors and Value property receive M: and P: ids like any member, and a case type is an ordinary type with its own id. SerializableTypeId writes the type in C# syntax (SerializableTypeIdGenerator.cs:93-112 and :174-197, which handle Struct), and SymbolId.cs:44-60 wraps Roslyn's SymbolKey, which handles every symbol. DurableRef, DeclarationIdRef and TypeIdRef build on these ids (Metalama.Framework.Engine/CodeModel/References/). No round-trip is affected.

Serialization: there is no JsonSerializationBinder in the repository. The compile-time serialization binders are CompileTimeSerializationBinder.cs and BaseCompileTimeSerializationBinder.cs in Metalama.Framework.Engine/CompileTime/Serialization/; they bind assembly-qualified names of compile-time types. The IType serializers TypeIdRefSerializer.cs, SerializableTypeIdSerializer.cs, DurableRefSerializer.cs and SerializableDeclarationIdSerializer.cs serialize the ids above. SerializationIntrinsicTypeExtensions.cs:166,213,249 switch on the Roslyn TypeKind for enums, type parameters and arrays only. Unaffected.
Metalama.Framework.Introspection and Metalama.Framework.Engine/Introspection/ do not read TypeKind, IsRecord or IsSealed. Unaffected.
Metalama.Framework.Workspaces, Metalama.Framework.DesignTime and Metalama.LinqPad do not switch on TypeKind. Unaffected.

DeclarationFactory: GetIType (DeclarationFactory.Symbols.cs:117-131) dispatches on SymbolKind and reaches GetNamedType for a union; GetNamedType (:160-185) treats the union as any named type. RefFactory, SymbolRef, SymbolNormalizer and RefTargetKind (Metalama.Framework.Engine/CodeModel/References/) are keyed by SymbolKind and RefTargetKind, neither of which gains a value. Unaffected.

DeclarationEqualityComparer and StructuralDeclarationComparer: equality of two references to the same union, or to the same closed class, is structural on name, arity and containing declaration and does not read TypeKind beyond the Struct arm. The symbol-free conversion classifier at DeclarationEqualityComparer.Conversions.cs:80-140 does not know the union conversion from a case type to the union, but it is used only when symbols are bypassed (DeclarationEqualityComparer.cs:106-112), that is, for introduced types, which cannot be unions.
DerivedTypeIndex.Builder.AnalyzeType (DerivedTypeIndex.Builder.cs:58-96) indexes the implicit IUnion interface of a union as any interface. A closed class is indexed like any base class. Unaffected.
GenericContext and TypeSymbolRewriter: a generic union Pet<T>(Cat<T>, Dog) is a generic struct for both (GenericContext.*, TypeSymbolRewriter.cs:39-51). Unaffected.

ModifierHelper.GetTypeSyntaxModifierList (ModifierHelper.cs:198-236) is used only by IntroduceNamedTypeTransformation (rg GetSyntaxModifierList( on 2026-09-03), so a source closed class or union never has its modifiers regenerated by the code model; the linker (LinkerInjectionStep.Rewriter.VisitTypeDeclaration, :359-455) keeps the original modifier list, including closed.

SyntaxGeneratorForIType.TypeSyntaxGeneratorVisitor (SyntaxGeneratorForIType.TypeSyntaxGeneratorVisitor.cs:83-112) generates a type reference to a union from its name and type arguments, like any named type. Unaffected.

TypeKindConstraint (Metalama.Framework/Code/TypeKindConstraint.cs) and its switches (GenericParameterExtensions.cs:18-68, ContextualSyntaxGenerator.cs:291-323) are unaffected: a union satisfies the struct constraint and neither proposal adds a constraint kind.

IsRecordCopyConstructor (Metalama.Framework/Code/DeclarationExtensions.cs:323-331) requires IsRecord, false for a union, so the record-specific constructor logic (PullConstructorParameterAdviceImpl.cs:248, OnConstructedEpilogueEmitter.cs:72, ConstructorInitializeAdvice.cs:72) does not misfire on the synthesized union constructors.
Closed enums are not in C# 15 (FACTS.md, MessageID.RequiredVersion), so TypeKind.Enum handling is unaffected.

A closed or union declaration inside compile-time code (an aspect class declared closed) fails in the compile-time compilation because that compilation is C# 14; this is the language-version theme (01), not a code-model defect.

findings.title: The injection rewriter does not visit union declarations; injected members targeting a union are never inserted and the registry asserts
findings.what_happens_today: Every advice kind that produces an InjectedMember (override, introduction, contract with auxiliary member, initializer method, interface member implementation) on a union or on a member of a union ends with AssertionFailedException from LinkerInjectionRegistry.cs:326. IntroduceAttribute on the union type and ImplementInterface with no member to introduce do not produce an InjectedMember; their effect is silently lost because RewriteDeclarationAttributeLists (line 70-137) and GetIntroducedInterfacesForTypeDeclaration are only reached from VisitTypeDeclaration. Members of a union are still visited by Roslyn's default visit, so VisitParameter (line 1606) and VisitAccessorDeclaration (line 1760) run, but VisitMethodDeclarationCore (line 1553), VisitConstructorDeclarationCore (line 1482), VisitPropertyDeclarationCore (line 1652) and VisitIndexerDeclarationCore (line 1712) do not, so contracts and initializer statements targeting union members are also never injected. Supporting detail from the Where item: LinkerInjectionStep.Rewriter.cs:316-324 overrides VisitClassDeclaration, VisitStructDeclaration, VisitInterfaceDeclaration, VisitRecordDeclaration and VisitExtensionBlockDeclaration, each delegating to VisitTypeDeclaration<T> (line 359); there is no VisitUnionDeclaration and no override of VisitCore/DefaultVisit that would catch other TypeDeclarationSyntax kinds. VisitTypeDeclaration<T> (lines 359-455) is the only place that consumes InsertPosition( After, member ) (line 398-402) and InsertPosition( Within, node ) for type nodes (line 405-409), applies primary-constructor member-level transformations (line 370-374), injects introduced interfaces (GetIntroducedInterfacesForTypeDeclaration, line 364, backed by LinkerInjectionStep.TransformationCollection.cs:334-344), and rewrites the type's attribute lists (line 451-452). findings.title: Inlining copies user labels verbatim; labeled loops make label collisions between template and target realistic
findings.what_happens_today: A label can only be useful with `goto`, which templates cannot use, so a template body and a target body never carried the same label. With C# 15, `outer: foreach (...) { ... break outer; }` becomes an ordinary idiom, and a template that contains such a loop and is inlined into a target method that also declares `outer` yields two `outer:` labels in one block after flattening (CS0140), or a label shadowing a label of a contained scope when the blocks are not flattened (CS0158). The same happens when one template with a labeled loop is applied to a method that is later inlined into another override of the same template (two copies of the same template are never inlined into one method because a semantic is inlined only when referenced once, linker-inlining.md, "Why exactly once"), so the practical case is template versus target. Supporting detail from the Where item: Linking/Substitution/InliningSubstitution.cs:34-73 inlines the substituted body as a FlattenableBlock; Linking/LinkerLinkingStep.CleanupBodyRewriter.cs:93-108, 194-205 flattens those blocks into the enclosing statement list; Linking/LexicalScopeFactory.Visitor.cs:86-91 collects user label identifiers so that the linker's own labels (__aspect_return_N, epilogue, postBase) are unique, but no substitution renames user labels (grep of LabeledStatement under Linking/ finds only CleanupBodyRewriter, SemanticBodyAnalyzer, RemoveTrivialLabelRewriter, LexicalScopeFactory.Visitor and BlockWithReturnBeforeUsingLocalSubstitution); templates may contain labeled statements (Templating/TemplateAnnotator.cs has no VisitLabeledStatement override; only `goto` is rejected at lines 2601-2606).
findings.consequence_class: Build or restore error (in the transformed compilation).
findings.proposed_change: Add a label-renaming substitution applied to inlined bodies: collect LabeledStatementSyntax identifiers of the inlined body, allocate unique names through LexicalScopeFactory.GetLexicalScope( destination ).GetUniqueIdentifier, and rewrite LabeledStatementSyntax.Identifier, GotoStatementSyntax.Expression, and the Name of BreakStatementSyntax and ContinueStatementSyntax. The last two members do not exist in Roslyn 5.0.0, so the rewrite must go through Update-free code: rebuild the statement with SyntaxFactory.BreakStatement( attributeLists, breakKeyword, name, semicolon ) only in the 5.10 variant, or rewrite the IdentifierNameSyntax child generically by visiting IdentifierName nodes whose parent kind is BreakStatement/ContinueStatement (a CSharpSyntaxRewriter override of VisitIdentifierName needs no new API). Add linker tests Methods/Overrides/Labels/* with a labeled loop in both the override and the target.
findings.confidence: Plausible (the collision mechanism is verified from the code; the C# diagnostics are from the language rules on label scope).
open_questions: Whether the template compiler preserves BreakStatementSyntax.Name when it re-emits template statements (template analyst; FACTS.md notes the generator strips the experimental field).
