non_findings: Labeled `break` and `continue` in the linker rewriters: no linker rewriter reconstructs an existing BreakStatementSyntax or ContinueStatementSyntax. The only construction sites are Linking/Substitution/ReturnStatementSubstitution.cs:79-110, 150-160, which create a fresh unlabeled `break;` to replace a `return;` located directly in a switch section (decided by LinkerAnalysisStep.SemanticBodyAnalyzer.cs:163-168), and an unlabeled `break` still targets the innermost `switch` under C# 15. LinkerLinkingStep.CountLabelUsesWalker.cs:24-31 counts `goto` uses only and RemoveTrivialLabelRewriter.cs:49-60 removes `goto L; L:` pairs; a `break L;` is not counted, but the removed pair can only be linker-generated (__aspect_return_N), which user code does not reference. CleanupBodyRewriter.cs:135-152 may attach a linker label to a following user loop (`__aspect_return_1: for (...)`), which is legal and does not change the resolution of user labels. ConstructorEpilogueRewriter.cs:45-63 rewrites `return;` only. BlockWithReturnBeforeUsingLocalSubstitution.cs:26-90 reasons about outgoing `goto` statements only; a labeled break can only target an enclosing statement, so it cannot jump forward past a `using` declaration. All linker rewriters derive from SafeSyntaxRewriter (Metalama.Framework.Sdk/Utilities/Roslyn/SafeSyntaxRewriter.cs), whose VisitCore calls the Roslyn base Visit, so the Name child of a break or continue statement is carried by Roslyn's own generated VisitBreakStatement/VisitContinueStatement.

SemanticBodyAnalyzer.DiscoverExitFlowingStatements (LinkerAnalysisStep.SemanticBodyAnalyzer.cs:330-336) already descends into LabeledStatementSyntax.Statement, so a labeled loop that ends a method is analyzed like an unlabeled one.

Collection expression arguments: Formatting/CodeFormatter.CustomSimplifier.cs:29-40 (DefaultVisit passes unknown nodes through), SyntaxGeneration/ContextualSyntaxGenerator.cs:1052 (CollectionExpression needs no parentheses under a cast, also true with a leading `with(...)` element), SyntaxGeneration/ContextualSyntaxGenerator.RemoveReferenceNullableAnnotationsRewriter.cs:77-88 (the WithElements there is TupleTypeSyntax.WithElements, unrelated), Templating/TemplateAnnotator.cs:3495-3502 (visits each element through Visit, so a WithElementSyntax is visited by the Roslyn default and its ArgumentList child is annotated). No throwing default over CollectionElementSyntax kinds exists in the engine (grep for SpreadElement, ExpressionElement, WithElement in Metalama.Framework.Engine finds none).

CodeFormatter pipeline (Formatting/CodeFormatter.cs:86-207): custom simplification, ImportAdder, Simplifier.ReduceAsync, SimplifierFixer (token-level) and Formatter.FormatAsync are all Roslyn-driven or node-kind-agnostic; FormattingAnnotations.cs is annotation plumbing only. The only throwing kind switch in SyntaxGeneration/ContextualSyntaxGenerator.cs:786-815 (AddAttribute( SyntaxNode, IAttributeData ), which lacks RecordDeclaration, ExtensionBlockDeclaration and UnionDeclaration) has no caller in Metalama.Framework, Metalama.Patterns, Metalama.Extensions or Metalama.Migration (grep for SyntaxGenerator.AddAttribute); it is a [PublicAPI] helper for weavers.

`closed` classes in the linker and advice: the rewriters preserve the modifier list of the original declaration (LinkerInjectionStep.Rewriter.cs:359-455, LinkerRewritingDriver.Types.cs:18-45). IntroduceMemberAdvice.ValidateBuilder (IntroduceMemberAdvice.cs:206-214) uses IsAbstract, which a closed class reports as true through the symbol (the proposal makes closed classes implicitly abstract), so abstract members may be introduced. OnConstructedMethodAdvice and OnConstructedEpilogueEmitter (OnConstructedMethodAdvice.cs:164-165, 221; OnConstructedEpilogueEmitter.cs:69) key the guard on IsSealed and TypeKind.Struct, both unaffected. InitializeMethodAdvice.cs:80, 116, 163 likewise. AspectReferenceResolver.cs:591-606 special-cases interface members only.

Extension indexers and the aspect-reference resolver: the resolver has no indexer-specific or extension-specific branch (grep -i extension Linking/AspectReferenceResolver.cs finds only the TypeKind alias); element accesses are handled by Linking/Substitution/AspectReferenceRenamingSubstitution.cs:102, 155 and AspectReferenceBaseSubstitution.cs:94, which rewrite the annotated ElementAccessExpressionSyntax regardless of its receiver. The property inliners match on the ReturnStatement/assignment shape around the annotated root (Linking/Inlining/PropertyGetReturnInliner.cs:16-58, PropertyInliner.cs:11-15), not on the receiver.

Extension blocks in the injection step: LinkerInjectionStep.Rewriter.cs:622-637 injects members into introduced extension blocks and LinkerInjectionStep.cs:251-263, 837-880 distributes receiver-contract statements per member including extensionBlock.Indexers (line 1156-1159).

Static members in interfaces: IntroduceMemberAdvice.ValidateBuilder (IntroduceMemberAdvice.cs:174-186) rejects only static virtual members outside interfaces and static sealed members; ModifierHelper.GetMemberSyntaxModifierList (ModifierHelper.cs:100-102, 122-140) emits `static` for interface members and `abstract`/`virtual` only when the member declares them. No engine code checks runtime support for default interface members (grep for DefaultInterface, RuntimeFeature, DIM in Metalama.Framework.Engine finds nothing). The feature therefore changes nothing in these themes; whether the introduced-member eligibility for net472 targets needs relaxing is a code-model or platform question.

Records as union candidates: the record-specific code in LinkerInjectionStep.Rewriter.cs:376-387 (compensating Deconstruct), LinkerInjectionStep.cs:1005-1053 (primary constructor materialization), LinkerRewritingDriver.Types.cs:64-155 (positional properties), LinkerRecordHelper.cs, and the copy-constructor exclusions (ConstructorInitializeAdvice.cs:72, OnConstructedEpilogueEmitter.cs:72, PullConstructorParameterAdviceImpl.cs:248, EligibilityRuleFactory.cs:54, 157, 188) all key on IsRecord (SourceNamedTypeImpl.cs:173, from INamedTypeSymbol.IsRecord) or on RecordDeclarationSyntax. A union is not a record and has no positional properties, primary constructor or copy constructor, so none of these sites should be extended to unions; the union-specific constraints are covered by LK-8.

Introduction builders: IndexerBuilder (CodeModel/Introductions/Builders/IndexerBuilder.cs:28-38) accepts any INamedType including ExtensionBlockBuilder/ExtensionBlockImpl, so LK-6 needs no builder change; ExtensionBlockBuilder.cs:34 already models the static-extension case needed for the LK-6 rule.

Tests pinning current behaviour that a union or closed change must keep green: 82 record aspect tests (find Tests -iname '*Record*'), Tests/Aspects/Initialization/BeforeInstanceConstructor_Record_*, Tests/Fabrics/Target_Record*, Tests/Aspects/CSharp14/ExtensionMembers/* (19 inputs), Tests/Aspects/Overrides/Indexers/* (13 inputs, including NotInlineable which pins LAMA0699), linker tests Tests/Methods/Overrides/TargetBody/Switch*_EndFlow (pin the `return` to `break` rewrite inside switch sections). No existing test contains `union` or `closed` as a keyword (grep -w union|closed under tests matches only identifiers named Generic_Closed*).

angle: Group by subsystem and file ownership. Each story is scoped so that it touches one area of the code base, so that one reviewer who owns that area can review the whole pull request without reading the other stories. The primary key is the directory that the change edits, not the language feature that motivates it: for example every edit to the shared syntax-kind predicates of Metalama.Framework.Engine/Utilities/Roslyn goes into one story whoever reported it (the code model, the linker, the templating and the design-time analysts all reported the same lines), and the design-time partial-declaration generator is one story even though three themes described it. Where a language feature spans several areas (unions span the shared predicates, the visitors, the compile-time rewriter, the code model, the linker and the design time generator), it becomes a chain of one-area stories linked by blocked_by rather than one large feature story. The consequence of this angle is that the build files (eng/src/Program.cs, the package build props and targets, Directory.Packages.props), the documentation and the Metalama.Premium repository each collect their own stories rather than being split across feature stories, and that a few findings sit in a story whose motivating theme is not their reporting theme.

clusters.title: The shared syntax-kind predicates and kind lists omit UnionDeclaration
clusters.rationale: Five findings from four themes describe the same three files. SyntaxKindExtensions.cs:33 (IsTypeDeclaration) and :41 (IsBaseTypeDeclaration) enumerate class, struct, interface, record and record struct; SyntaxExtensions.cs:33, :61 and :116 repeat a longer enumeration in FindMemberDeclarationOrNull, FindSymbolDeclaringNode and GetDeclaringType. CM-2 reaches them through INamedType.IsPartial (SourceNamedTypeImpl.cs:329-352), DT-1 through the wrong LAMA0048 on a partial union and the missing generated file, DT-6 through the suppression path, CM-6 and LK-3 through the linker and design-time consumers. Widening the predicates once fixes all five, and widening them twice would produce conflicting edits to the same lines. The cluster also owns the decision, raised in CM-6 and LK-3, between a narrow predicate (a type declaration that can contain members) and the broad SyntaxFacts.IsTypeDeclaration, which also matches delegates, enums and extension blocks.

clusters.title: The design-time generated partial part of a union is emitted as partial struct
clusters.rationale: Three themes describe one method, DesignTimeSyntaxTreeGenerator.CreatePartialType (DesignTimeSyntaxTreeGenerator.cs:697-790), and reach the same conclusion: the arm that produces a struct declaration for TypeKind.Struct produces CS0261 for a union, and the generated part must omit the case list because only one partial part may carry a parameter list. LK-4 adds the finding that the closed modifier needs no change, because Roslyn merges partial modifiers. One factory call, one arm, one test file.

clusters.title: The hand-written syntax visitors and the design-time classifier have no union branch
clusters.rationale: CM-7 inventories the visitors that derive from the Roslyn base classes and therefore silently skip a union declaration, and LK-10 reports the same defect in Formatting/TextSpanClassifier.cs:113-119, whose VisitClassDeclaration, VisitStructDeclaration and VisitRecordDeclaration route to a shared helper that a union never reaches. LK-10 additionally shows that the classifier cannot be fixed alone, because TemplateAnnotator has no union dispatch either and its default path would classify a run-time union as compile-time. The two are one edit set over the same shape of code.

clusters.title: The compile-time code rewriter drops or copies a union verbatim
clusters.rationale: CM-9 and TP-6 describe the same two visitors of CompileTimeCompilationBuilder: FindCompileTimeCodeVisitor, which classifies the declarations of a syntax tree, and ProduceCompileTimeCodeRewriter, whose four type-declaration overrides route to a private VisitTypeDeclaration. A union nested in a compile-time class is copied verbatim and a union in a run-time class is dropped. One override, or one type test that replaces the four overrides, closes both.

clusters.title: Every C# language-version table stops at C# 14
clusters.rationale: Four themes converge on SupportedCSharpVersions.cs (Latest at :31, ToLanguageVersion at :52, DefaultParseOptions at :50, GetMaxLanguageVersion at :149), on AllLanguageVersions.cs, on LanguageVersionProvider.cs and on LanguageVersionExtensions.ToDisplayStringSafe. LV-2 reports the throwing display mapping, LV-3 the tables and the variant-awareness of Latest, TP-2 the same mapping seen from the template verifier, TP-8 the raise of the constants themselves, DT-4 the deliberate non-change at design time, LV-7 the comment that distinguishes the repository ceiling from the product ceiling, and LV-6 the verification that the operator table needs nothing. They are one edit to one small set of files and they cannot be split without leaving the tables inconsistent between two pull requests.

clusters.title: The compile-time project manifest language version
clusters.rationale: LV-4 reports that CompileTimeProjectManifest.ResolvedLanguageVersion is dead code that disagrees with the two live fallbacks at CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.cs:1355 and CompileTimeProjectRepository.Builder.cs:596, and LV-5 reports that the manifest value must be clamped when a library compiled at a higher language version is read by a lower Roslyn variant. Both concern the same property and the same two reading sites, and the clamp of LV-5 is meaningless unless the fallback of LV-4 is settled at the same time.

clusters.title: The test harness cannot request C# 15 and skips silently instead
clusters.rationale: Three themes describe TestOptions.cs:681-721, where an unrecognised @LanguageVersion value marks the test skipped with a reason and nothing fails. LV-8 records the behaviour as adequate today, DT-7 records that it silently hides a whole C# 15 suite, and UT-19 defines the directory and constant conventions that a C# 15 suite would follow. One change to the harness plus one convention document.

clusters.title: Renumbering the latest Roslyn variant from the 5.10 prerelease to the stable 5.12
clusters.rationale: LV-12 decides the target version and the version strings, LV-13 enumerates the eight edit sites and the two silent failure modes of a mismatch, DT-8 shows that the prerelease pin is a restore failure for every external consumer of Metalama.Framework.Workspaces, Metalama.Testing.AspectTesting and Metalama.LinqPad and therefore a release gate, and PR-1 is the same edit set in Metalama.Premium. It is one work item, but it cannot be one pull request, because it spans two repositories; the two stories are linked by blocked_by.

clusters.title: Regenerating the syntax rewriters, verifiers and hashers from the stable grammar
clusters.rationale: All three findings are the same operation on eng/src/GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter: add the grammar of the consumed Roslyn, whose experimental markers on the union, with-element and labeled break and continue nodes have been removed, and regenerate. TP-1 owns the grammar file and the guard against forgetting it, TP-9 owns the design-time hashers that the same run produces, and DT-3 owns the design-time diff that consumes them. The generated output is one file set produced by one command.

clusters.title: No project builds or tests against net11.0 or under the .NET 11 SDK
clusters.rationale: Five findings describe one coverage gap from five angles: the test projects have no net11.0 leg, the tested-target-framework standalone scenario deliberately omits net11.0 and net11.0-windows, the other standalone scenarios run on net10.0 only, the test infrastructure package pins were derived for a different baseline, and Metalama.Premium has the same gap. They share one prerequisite, the .NET 11 SDK in the build container, and they share the risk that the snapshots of the aspect tests diverge between the two legs.

clusters.title: The build container and the build host baseline
clusters.rationale: One file in each repository, eng/src/Program.cs, and the docker definitions generated from it. The core file today pins dotNetSdkVersion to 10.0.400, VisualStudioBuildToolsComponentVersion.v18_9_2 and MSBuildVersion 18.9 (eng/src/Program.cs:26, :40-41, :63). UT-1 and LV-9 ask for a second .NET SDK, LV-11 for the November 2026 Visual Studio component, and PR-3 and PR-4 are the same file in Metalama.Premium, where the equivalent change is already merged apart from two obsolete components. Splitting them would mean regenerating the container images more than once, which the record of issue #1902 says is expensive.

clusters.title: Extension indexers across advice, eligibility and contracts
clusters.rationale: LK-6 lifts the deliberate rejection of indexers in extension blocks at AdviceFactory.cs:1406 and adds the eligibility rules that the language requires instead, LK-7 covers the overriding half of the same feature and the non-inlined trampoline, and UT-16 is the contract advice and the not-null fabric over the same member shape. One advice surface, one test directory.

clusters.title: Closed classes in the code model and in type introduction
clusters.rationale: CM-4 and LK-5 propose the same member, INamedTypeBuilder.IsClosed with the emission of the closed modifier in ModifierHelper.GetTypeSyntaxModifierList; CM-5 is the read-only INamedType.IsClosed that the same pull request must add for symmetry; UT-15 confirms that the pattern libraries need no product change and asks only for observation tests. Two properties, one modifier emission and a few tests.

clusters.title: Unions in the public code model and their compiler-synthesized members
clusters.rationale: CM-1 adds the distinguishing members to INamedType and CM-8 makes the synthesized Value property and the per-case constructors readable by the model and reachable by the linker helpers. Both edit CodeModel/Source/SourceNamedTypeImpl.cs and the kind lists of Linking/SymbolExtensions.cs, and both depend on the same Roslyn API that only the latest variant exposes.

clusters.title: Labeled break and continue in templates and in inlining
clusters.rationale: TP-3 models the label in TemplateAnnotator and reports a diagnostic when a run-time break targets a compile-time loop; LK-9 renames labels when a body is inlined, which is the failure that the same feature makes realistic. Both must handle BreakStatementSyntax.Name and ContinueStatementSyntax.Name, a member that only the regenerated latest variant exposes, so writing them apart would duplicate the variant-gating work.

clusters.title: Metalama.Premium package pin hygiene
clusters.rationale: Both findings edit /home/user/metalama.premium/Directory.Packages.props: PR-6 the residual Microsoft.Build pins, the dead property and the stale rationale comments, PR-7 the contradictory StackExchange.Redis pair that makes the intended version update inert. One file, one reviewer.

clusters.title: The Roslyn 5.0 variant of Metalama.Premium is built but never executed
clusters.rationale: PR-2 is the missing variant test projects and the variant-awareness of the existing test project references; PR-13 is the comment in those same test projects that still describes a variant constant that no longer exists. The comment is corrected by the change that removes its cause.

clusters.title: Documentation that names members, versions and target frameworks that no longer exist
clusters.rationale: All four edit Markdown under Metalama.Framework/docs and Directory.Packages.md in the Metalama repository, even though two of them were reported by the Metalama.Premium analyst: PR-9 asks for a Premium entry in the drift-point list of platform-support.md and PR-14 for a Premium section beside the existing one about Metalama.Compiler. LV-14 corrects the Roslyn variant procedure and the renamed members, UT-18 the target framework and language version statements. One documentation pull request avoids four conflicting edits to platform-support.md.

stories.title: Raise the build container to the November 2026 platform baseline: a second .NET SDK and the Visual Studio build tools
stories.rationale: One file, eng/src/Program.cs, plus the docker definitions generated from it by Build.ps1 generate-scripts. Today it declares a single DotNetComponent at dotNetSdkVersion 10.0.400 (eng/src/Program.cs:26, :37), VisualStudioBuildToolsComponentVersion.v18_9_2 (:40) and MSBuildVersion 18.9 (:63). The story adds a .NET 11 SDK component, decides what global.json pins, and raises the Visual Studio component and MSBuildVersion when PostSharp.Engineering exposes the November 2026 build tools. It is the prerequisite of every net11.0 test leg, so it is scheduled first even though it ships no product change. The comment already in the file at eng/src/Program.cs:19-25 records the MSB4062 conflict that two feature bands caused, and CLAUDE.md records that MSBuildExtensionsPath is the missing entry of the mitigation in PostSharp.Engineering, which is an external prerequisite of this story and not deliverable in this repository. The one-line correction of MaximumSdkVersion that LV-9 also proposes is deliberately not in this story: it lives in Metalama.Framework.Package/build/Metalama.Framework.props, a different area with a different owner, and is delivered by S02.

stories.title: Compare the .NET SDK against the supported ceiling on major and minor only
stories.rationale: MaximumSdkVersion is 11.0 at Metalama.Framework.Package/build/Metalama.Framework.props:33 and the comparison at Metalama.Framework.targets:410-413 uses the full NETCoreSdkVersion, so every .NET 11 SDK, including 11.0.100, reports LAMA0601 although the same file declares .NET 11 supported at :39. The fix introduces a second property holding the first two components and uses it in the maximum rule only, so that MinimumSdkVersion keeps feature-band precision, which this repository itself relies on by pinning 10.0.400. A standalone scenario at the boundary is added in the same pull request. The area is the package build files, owned by whoever owns the supported-platform check introduced by issue #1884.

stories.title: Correct the LangVersion clamp and its warning in Metalama.Framework.targets
stories.rationale: Metalama.Framework.targets:115-121 rewrites an SDK-implied LangVersion that is not one of 12.0, 13.0, 14.0 or a symbolic value down to 12.0, and the warning at :243 explains it wrongly. When the compiler toolset raises the implied version for net11.0, the project silently loses C# 13, C# 14 and C# 15 at once. The story adds the Code attribute to the Warning task, corrects the message and the suppression advice (MSBuildWarningsAsMessages, not NoWarn), allocates a code in the LAMA06xx platform range beside LAMA0600 to LAMA0602, and adds a net11.0 standalone scenario beside Standalone/DefaultLanguageVersion/DotNet, correcting the stale comment there that still names .NET 8 and C# 12. The scenario needs the .NET 11 SDK, hence the dependency on S01. This story owns Metalama.Framework.targets:115-121 for the release; the extension of the accepted-value list with 15.0 is left to S06, which lands after it.

stories.title: Renumber the latest Roslyn variant from the 5.10 prerelease to the stable 5.12
stories.rationale: A mechanical renaming across build files and a few engine constants: Directory.Packages.props (RoslynApiMaxVersion, RoslynMaxVersion), eng/RoslynVersions/Roslyn.5.10.0.props and its DefineConstants, eng/src/GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter version list, SupportedCSharpVersions.ToNuGetVersionString at SupportedCSharpVersions.cs:77 (which also turns the roslyn-consolidated source off when the label loses its hyphen), RoslynVariantPolicy and its tests, and the variant project names. The story carries the two silent failure modes that LV-13 names: TargetedAssemblyReference compares the declared Roslyn version by equality, and ExtensionLoaderBase drops a non-matching extension assembly with no diagnostic. It also carries the release gate that DT-8 identifies, namely that Metalama.Framework.Workspaces, Metalama.Testing.AspectTesting and Metalama.LinqPad must not ship a dependency on a package that nuget.org does not serve, which already reached a user in issue #1106. Metalama.Compiler is listed because the rebase of that repository onto Roslyn 5.12 is the prerequisite named by updating-roslyn.md step 1 and is a separate pull request there; it was not verifiable in this session because that repository is not cloned.

stories.title: Add the Roslyn 5.12 grammar and regenerate the syntax rewriters, verifiers and hashers
stories.rationale: One directory, eng/src/GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter. TreeReader.RemoveExperimentalDeclarations strips every node and field carrying ExperimentalUrl, which is why no generated visitor, verifier or hasher knows the union declaration, the with-element or the Name field of break and continue. Adding Syntax-5.12.0.xml, whose markers are removed for those three, and regenerating produces the visitors, the version verifier arms and the design-time hashers in one run. The story also adds the guard that TP-1 asks for, comparing the local grammar file with the grammar of the exact consumed Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.CSharp package rather than keying on the prerelease label, because the unsafe expression keeps its marker and a label-based check would fail permanently. Two hasher test cases from TP-9 and the design-time diff cases from DT-3 land in the same pull request, since they assert exactly what the regeneration produces.

stories.title: Add C# 15 to the engine language-version tables and make the latest version variant-aware
stories.rationale: A small set of files under Metalama.Framework.Engine/Utilities and one pipeline check: AllLanguageVersions.cs gains CSharp15 as the numeric cast 1500, SupportedCSharpVersions.Latest at :31 becomes variant-aware rather than a shared constant, ToLanguageVersion at :52 maps the renumbered latest variant to C# 15 while the 5.0.0 variant stays at C# 14, GetMaxLanguageVersion at :149 gains the arm for the version at which the compiler toolset actually raises the implied version, LanguageVersionExtensions.ToDisplayStringSafe stops throwing, LanguageVersionProvider maps the .NET 11 SDK, and CompileTimeAspectPipeline.VerifyLanguageVersion reports LAMA0052 instead of crashing. The story also carries the MSBuild constants that follow the same decision (the accepted-value list of Metalama.Framework.targets, LangMaxVersion and MetalamaTemplateLanguageVersion in Directory.Build.props, with the comment correction LV-7 asks for), the deliberate non-change at design time that DT-4 documents, and the verification of LV-6 that the operator table needs nothing for C# 15. Splitting these would leave the tables inconsistent between two pull requests, because Latest, All, the mapping and the display string are read by each other.

stories.title: Settle the language version of the compile-time project manifest and clamp it when reading
stories.rationale: CompileTimeProjectManifest.ResolvedLanguageVersion is dead code that documents C# 13 while the two live fallbacks at CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.cs:1355 and CompileTimeProjectRepository.Builder.cs:596 use the latest version. Either delete the property or route both fallbacks through it. In the same file set, clamp the manifest value to what the running Roslyn accepts when a library compiled at C# 15 is read by the 5.0.0 variant, and report a warning rather than letting Roslyn produce CS8192, which is exactly the failure recorded in issue #1185. The warning must not format the unknown value with ToDisplayStringSafe unless S06 has already added the arm, which is why this story follows it.

stories.title: Let the aspect test harness request C# 15, and fail visibly when a language version is unavailable
stories.rationale: One area, Metalama.Testing.AspectTesting and Metalama.Testing.UnitTesting. TestOptions.cs:681-721 parses @LanguageVersion and marks the test skipped when the value is not recognised by the running Roslyn, which is correct while a variant genuinely cannot serve the version and wrong when a whole suite silently disappears. The story makes the skip reason distinguish the two cases, gives the unit test context and the aspect test projects a way to request the new version, and writes down the conventions that a C# 15 suite follows: the directory Tests/Aspects/CSharp15 with a RequiredConstants gate in its metalamaTests.json naming the constant of the renumbered latest variant, and the ordering constraint that neither the directory nor the directive is meaningful before the variant moves.

stories.title: Decide and implement how engine source names the Roslyn members that only the latest variant has
stories.rationale: A decision with a small proof of concept, and the prerequisite of every union and closed-hierarchy story. Metalama.Framework.Engine.5.0.0 compiles the same source files against Roslyn 5.0, whose public API has neither UnionDeclarationSyntax nor ITypeSymbol.IsUnion, and issue #1881 removed all 177 conditional-compilation blocks from production source, leaving ROSLYN_5_10_0_OR_GREATER used only by two aspect tests. The three candidate mechanisms are conditional compilation, numeric syntax-kind values with a runtime guard, and a per-variant service that answers the few questions by reflection; issue #1215 already moved one reader away from reflection, which argues against the third. The outcome must also settle the RSEXPERIMENTAL006 suppression, which disappears when the latest variant reaches Roslyn 5.12, and the behaviour of the 5.0 variant when it meets a referenced union or closed type. Delivering the decision as a written note plus one worked example in the smallest consumer keeps the later stories mechanical.

stories.title: Make the shared syntax-kind predicates recognise a union declaration
stories.rationale: Three files in Metalama.Framework.Engine/Utilities/Roslyn and one property of the code model. SyntaxKindExtensions.cs:33 and :41 and the three enumerations of SyntaxExtensions.cs at :33, :61 and :116 are read by the code model (INamedType.IsPartial at SourceNamedTypeImpl.cs:329-352), by the linker, by the suppression path and by the design-time generator, so a union is not a type declaration anywhere until they are widened. The story must choose between the narrow predicate that the documentation of SyntaxKindExtensions promises, which is a type declaration that can contain members, and the broad Roslyn helper, which also matches delegates, enums and extension blocks and would change behaviour for extension blocks that already ship. It must also keep the convention that the KindCheckOptimizationAnalyzer of issue #1307 enforces. Two consumers named in LK-3 need care rather than widening, because the parameter list of a union is a case list and not a parameter list.

stories.title: Add union dispatch to the hand-written syntax visitors and to the design-time classifier
stories.rationale: The visitors that derive from the Roslyn base classes skip a union declaration silently, because the base dispatch has no override to call. The classifier at Formatting/TextSpanClassifier.cs:113-119 is the visible case: VisitClassDeclaration, VisitStructDeclaration and VisitRecordDeclaration route to a shared helper, so a compile-time union is not classified. LK-10 shows that the classifier cannot be corrected alone, because TemplateAnnotator has no union dispatch either and its default path would then mark a run-time union as compile-time, which would also change the existing behaviour for interfaces and extension blocks and require the Formatting baselines to be re-adopted. The story therefore covers the annotator and the classifier together with the remaining visitors of the inventory, and it is where the mechanism chosen in S09 is applied at scale.

stories.title: Handle a union declaration in the compile-time code rewriter
stories.rationale: Two visitors in Metalama.Framework.Engine/CompileTime: FindCompileTimeCodeVisitor, which decides whether a syntax tree contains compile-time code, and ProduceCompileTimeCodeRewriter, whose four type-declaration overrides route to a private VisitTypeDeclaration. A run-time union in a file that also contains an aspect breaks the compile-time compilation with a message that names a language version or a missing framework type, and a compile-time union is copied verbatim without a manifest entry. Either one override or a type test that replaces the four overrides closes both, and the story includes the aspect test that puts a run-time union and an aspect in one file, which is the case a user hits first.

stories.title: Expose unions in the public code model and make their synthesized members readable
stories.rationale: One area, Metalama.Framework.Engine/CodeModel plus the two helper files that read a member's declaring syntax. A union is currently an undistinguishable struct: the TypeKind mapping at SourceNamedTypeImpl.cs:69-79 reports Struct, IsRecord is false and nothing tells an aspect that instance fields are forbidden. The story adds IsUnion and the case types to INamedType, deliberately without a new TypeKind value, since TypeKind.RecordClass and TypeKind.RecordStruct are already obsolete for the same reason and a new value would require an arm in every switch, several of which throw. It also makes the synthesized Value property and the per-case constructors reachable, which extends the mechanism of the open pull request #1879 rather than duplicating it, so it should be rebased onto that branch. The public shape of IsUnion is a product decision, because ITypeSymbol.IsUnion is also true for a hand-written type carrying the union attribute.

stories.title: Emit a union declaration for the design-time partial part
stories.rationale: One method, DesignTimeSyntaxTreeGenerator.CreatePartialType at DesignTimeSyntaxTreeGenerator.cs:697-790, whose TypeKind.Struct arm produces partial struct and therefore CS0261 in the generated document for a union with introduced members. The part must omit the case list, because a second partial part carrying a parameter list is CS8863, and the discriminator must be the kind of the primary declaration syntax rather than the Roslyn union flag, which is also true for a hand-written attributed type whose generated part must stay a class or a struct. LK-4 records that the closed modifier needs no counterpart, because Roslyn merges the modifiers of partial parts. It follows S13 because it reads the code model member added there.

stories.title: Give the aspect linker a union branch in the injection and linking rewriters
stories.rationale: One directory, Metalama.Framework.Engine/Linking. LinkerInjectionStep.Rewriter.cs:316-322 has four overrides that route to VisitTypeDeclaration and LinkerLinkingStep.LinkingRewriter.cs:37-66 has four more, so a member injected into a union is never inserted and, once it is, never linked. The story replaces the per-kind dispatch by a version-neutral one over TypeDeclarationSyntax, which avoids naming a syntax type that the Roslyn 5.0 variant does not have, and it must keep the union case list intact: the fallback has to preserve ParameterList and must not run through the record and struct paths, whose removed-primary-constructor branch would delete it. Correct linking is necessary and not sufficient, which is why the eligibility guard is a separate story.

stories.title: Refuse advice that would produce code the union rules reject
stories.rationale: One area, Metalama.Framework/Eligibility and the validation helpers of AdviceFactory. A union forbids instance fields, auto-properties and field-like events, forbids a public single-parameter constructor, and requires every explicit constructor to chain to a generated one, so an aspect that introduces a backing field or an initializer emits code that the compiler rejects, with the diagnostic on generated code. For 2027.0 the recommended shape is one blanket diagnostic that covers the three compiler errors and the silent case where an initializer is injected into a constructor that has no syntax, rather than a rule per advice kind. The eligibility rules live in the public assembly, which does not reference Roslyn, so they must read the code model member added by S13 rather than the Roslyn flag. It should be scheduled as the first, defensive slice of union support and can ship even if S15 does not.

stories.title: Model closed classes in the code model and in type introduction
stories.rationale: One feature, two symmetrical members and one modifier emission, all in the code model and the introduction builders: a read-only INamedType.IsClosed, a settable INamedTypeBuilder.IsClosed with the validation that mirrors the compiler rules, and the emission of the closed token in ModifierHelper.GetTypeSyntaxModifierList instead of abstract, which the compiler implies. The story also documents that DirectOnly enumeration of derived types is exhaustive for a closed type declared in the current compilation, and carries the observation tests that UT-15 asks for in the pattern libraries, which need no product change. Union introduction is explicitly out of scope and remains a separate future story.

stories.title: Support labeled break and continue in templates and rename labels when inlining
stories.rationale: Two files that must agree about the same syntax member: TemplateAnnotator, which today has no VisitLabeledStatement and whose break and continue handling ignores the label, and the inlining substitution of the linker, which copies user labels verbatim into a destination that may already declare them. The annotator must record label to scope, report a diagnostic when a run-time break targets a compile-time loop, and preserve the label through the rewriter; the linker must allocate unique names through the existing lexical scope factory. Both read BreakStatementSyntax.Name and ContinueStatementSyntax.Name, which only the regenerated latest variant exposes, so doing them apart would duplicate the gating work.

stories.title: Template compiler support for the with element and a guard for experimental syntax
stories.rationale: Three findings about the same two files, TemplateAnnotator and the generated meta-syntax rewriter. The with element in a collection expression crashes the template compiler in run-time scope before regeneration and needs only tests afterwards; the unsafe expression keeps its experimental marker on the target Roslyn and therefore needs a name-free guard driven by the generator, so that it is rejected with the template diagnostic instead of reaching the compile-time compilation and producing a C# feature error there; the closed modifier and patterns over unions need nothing from the templating layer, which the story records as a negative scope statement together with the note that a closed compile-time class would need two polyfill attributes.

stories.title: Extension indexers: lift the introduction restriction, cover overriding and contracts
stories.rationale: One advice surface. AdviceFactory.cs:1406 rejects an indexer in an extension block by design, a restriction that issue #1587 recorded in the documentation; C# 15 makes it a gap. The story removes the validation, adds the eligibility rules that the language requires (a named receiver parameter, no init accessor, no abstract, virtual, override, new, sealed, partial or protected modifier), creates the accessor methods in the introduction transformation, and adds the overriding and contract tests, including the receiver-parameter contract that issue #1127 established. The non-inlined trampoline is bounded by the pre-existing LAMA0699 limitation tracked in issue #937, which the story must state rather than fix. Every test needs the C# 15 language version, hence the dependency on S06.

stories.title: Decide what happens to a template declared inside an extension block
stories.rationale: A pre-existing gap in ProduceCompileTimeCodeRewriter, unrelated to C# 15 and reachable since C# 14: the member switch of TransformCompileTimeType at CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.ProduceCompileTimeCodeRewriter.cs:506-562 throws for an indexer and falls through for an extension block, so a template declared inside an extension block is copied verbatim. The cheap outcome is a diagnostic; supporting it requires extracting the member loop, because ExtensionBlockDeclarationSyntax is a TypeDeclarationSyntax whose Identifier returns default and whose base-list mutators throw. It is filed separately so that it is not blocked by, and does not delay, the C# 15 chain.

stories.title: Make the attribute-adding code action cover every declaration kind
stories.rationale: One file, Metalama.Framework.DesignTime/Refactoring/CSharpAttributeHelper.cs, whose per-kind switch at :74-191 returns null for records, record structs and extension blocks today, and would return null for unions later; the caller propagates the null and the code action does nothing. Replacing the type and member arms by one call to MemberDeclarationSyntax.AddAttributeLists, narrowed so that namespaces, enum members and global statements keep returning null, covers all of them without naming a syntax kind that the Roslyn 5.0 variant lacks. The trivia tests added for issue #779 must not regress. The record and extension-block half is independent of C# 15 and can ship at any time; only the union test waits for the variant decision.

stories.title: Workspaces, LinqPad and the design-time host simulator against the .NET 11 SDK
stories.rationale: One area, the components that host MSBuild in process: Metalama.Framework.Workspaces with its MSBuildInitializer, the LinqPad driver, and Metalama.DesignTime.HostSimulator with the DesignTimeSolution entry of eng/src. They share one rule, the selection of an SDK whose major version does not exceed the host runtime major, which makes a .NET 10 host refuse a machine that carries only the .NET 11 SDK, and they share the MicrosoftBuildVersion pin, which stays at the lowest supported host and needs verification rather than a bump. LV-10 belongs here because the net10.0 literals it inventories are exactly these projects plus the payload folder names, and the story is the right place to record which of them move with the SDK pin and which move only with the embedded Core flavour. DT-9 contributes the package README statement that a .NET 10 host needs a .NET 10 SDK.

stories.title: Add net11.0 legs to the test projects and the standalone scenarios
stories.rationale: The declared support matrix names net11.0 and the .NET 11 SDK, and nothing executes on either. The story adds the second Core leg to the test projects, adds net11.0 and net11.0-windows to Standalone/SupportedPlatform.TestedTargetFrameworks while correcting the comment that says they are omitted, adds a net11.0 sibling of the default language version scenario that clears LangVersion so that the implied version is observable, and re-derives the test infrastructure package pins and their stale comments. It is sized L because the snapshots of the aspect tests may diverge between the two legs and each divergence has to be read rather than adopted. It must not be started before S02, since the maximum SDK warning would otherwise fail the scenarios that forbid warnings.

stories.title: Replace the residual net8.0 constants in the engine and the test defaults
stories.rationale: Two constants that the removal of .NET 8 in issue #1876 did not reach, because they are C# literals rather than build files: the default target frameworks of the nested compile-time reference project in CompileTimeAssemblyLocator, which makes an additional compile-time package resolve its netstandard2.0 asset and keeps restoring an out-of-support target framework, and the target framework that DefaultProjectOptions reports, which makes every test observe net8.0 whatever the leg targets. The fixtures that pin the first value, including the Issue1789 standalone scenario and its unit test, are edited in the same change, and one aspect test snapshot that prints the second value has to be re-accepted.

stories.title: Remove the dead preprocessor gates that silently exclude tests
stories.rationale: Two test suites contain conditions on symbols that no configuration defines, so the tests never run and nothing fails. DoubleTests in the Contracts unit tests is guarded on NET6_0 rather than NET6_0_OR_GREATER and must keep a guard, because the two facts call Math.BitDecrement and Math.BitIncrement, which the net472 leg does not have. Two interface-implementation aspect tests are gated on ROSLYN4_4_OR_GREATER, a name that no variant defines and that the cleanup of issue #1881 missed because it does not follow the ROSLYN_ naming convention; the target framework gate must stay, because both declare a static abstract operator. Re-enabling them may expose real behaviour differences, which is why the story includes reading and adopting the results rather than only editing the directives.

stories.title: Re-run the dependency audit under the .NET 11 SDK and correct the pin comments
stories.rationale: No version bump follows from .NET 11: package pruning and the transitive audit default are behaviours of the .NET 10 SDK and are unchanged, and the end-of-life warning for net8.0 is not in the .NET 11 SDK sources. What remains is hygiene in Directory.Packages.props and the test props: re-run the vulnerability audit under the new SDK, remove the audit suppressions whose cause the Roslyn floor move removed, correct the comment on the audit mode override, which is now live for a different reason than the one it states, and record the rule that decides the per-variant System.Text.Json version. The audience paragraph of Directory.Packages.md is deliberately excluded, because issue #1903 already owns it.

stories.title: Unions in the pattern and extension libraries
stories.rationale: One area, Metalama.Patterns and Metalama.Extensions, four aspects and one shared premise: a union is an ordinary struct to every one of them. Observability already rejects it and needs only a test that pins the two diagnostics; Immutability classifies it as mutable and produces a spurious warning, which needs a classification rule that distinguishes the declaration form from a hand-written attributed type; Caching keys and serialises it as an opaque struct, which needs a discriminator, and the practical one is the interface that the generated struct implements rather than an attribute lookup; Multicast is correct for every target except the implicit parameterless constructor, where materialising an override produces a compiler error. The four are one pull request because they share the code model member that S13 adds and the same test shape.

stories.title: C# 15 statement and collection syntax coverage in the metrics and observability tests
stories.rationale: No product change. The metric providers count nodes and statements generically, so a labeled break and a with element need no new case, and the value of the story is the tests that record it: two metric unit tests, which can be written before the language version moves if the compilation ignores the feature diagnostic, and one observability aspect test with a labeled loop in a getter, which needs both the variant constant and the language version directive and therefore waits for S06.

stories.title: Correct the documentation that names removed members, dropped target frameworks and superseded versions
stories.rationale: One pull request over the Markdown of the Metalama repository, so that four sets of edits do not conflict in platform-support.md. It corrects the Roslyn variant update procedure, which still names a member renamed by the merged pull request #1911 and merges the add-a-variant list with the renumbering list; it replaces the stale member names in platform-support.md and Directory.Packages.md; it rewrites the target framework and language version statements that still name net8.0 and C# 14 as the latest; it adds the Metalama.Premium section beside the existing section about Metalama.Compiler and extends the drift-point list to the Premium build files, which are the two Premium findings that nonetheless edit files in this repository. Two items are deliberately excluded: the audience paragraph owned by issue #1903, and the source generator attribute list, which is functional rather than documentation and needs its own behavioural change and test. Metalama.Documentation is listed because whether release notes live there rather than in NOTES.md is an open question.

stories.title: Metalama.Premium: mirror the Roslyn 5.12 renumbering and leave the prerelease feed
stories.rationale: The same edit set as S04 in the second repository, and it cannot be the same pull request. Premium carries the prerelease Roslyn version in two fallback literals of Directory.Packages.props, in nuget.base.config, in the variant property file, and in eleven tracked files that repeat the version string: the InternalsVisibleTo entries, the packaging paths and the extension-assembly metadata with its TargetRoslynVersion attributes. If the two repositories do not move in the same release, either the feed is removed on one side while the other still resolves a preview from it, or Premium ships variant assemblies whose name no longer matches the variant the core repository loads, which the extension loader drops without a diagnostic.

stories.title: Metalama.Premium: execute the Roslyn 5.0 variant of the engines in tests
stories.rationale: The lower variant of the Premium engines is compiled by the solution build but never executed, and it is the variant that serves Rider and the C# Dev Kit, hosts that nobody tests by hand. The story first makes the existing aspect test projects variant-aware, replacing the hardcoded project reference to the unsuffixed engine by the suffixed pattern that the core aspect test project already uses, and only then adds the variant shims; without that order a shim would compile the test sources under one property set and load the other engine. The unit test shims additionally need a Roslyn 5.0 variant of the core unit test helper package, which is a change in the other repository and is the reason for the L size. The stale comment about a variant constant that no longer exists is corrected by the same change, since it is corrected by removing its cause.

stories.title: Metalama.Premium: resolve the residual and contradictory package pins
stories.rationale: One file, Directory.Packages.props of the Premium repository. It carries Microsoft.Build pins below the core value, a package entry that no project references and that does not exist on nuget.org, a dead property in the test props, and rationale comments that name a Visual Studio version the baseline no longer supports. It also carries two entries for the same Redis client, which makes the intended version update inert, so the backend ships against an older client than the file intends. The Microsoft.Build raise must follow, or accompany, the move of the licensing build task off the older target framework, because the newer package has no compile asset for it.

stories.title: Metalama.Premium: raise the template language version to C# 14
stories.rationale: One property and its comment in the Premium Directory.Build.props. The value is still 13.0 with a rationale that names a Visual Studio version, while the blocker that the core issue #1896 recorded, the Roslyn 4.12 variant, has been removed by the merged Premium pull request #85. The comment must name the lowest Roslyn variant of this repository rather than copying the core text verbatim, because Premium defines no RoslynApiMinVersion property. The change has no user-visible effect, since the Premium packages contain validators rather than templates, but it makes the two repositories move together on the next floor change and it changes which system-type polyfills the Premium compile-time compilation embeds, which should be expected rather than investigated.

stories.title: Metalama.Premium: make the accessibility code fix cover every declaration kind
stories.rationale: One file, ChangeVisibilityCodeAction, whose per-kind overrides silently skip interfaces and indexers today and would skip unions later, so the code action reports success and changes nothing. Replacing the type-declaration arms by one branch over TypeDeclarationSyntax.WithModifiers, placed in the VisitCore override because the base Visit is sealed, covers interfaces now and unions when the variant moves, without naming a syntax type that the lower variant lacks. The interface and indexer half is independent of C# 15 and can ship immediately; only the union test waits for the variant decision of S09.

stories.title: Metalama.Premium: accept an extension block as a reference validation target
stories.rationale: One switch arm. ReferenceValidationContext.GetInboundGranularity throws for a validated extension block, and the exception is reported as an error diagnostic from inside the user validator, so a customer of the current release can reach it: extension blocks are C# 14 and already ship. The story maps the declaration kind to the type granularity and adds the aspect test with an extension method, which compiles against the Roslyn the repository consumes today. The extension indexer variant of the test is added later, when the language version allows it, and is not a reason to delay this fix.

stories.title: Index the case types of a union in the reference graph, and pin it with architecture rule tests
stories.rationale: The only union defect that the Premium analysis found is in the core reference graph: the reference index walker has no union declaration override, so a reference from a union to its case types is never attributed and an architecture rule on a case type under-reports with no diagnostic. The fix is one override in the core walker on the latest variant; the acceptance criterion is two architecture rule tests in the Premium repository, which is why both repositories are listed and why the core half must land first. The closed modifier needs nothing in either repository.

stories.title: Metalama.Premium: remove the obsolete build container components
stories.rationale: The main body of the container move is merged: the Premium pull request #86 raised the engineering package, moved the image to the Visual Studio 2026 build tools, set the MSBuild version and removed the .NET 9 runtime. What remains is small and local to eng/src/Program.cs and the docker context: the .NET 8 SDK and .NET 6 runtime components, whose stated reason disappeared when every net8.0 target framework was replaced, the stale Visual Studio 2022 channel manifest still sitting at the top of the docker context, and the decision whether the prerelease flag of the SDK version should follow the core repository.

stories.title: Metalama.Premium: a .NET 11 SDK test leg
stories.rationale: Premium mirrors the core gap: nothing exercises the .NET 11 host runtime, the net11.0 target framework or the compiler whose default language version changes with the stable SDK. The story follows whatever the core repository decides in S01 and S24, applying it to the solution and the three MSBuild-based standalone entries of the Premium eng project. It is worth scheduling only after the stable .NET 11 SDK ships, because a preview SDK carries a compiler that still defaults to the previous language version and would prove nothing. The originally suspected risk, an assembly binding failure of the merged licensing task on the newer runtime, is unlikely and is not the justification.

stories.title: Already delivered: the Premium variant alignment and the net10.0 build project
stories.rationale: No new work. Both findings are fully covered by merged pull requests and are listed here only so that they are not proposed again. The Premium pull request #85 deleted the Roslyn 4.12 variant, added the lower and latest variants with their package pins, InternalsVisibleTo entries and packaging paths, and added the configuration that declares the prerelease feed; the Premium pull request #86 retargeted the engineering project and removed the runtime component that only it required. The residues of those changes are tracked by S31, S32 and S38, not here.

decisions: Does C# 15 support ship in 2027.0 at all? No Roslyn that Metalama consumes today exposes C# 15 as a non-preview language version: the stable 5.9.0 and the consumed 5.10.0-1.26365.3 preview reach the six features only under LanguageVersion.Preview, and LanguageVersion.CSharp15 exists only on the main branch that becomes 5.12, expected with Visual Studio 2027 and the .NET 11 SDK in November 2026, with the release general availability on 2027-01-01. Option A, full support: the whole chain S04 to S20 and S28 lands after the Roslyn 5.12 rebase of Metalama.Compiler, which leaves roughly six weeks between the stable Roslyn and the release date for work sized at several weeks. Option B, plumbing only: ship S04 to S08, so that a C# 15 project builds, reports the designed diagnostics instead of crashing, and is not silently downgraded to C# 12 by the clamp, and refuse advice on a union with one clear diagnostic (S16), while unions, closed classes, labeled break and extension indexers remain unsupported and are documented as such. Option C, defer: keep the latest variant on the prerelease Roslyn, which DT-8 shows is a restore failure for every external consumer of three published packages and therefore not shippable as it stands. Option B is the only one that does not depend on an external date, and it is the one the rest of this plan is sequenced for.

How is the union and closed API gated between the Roslyn 5.0 variant and the latest variant? Metalama.Framework.Engine.5.0.0 compiles the same source files against a Roslyn whose public API has neither UnionDeclarationSyntax nor ITypeSymbol.IsUnion, and issue #1881 removed all 177 conditional-compilation blocks from production source on purpose. Option A, conditional compilation: reverses part of that decision, is the only mechanism that can carry a visitor override or a syntax factory call, and requires the constant to be renamed with every variant renumbering. Option B, numeric syntax-kind values with a runtime guard on the current variant: names no experimental member, keeps one source file, and cannot express an override or a factory call. Option C, a per-variant service resolved through the existing dependency injection: reintroduces the reflection that issue #1215 deliberately removed. The realistic answer is a mixture, conditional compilation for the overrides and the factory calls and a numeric or resolved value for the kind tests, and the product owner has to accept that production source will carry variant branches again. This is story S09 and it blocks eight other stories, so it should be decided first.

What does the Roslyn 5.0 variant do when it meets a union or a closed type that it cannot see? Option A, silence: IsUnion and IsClosed return false, so Rider and the C# Dev Kit treat a union as an ordinary struct and an aspect may produce code that the command-line build rejects, with no design-time indication. Option B, a diagnostic: the lower variant reports that the type uses a language feature it cannot model, which is honest and noisy, since the same project builds correctly from the command line. Option C, no design-time implementation for such a project, following the degradation that issue #1898 introduced for a host below the Roslyn floor. The choice decides how a Rider user experiences a solution that contains one union.

Are unions supported as aspect targets in 2027.0, or refused? Option A, support: requires S13, S14, S15 and the union parts of S10, S11 and S12, and even then most advice produces code the compiler rejects, because a union forbids instance fields, auto-properties, field-like events, a public single-parameter constructor and an unchained constructor. Option B, refuse with one diagnostic (S16 alone): costs a fraction of the work, prevents every silently invalid output, and can be delivered before the Roslyn move, since it needs only the code model flag. Option C, refuse for advice but read correctly, that is S13 plus S16 plus the syntax plumbing, so that unions are visible to fabrics, validators and architecture rules while advice on them is declined. Option C is the natural first release and Option A the natural second.

Can an aspect introduce a closed class, and can it introduce a union? The closed modifier is one settable property and one token in the modifier list (S17) and is cheap; a union is not, because introduced type support does not cover structs, records, enums or delegates today (issues #869, #867, #866, #865 are all open). Option A, closed only, with union introduction stated as out of scope. Option B, neither, which leaves the code model asymmetric once IsClosed is readable. Option C, both, which is a large piece of work with no evidence of demand.

Does the template language version move to C# 15, and what is the consequence for Rider? MetalamaTemplateLanguageVersion is pinned to 14.0 and the comment in Directory.Build.props ties it to the lowest Roslyn variant, because the compile-time assembly of an aspect library must be compilable inside every supported host. Option A, keep 14.0: aspect authors cannot use C# 15 in templates, which is a documented limitation and costs nothing. Option B, raise to 15.0: an aspect library whose templates use C# 15 cannot have its compile-time assembly built inside Rider 2026.2, which runs on Roslyn 5.0. Option C, 15.0 as an opt-in property with a documented consequence. The question is whether the Rider limitation is acceptable, and only the product owner can weigh it.

Should the .NET 11 SDK be installed in the build container as a second feature band, and what does global.json pin? A second SDK is the prerequisite of every net11.0 test leg (S01, S24, S39), and the comment at eng/src/Program.cs:19-25 records that two bands under one dotnet directory already caused an MSB4062 restore failure whose mitigation in PostSharp.Engineering is incomplete by one environment variable. Option A, add the second SDK and complete the mitigation first, which is an external change in PostSharp.Engineering. Option B, keep one SDK and accept that net11.0 remains declared and untested, which the exclusion comment of the tested-target-framework scenario already admits. Option C, move the container to a .NET 11 SDK entirely, which would exercise net11.0 and stop exercising the .NET 10 SDK that the baseline also declares supported.

Is a container regeneration for the November 2026 Visual Studio acceptable? Issue #1902 was closed as not planned in September 2026 with the reason that regenerating the Visual Studio base images is expensive and the move was hygiene without benefit, and the container has since moved to the 18.9.2 build tools anyway. The November 2026 long-term servicing baseline is the floor that platform-support.md names, so testing on 18.9 tests a version below the floor. Option A, regenerate for the November baseline, accepting the cost once. Option B, stay on 18.9 and document that the build host is below the declared floor. The same decision governs whether the Visual Studio floor measurement scheduled for after 2026-11-10 is performed on time.

Is the prerelease Roslyn pin a release gate, and for which releases? Metalama.Framework.Workspaces, Metalama.Testing.AspectTesting and Metalama.LinqPad currently declare a dependency on a Roslyn version that nuget.org does not serve, which failed for a user in issue #1106. Option A, gate the general availability only, so that previews may ship with the prerelease pin, which reproduces #1106 for anyone who restores a preview. Option B, gate every public publication, including previews, which means either moving to the stable Roslyn earlier or renumbering the latest variant to the stable 5.9.0, which exposes the same public API as the consumed preview and is available today. Option B with a build-time check that refuses to pack a prerelease Roslyn pin is the safe answer and costs one target.

Should the aspect test harness fail rather than skip when a requested language version is not available? Today an unrecognised @LanguageVersion marks the test skipped with a reason and the suite passes, which is correct when a variant genuinely cannot serve the version and wrong when a whole C# 15 suite disappears without anyone noticing. Option A, keep skipping, and rely on reviewers reading the skip list. Option B, fail when the version is one the current baseline claims to support and skip only when the running variant is the reason. Option B changes the behaviour of a shared harness that the Patterns and Premium suites also use, so it needs an explicit decision.

How is a union exposed in the public code model? Option A, INamedType.IsUnion beside IsRecord, with the case types as a separate member, which follows the precedent that TypeKind.RecordClass and TypeKind.RecordStruct were made obsolete in favour of a flag and avoids adding an arm to seventeen switches, twelve of which throw in the default arm. Option B, a TypeKind.Union value, which is more discoverable and is a breaking change for every user switch over TypeKind. A second part of the same question: the Roslyn flag is also true for a hand-written class or struct carrying the union attribute, so the model has to decide whether IsUnion means the declaration form or the attributed form, and the design-time partial generator (S14) and the immutability classification (S28) each need the declaration form specifically.

Does the LinqPad driver get a .NET 11 target, and does Metalama.Tool keep the rule that refuses an SDK newer than the host runtime? The rule makes a .NET 10 host refuse a machine that carries only the .NET 11 SDK, which is plausible once the .NET 11 SDK is the default installation. Option A, leave it and document that a .NET 10 host needs a .NET 10 SDK. Option B, relax the rule, given that Roslyn performs the project evaluation in a build host process that selects its own runtime. Option C, add a .NET 11 target to the affected packages, which depends on the runtime that a LINQPad release hosts, a fact that could not be established in this session.

Where do the release notes and the user-facing platform statements live? Several documentation corrections in S30 assume that NOTES.md in this repository is the release note, and the file does not say. If the release notes live in Metalama.Documentation instead, the story acquires a second repository and a second reviewer, and the statement that the template language stays at C# 14 while user code may use a later version has to be written for a user audience rather than a contributor audience.

The theme document for "Union types and closed hierarchies in the code model" is written at Metalama.Framework/docs/2027.0/03-code-model-unions-closed.md (872 lines), following the house style of the sibling document 02-syntax-generator-and-templates.md and the prescribed structure: title, scope paragraph naming the date and the branch, Summary (8 numbered items), Findings (CM-1 to CM-10, each with Where, What happens today, Consequence, Proposed change, Size, Status, Verification and Open questions), Withdrawn findings, Non-findings, Related themes.

All ten findings were kept; none was withdrawn, so the "Withdrawn findings" section instead records the two findings whose mechanism changed materially (CM-1 and CM-9) and the three individual claims that the verification passes refuted without removing the finding that carried them, so that the reader knows they were considered.

Corrections merged into the fields, with the code lens taken as authoritative for repository paths and line numbers and the semantics lens for Roslyn and csharplang behaviour. Where the two lenses disagreed on a line number I re-read the file with grep and sed rather than choose: ModifierHelper.cs (abstract at :226, sealed at :231), IMemberOrNamedTypeBuilder.cs (45 lines, so the cited range 64-95 does not exist), NamedTypeBuilderData.cs (57 lines, so :364 does not exist), SourceNamedTypeImpl.cs (CanBeInherited :44, IsReferenceType :133, IsRecord :173, HasDefaultConstructor :175-179, Constructors :247), DesignTimeSyntaxTreeGenerator.cs (CreatePartialType :697-790 with arms at :722, :734, :749, :761, :776 and a throwing default at :788; AddHeader :817, applied at :332), SyntaxExtensions.cs (the three kind lists at :29-36, :57-64 and :116-118), Linking/SymbolExtensions.cs (GetDeclarationFlags :18, list :29, throw :63), TypeKind.cs (:29-30 and :67-68 with their exact obsolete messages), GeneralDiagnosticDescriptors.cs:209 (TypeNotPartial), and KindCheckOptimizationAnalyzerTests.cs (line 1115 opens the IsRecordDeclaration region; the IsTypeDeclaration tests are at :951 and :1309, and they pin no set of syntax kinds). One path in the Non-findings section was wrong in the source report and was corrected after checking the file system: DocumentationIdHelper.GeneratorOfDeclarationIdFromDeclaration.cs is under SerializableIds, not Formatting.

Substantive merges worth noting for the story writers: CM-1's consequence is now silent loss of the introduced member through the missing VisitUnionDeclaration override of the linker injection rewriter, not the compiler error CS9373; CM-2 is medium rather than small, because the edit cannot be written without the CM-10 mechanism; CM-3's open question is resolved in the opposite direction (the generated part must omit the case list) and the arm must precede the existing struct arm and pass the base list; CM-5's open question about [CompilerFeatureRequired("ClosedClasses")] is answered and closed as no impact; CM-9's failing placements are a union inside a namespace and a union nested in a compile-time type, while a top-level union is filtered out; CM-10 gains a fourth mechanism and the finding that the consumed Roslyn build lacks ITypeSymbol.UnionCaseTypes entirely and marks the rest RSEXPERIMENTAL006.

Cross-references follow the clusters rather than repeating findings owned elsewhere: CL-01 (CM-2, CM-6 with LK-3, DT-1, DT-6), CL-02 (CM-7 with LK-10), CL-03 (CM-9 with TP-6, owned by the templates theme, stated in CM-9's Status), CL-04 (CM-3 with DT-2 and LK-4, owned by the design-time theme), CL-13 (CM-8 with LK-1, LK-2, LK-8, owned by the linker theme, and the dependency on the open pull request #1879), CL-14 (CM-4 and CM-5 with LK-5, which duplicates CM-4, plus TP-10 and UT-15), CL-05 and CL-06 (the Roslyn 5.12 renumbering and the C# 15 language version tables), CL-18 (UT-14 and PR-12 as consumers of the CM-1 surface), and CL-09 (CM-10 as the prerequisite of everything else).

Status values: CM-1 to CM-9 are "new work" (every scope lens found them neither implemented, in progress nor tracked); CM-10 is "decision required", naming the choice of variant mechanism. Issue references are given as #NNNN and are limited to those in the verified data. The platform baseline is referred to as PB-2027.0 and platform-support.md, Directory.Packages.md and updating-roslyn.md are cited by link rather than restated. No file outside the named output was modified, nothing was built and no test was run.
