findings.title: Regeneration of the 5.10.0 generated files when the stable grammar drops ExperimentalUrl
findings.what_happens_today:
TreeReader.ReadTree removes the four experimental declarations before VersionDetector and Generator run, so the 5.10.0 outputs are structurally identical to the 5.0.0 outputs for these nodes. Generation runs in OnPrepareCompleted (eng/src/Program.cs:237-260), which the prepare step of Build.ps1 raises; the CI configurations run Build.ps1 test, which begins with the prepare step (CLAUDE.md, "Debugging Build Issues", item 2). The outputs land in Metalama.Framework/.generated/<version>/... (GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter.cs:37), are git-ignored (.gitignore:62) and are compiled through the wildcard includes of the Engine and DesignTime projects. There is no hand-written visitor that must be edited in step; the hand-written partial classes (MetaSyntaxRewriter.cs, RoslynVersionSyntaxVerifier.cs, BaseCodeHasher.cs) contain no member per node kind.

What changes on regeneration, for the 5.10.0 directory only (the 5.0.0 directory derives from Syntax-5.0.0.xml, GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter.cs:30-37):
- Metalama.Framework.Engine/MetaSyntaxRewriter.g.cs: new VisitUnionDeclaration/TransformUnionDeclaration, VisitWithElement/TransformWithElement, VisitUnsafeExpression/TransformUnsafeExpression (Generator.cs:403-431). TransformBreakStatement and TransformContinueStatement change from a single factory call to a switch (this.TargetApiVersion) with cases V4_0_1 to V5_0_0 calling the three-argument SyntaxFactory.BreakStatement and case V5_10_0 calling the four-argument overload with Transform(node.Name) (Generator.cs:432-479; the fields have different MinimalRoslynVersion values, VersionDetector.cs:159-184). MetaSyntaxFactoryImpl gains UnionDeclaration, WithElement and UnsafeExpression methods, and its BreakStatement/ContinueStatement methods gain a name parameter (Generator.cs:537-602). No hand-written code calls MetaSyntaxFactory.BreakStatement or ContinueStatement (grep of Metalama.Framework.Engine excluding .g.cs: no match).
- Metalama.Framework.Engine/RoslynVersionSyntaxVerifier.g.cs: new VisitUnionDeclaration, VisitWithElement and VisitUnsafeExpression overrides calling VisitVersionSpecificNode(node, RoslynApiVersion.V5_10_0) (Generator.cs:118-124); new VisitBreakStatement and VisitContinueStatement overrides calling VisitVersionSpecificField(node.Name, RoslynApiVersion.V5_10_0) (Generator.cs:127-156).
- Metalama.Framework.Engine/SyntaxNodePartialUpdateExtensions.g.cs: PartialUpdate for BreakStatementSyntax/ContinueStatementSyntax gains an Option<IdentifierNameSyntax?> name parameter and calls the four-argument Update; new PartialUpdate methods for the three new nodes (Generator.cs:761-800). No hand-written caller passes positional arguments to these two methods (grep of .PartialUpdate( for break or continue: no match), so the 57 existing call sites are unaffected.
- Metalama.Framework.DesignTime/RunTimeCodeHasher.g.cs and CompileTimeCodeHasher.g.cs: VisitBreakStatement/VisitContinueStatement gain this.Visit(node.Name); new VisitUnionDeclaration, VisitWithElement, VisitUnsafeExpression (Generator.cs:637-708).
- Metalama.Framework.Engine/RoslynApiVersion.g.cs: unchanged, because the version list is unchanged (Generator.cs:64-98).

Precondition that is easy to miss: the generated code references BreakStatementSyntax.Name and the three node types directly. With the currently consumed package 5.10.0-1.26365.3 those members carry [Experimental], and a reference from generated code is an RSEXPERIMENTAL error (TreeType.cs:428-435, Field.cs:347-354). Regeneration therefore has to wait until RoslynApiMaxVersion (Directory.Packages.props:28) is the stable 5.10 package, and Syntax-5.10.0.xml has to be replaced by the stable grammar at the same time (Metalama.Framework/docs/updating-roslyn.md:11-14). If only the package is updated and the XML keeps the attributes, the stripping stays in force and nothing is generated; if only the XML is updated, the build of Metalama.Framework.Engine.5.10.0 fails with RSEXPERIMENTAL. Neither mismatch is detected by a test.
findings.consequence_class: Build or restore error (if the two updates are not simultaneous); otherwise no impact.
findings.proposed_change: Add a unit test in Metalama.Framework.Tests.UnitTests (or a check in GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter.Generate) that fails when Syntax-<RoslynApiMaxVersion>.xml still declares an ExperimentalUrl on a node while the consumed package version carries no prerelease label, so that step 4 of updating-roslyn.md cannot be forgotten; add to updating-roslyn.md the sentence that a stable grammar un-strips nodes and therefore changes the generated code of the latest variant.
findings.confidence: Verified (generator behaviour), plausible (Roslyn attribute on the stable package).
open_questions: Whether the stable Roslyn 5.10 keeps UnsafeExpressionSyntax experimental (the feature is Preview only according to FACTS). If it does, the node stays stripped and TP-5 remains in force after regeneration.

findings.title: The version checker maps Roslyn 5.10 to C# 14, so C# 15 syntax passes as C# 14
findings.what_happens_today: For a node that exists only in the latest grammar, the generator emits an override that calls VisitVersionSpecificNode(node, RoslynApiVersion.V5_10_0) and does not call the base visitor, so the children of such a node are not walked (Generator.cs:120-123). VisitVersionSpecificNode reports LAMA0232 when version.ToLanguageVersion() > MaximalAcceptableLanguageVersion and raises MaximalUsedVersion (RoslynVersionSyntaxVerifier.cs:41-52). MaximalUsedVersion becomes usedApiVersion, which is the TargetApiVersion of the TemplateCompilerRewriter (TemplateCompiler.cs:108, :232) and the UsedApiVersion stored in the manifest, from which LAMA0282 is derived (TemplateExpansionContext.cs:864-877). Because ToLanguageVersion(V5_10_0) is CSharp14 (SupportedCSharpVersions.cs:60), a regenerated verifier would accept break outer;, with(...) and union in a template whose language version is 14 (no LAMA0232), and an aspect using them would not warn with LAMA0282 when applied to a C# 14 project. The TargetApiVersion switch of TransformBreakStatement (TP-1) would still select the four-argument factory, so the generated code would be right, but the diagnostics would be wrong. GetMaxLanguageVersion (SupportedCSharpVersions.cs:149-159) has the same defect for the msbuild.exe path of LanguageVersionProvider (LanguageVersionProvider.cs:111).
findings.consequence_class: Silent wrong output (missing diagnostics), after regeneration.
findings.proposed_change: In the same change as the grammar update, set RoslynApiVersion.V5_10_0 => AllLanguageVersions.CSharp15 in ToLanguageVersion, add (5, >= 10) => AllLanguageVersions.CSharp15 before (>= 5, _) => AllLanguageVersions.CSharp14 in GetMaxLanguageVersion, and add CSharp15 = (LanguageVersion) 1500 to AllLanguageVersions.cs:14-18. Add an aspect test under Tests/Aspects/LanguageVersion/ in the style of Template_OldVersion.cs (@LanguageVersion(14) on the target project, a Dependency.cs aspect using break outer;) expecting LAMA0282, and a standalone scenario in the style of Standalone/TemplateLanguageVersion14 expecting LAMA0232 with MetalamaTemplateLanguageVersion=14.0.

findings.title: Labeled break and continue are not modelled by the annotator; the label is dropped silently by the generated rewriter
findings.what_happens_today:
Template scope classification: VisitBreakStatement and VisitContinueStatement annotate the statement with CurrentBreakOrContinueScope (TemplateAnnotator.cs:1375-1379), which every loop and switch sets to its own scope for its body (ScopeContext.cs:123-132, callers at :1414, :2500, :2533, :2559, :2927). The Name child is never read, so a break outer; inside a run-time inner loop nested in a compile-time outer loop is classified run-time, and the reverse is classified compile-time, whatever the label designates. Neither TemplateAnnotator nor TemplateCompilerRewriter overrides VisitLabeledStatement (override lists at TemplateAnnotator.cs:702-3505 and TemplateCompilerRewriter.cs:306-3289); a labeled statement gets no scope annotation of its own because AddScopeAnnotationToVisitedNode returns statements untouched (TemplateAnnotator.cs:676-680), and its transformation kind is then decided by IsCompileTimeCode from the parent chain or from an annotation forced by an enclosing compile-time if or foreach (TemplateAnnotator.cs:1360-1361, :1423; TemplateCompilerRewriter.cs:196-266).

Run-time scope: the generated TransformBreakStatement builds SyntaxFactory.BreakStatement(attributeLists, breakKeyword, semicolonToken) from the stripped field list (Generator.cs:481-519), so the label is dropped and the generated run-time code contains a plain break; that exits the innermost loop of the target. No diagnostic.

Compile-time scope: the statement is kept as compile-time C# (TemplateCompilerRewriter.cs:2266-2287, case StatementSyntax). The base CSharpSyntaxRewriter.VisitBreakStatement visits Name through VisitIdentifierName (TemplateCompilerRewriter.cs:2908-2980), where the compile-time branch delegates to _compileTimeOnlyRewriter (:2980), so the label identifier is preserved. The result is a compile-time break outer; inside the compiled template; whether the compile-time compilation accepts it depends on TP-8 (compile-time language version) and on whether Roslyn enforces IDS_FeatureLabeledBreakContinue in the binder or only in the parser, since CSharpSyntaxTree.Create does not re-parse (CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.cs:349-354).

A labeled statement whose loop is run-time inside a compile-time block: the forced CompileTimeOnly annotation (TemplateAnnotator.cs:1423) makes the generated VisitLabeledStatement take the base.VisitLabeledStatement branch (Generator.cs:419-420), which casts the transformed child, an InvocationExpressionSyntax, to StatementSyntax. The InvalidCastException is wrapped into SyntaxProcessingException by SafeSyntaxRewriter.Visit (SafeSyntaxRewriter.cs:56-61). A labeled statement directly in the template body has no annotation and is transformed as run-time code (TemplateCompilerRewriter.cs:239-262, the null parent case returns false), which wraps a compile-time loop into a run-time labeled block through TransformStatement (TemplateCompilerRewriter.cs:625-630). Labels are useless in templates today because goto is rejected (TemplateAnnotator.cs:2601-2606), so none of these paths is covered by a test (Tests/UnsupportedSyntax/GotoNotSupported.cs is the only labeled statement in the template test suites).

Reachability: a template containing break outer; is rejected before any of this runs while the aspect project is compiled at C# 14 or lower, because the parser reports the feature error and TemplateCompiler.TryCompile stops on source errors (TemplateCompiler.cs:159-217); C# 15 and preview are refused by VerifyLanguageVersion (CompileTimeAspectPipeline.cs:62-90) unless MetalamaAllowPreviewLanguageFeatures is set. Adding C# 15 to SupportedCSharpVersions.All (TP-8) opens all the paths above.
findings.consequence_class: Silent wrong output (run-time scope, before regeneration); assertion or crash (labeled run-time loop inside a compile-time block); after regeneration, a run-time break outer; whose label was on a compile-time loop produces CS0159 in the transformed user code, which is a diagnostic reported in generated code.
findings.proposed_change: (1) In TemplateAnnotator, add VisitLabeledStatement that visits the inner statement and copies its scope annotation to the labeled statement, and record label name -> scope in ScopeContext; (2) in VisitBreakStatement/VisitContinueStatement, when Name is not null resolve the label scope from the context, annotate the statement with that scope, and report a new error (in the family of TemplatingDiagnosticDescriptors, next to LAMA0101) when a run-time break targets a compile-time loop, since the unrolled loop has no run-time counterpart; a compile-time break targeting a run-time loop must be annotated run-time so that the label survives in the generated code; (3) in TemplateCompilerRewriter, handle a labeled statement whose inner statement is run-time by transforming the whole labeled statement (the generated TransformLabeledStatement already exists) instead of letting the base rewriter cast. Because BreakStatementSyntax.Name is absent from Roslyn 5.0 and experimental in the current 5.10 package, step (2) must read the label through node.ChildNodes().OfType<IdentifierNameSyntax>() until the stable package is consumed, or be written after the package update. Add template tests under Tests/Syntax/ for the four combinations (compile-time or run-time outer loop, compile-time or run-time inner loop) with @LanguageVersion(15.0) so that the Roslyn 5.0 variant skips them (TestOptions.cs:681-699).
findings.confidence: Verified (annotation and generated factory paths), plausible (exact exception for the labeled run-time loop; the exact Roslyn base-visitor cast could not be read).
open_questions: Whether Roslyn checks IDS_FeatureLabeledBreakContinue in the parser only; if so, the compile-time compilation created with C# 14 parse options accepts a compile-time break outer; silently, and only the host Roslyn version decides.

findings.title: A collection expression with a with(...) element crashes the template compiler in run-time scope
findings.what_happens_today:
The annotator visits each element through DefaultVisitImpl (TemplateAnnotator.cs:3497); a WithElementSyntax has no ExpressionSyntax child (its only child is an ArgumentListSyntax), so it receives the neutral combined scope and follows the collection expression (:686-697). In run-time scope the generated TransformCollectionExpression calls Transform(node.Elements), which calls Transform<T>(element) for each element (MetaSyntaxRewriter.cs:144-158), which calls this.Visit(element) and casts the result to ExpressionSyntax (:137). There is no generated VisitWithElement, so CSharpSyntaxRewriter.VisitWithElement runs, visits ArgumentList through the generated VisitArgumentList, which returns an InvocationExpressionSyntax, and casts it to ArgumentListSyntax (assumption on the shape of the Roslyn base visitor). The InvalidCastException becomes a SyntaxProcessingException. In compile-time scope the collection expression is kept verbatim and reaches the compile-time compilation (TP-8 decides whether it compiles).

After regeneration: TransformWithElement calls WithElement(Transform(node.WithKeyword), Transform(node.ArgumentList)), and the Transform(ArgumentListSyntax?) overload exists (MetaSyntaxRewriter.cs:171-173). The annotator needs no change: VisitArgument (TemplateAnnotator.cs:1319) already classifies the arguments.
findings.consequence_class: Assertion or crash (before regeneration); no impact after regeneration.
findings.proposed_change: None beyond TP-1 and TP-2; add a template test Tests/Syntax/CollectionExpressions/WithElement_RunTime.cs and _CompileTime.cs with @LanguageVersion(15.0) once the stable grammar is consumed, so that the regenerated path is pinned.
findings.confidence: Verified (annotator and Transform<T> path), plausible (the base visitor cast).

findings.title: unsafe(...) expressions are not rejected by the annotator
findings.what_happens_today: The unsafe statement is reported as LAMA0101 (TemplateAnnotator.cs:2594-2599, pinned by UnsafeNotSupported.t.cs). The unsafe(...) expression is a new node with no override, so DefaultVisitImpl annotates it with the combined scope of its inner expression and no diagnostic is reported. The expression is only parseable under preview, which VerifyLanguageVersion refuses with LAMA0051 unless MetalamaAllowPreviewLanguageFeatures is true (CompileTimeAspectPipeline.cs:65-76). With the flag, in run-time scope the generated visitors have no VisitUnsafeExpression, so the base rewriter rebuilds an UnsafeExpressionSyntax whose inner expression is the meta-expression; the cast to ExpressionSyntax in Transform<T> succeeds, and the compiled template contains unsafe(SyntaxFactory...). That code is then compiled by the compile-time compilation. If Roslyn rejects the preview expression there, the user sees LAMA0xxx CannotEmitCompileTimeAssembly plus the CS error, located in the generated compile-time file rather than in the template (CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.cs:641-647). If Roslyn accepts it, unsafe(e) evaluates to e at compile time and the unsafe( wrapper disappears from the generated run-time code without any diagnostic.
findings.consequence_class: Diagnostic reported in the wrong place, or silent wrong output, depending on an unverified Roslyn behaviour.
findings.proposed_change: (1) Report LAMA0101 for the expression like for the statement. The type cannot be named from the annotator while it is experimental and while the 5.0.0 variant compiles the same source, so extend the generator: instead of dropping experimental nodes, TreeReader records their names, and Generator.GenerateVersionChecker emits a static readonly string[] ExperimentalKindNames in RoslynVersionSyntaxVerifier.g.cs; the hand-written RoslynVersionSyntaxVerifier resolves them once through Enum.TryParse<SyntaxKind> and reports LAMA0101 from an override of VisitCore when node.Kind() matches. This also covers any experimental node that a future Roslyn adds, and it needs no #if. (2) Add Tests/UnsupportedSyntax/UnsafeExpressionNotSupported.cs with @LanguageVersion(preview), @AllowPreviewLanguageFeatures (check the test option name in TestOptions.cs) and an expected LAMA0101.
findings.size: S for the guard, M if the generator refactoring is done together with TP-1.
findings.confidence: Verified (annotator and rewriter paths), plausible (compile-time compilation outcome).
open_questions: Whether the experimental field BreakStatementSyntax.Name can be detected by the same guard; a BreakStatementSyntax with an IdentifierNameSyntax child is the only observable sign without naming the property.

findings.title: A union declaration nested in a compile-time class is copied verbatim; nested in a run-time class it is dropped
findings.what_happens_today: In a compile-time type, the member switch lists ClassDeclaration, StructDeclaration, InterfaceDeclaration, RecordDeclaration and RecordStructDeclaration as nested types (:540-544); a UnionDeclaration member hits default: and is passed to this.Visit(member) (:555-558). No VisitUnionDeclaration override exists (:204-234), so the base rewriter copies the union, including its members, into the compile-time syntax tree without AddToManifestIfNecessary, without TransformMethodDeclaration for any template inside it, and without the accessibility and TypeFabric checks applied to classes. In a run-time type, PopulateNestedCompileTimeTypes handles ClassDeclaration (:274-357) and the struct, interface, record, enum and delegate kinds (:359-374); a nested union falls into default: (:376-378) and is ignored even when it is compile-time, so compile-time code referencing it fails in the compile-time compilation. The annotator's VisitTypeDeclaration overrides (TemplateAnnotator.cs:743-754) and the validator's overrides (TemplatingCodeValidator.Visitor.cs:299-323) have the same lists. The compile-time compilation is created with C# 14 parse options (CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.cs:349-354), so whether a copied union compiles depends on TP-8 and on where Roslyn checks IDS_FeatureUnions. Outside this theme but on the same path: SourceNamedTypeImpl.TypeKind throws InvalidOperationException for any Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.TypeKind other than the six listed (:69-78); FACTS records no new TypeKind for unions, and this has to be confirmed by the code-model analyst.
findings.consequence_class: Silent wrong output (missing manifest entry, missing classification, dropped nested compile-time union); diagnostic reported (compile-time compilation errors) when references break.
findings.proposed_change: After regeneration, add SyntaxKind.UnionDeclaration to the three switch lists and add VisitUnionDeclaration overrides beside VisitRecordDeclaration in ProduceCompileTimeCodeRewriter, TemplateAnnotator and TemplatingCodeValidator.Visitor. The 5.0.0 variant cannot name UnionDeclarationSyntax; either route the union through the existing TypeDeclarationSyntax code by testing member is TypeDeclarationSyntax instead of listing kinds (the union node derives from TypeDeclarationSyntax, Syntax-5.10.0.xml:1954), which needs no variant branch, or accept a #if ROSLYN_5_10_0_OR_GREATER (see TP-8 for the doctrine conflict). Prefer the type test. Add an aspect test Tests/Aspects/CSharp15/Unions/Union_NestedInAspect.cs and Union_NestedInRunTimeType.cs with @LanguageVersion(15.0).
open_questions: Whether a union declaration in a run-time type must be un-nested like a TypeFabric (probably not; report RunTimeTypesCannotHaveCompileTimeTypesExceptTypeFabrics as for structs).

findings.title: Extension blocks in compile-time classes are copied verbatim; extension indexers add nothing new
findings.what_happens_today: An ExtensionBlockDeclaration member of a compile-time static class hits default: and is copied by the base rewriter. ProduceCompileTimeCodeRewriter overrides no VisitMethodDeclaration, VisitPropertyDeclaration or VisitIndexerDeclaration (override list at :147-1778), so members inside the block, including [Template] members, are copied without template compilation and without manifest entries. This is the C# 14 state; an extension indexer (an IndexerDeclarationSyntax inside the block) takes the same path. The explicit throw new NotImplementedException("Indexers are not implemented.") (:515-516) applies only to an indexer that is a direct member of a compile-time type. The template test suites contain no aspect with an extension block (every extension( occurrence in the tests is in target code, for example Tests/Aspects/CSharp14/ExtensionMembers/ExtensionMembers_IntroduceMethod.cs). A grep of ExtensionBlockDeclaration in Metalama.Framework.Engine matches only in Linking/, Pipeline/DesignTime/ and AdviceImpl/Introduction/.
findings.consequence_class: No impact specific to C# 15 (the gap exists for C# 14 extension blocks); assertion or crash for a direct indexer in a compile-time type (pre-existing).
findings.proposed_change: No C# 15 work. Record the pre-existing gap as an issue: either support templates in extension blocks (route ExtensionBlockDeclaration through VisitTypeDeclaration, since it is a TypeDeclarationSyntax in Roslyn 5.x) or report a diagnostic when a [Template] is declared inside an extension block.
findings.size: S for the diagnostic, M for support.

findings.title: Raising the template language to C# 15
findings.what_happens_today:
Where the decision is made: TemplateCompiler.TemplateLanguageVersion is ILanguageVersionProvider.GetCompileTimeLanguageVersion() (TemplateCompiler.cs:51), overridden by MetalamaTemplateLanguageVersion when set and contained in SupportedCSharpVersions.All (:58-79). LanguageVersionProvider returns the minimum of the SDK-derived version (>= 10 => CSharp14, :54-60) and the project's LangVersion (:62-71); on the msbuild.exe path it uses GetMaxLanguageVersion of the bundled Roslyn (:111). The same value is the MaximalAcceptableLanguageVersion of the verifier and the parse-option version of the compile-time compilation (CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.cs:349-354, :425-433).

How the constant is tested: Standalone/TemplateLanguageVersion14 (README, and Test.cs using field), which asserts that a template may be written in C# 14 and states that the value is bounded by RoslynApiMinVersion; CompileTimeCompilationBuilderTests.TemplateLanguageVersion (:1914-1967) which checks the manifest's LanguageVersion; the aspect tests Tests/Aspects/LanguageVersion/*_OldVersion.cs which pin LAMA0282 with @LanguageVersion(10); Tests/Aspects/LanguageVersion/LanguageVersionPreview.cs and Tests/Aspects/Misc/LanguageVersion.cs which pin the LAMA0051 and LAMA0052 message texts including the list of supported versions (.t.cs files); and TestLanguageVersionProvider which returns SupportedCSharpVersions.Latest for unit tests (Metalama.Testing.UnitTesting/TestLanguageVersionProvider.cs:12).

What must change to accept C# 15 while a .NET 10 SDK host still compiles the compile-time compilation: (1) Latest => CSharp15 and All including CSharp15, through AllLanguageVersions.CSharp15 because Roslyn 5.0 has no LanguageVersion.CSharp15 member; (2) LanguageVersionProvider: >= 11 => CSharp15, >= 10 => CSharp14 (the cap on a .NET 10 SDK host is then C# 14, which is what keeps that host working); (3) ToLanguageVersion and GetMaxLanguageVersion as in TP-2; (4) ToDisplayStringSafe: (LanguageVersion) 1500 => "15.0", otherwise LAMA0051 and LAMA0052 throw ArgumentOutOfRangeException while formatting the supported list (LanguageVersionExtensions.cs:39, SupportedCSharpVersions.cs:45); (5) Metalama.Framework.targets:118: add '15.0' to the accepted implicit LangVersion values, otherwise a net11.0 project is rewritten to C# 12 with the MetalamaCheckLangVersion warning (FACTS, line 22); (6) update the .t.cs expectations that list the supported versions.

The variant problem: the 5.0.0 variant is compiled from the same source against Roslyn 5.0, whose parser does not know C# 15; SupportedCSharpVersions.DefaultParseOptions is Latest (:50) and every aspect test parses with it (BaseTestRunner.cs:216), and MSBuildProjectOptions.LanguageVersion falls back to Latest when the host cannot parse the project's LangVersion (:167-181). A Latest of 1500 on Roslyn 5.0 would therefore make the 5.0.0 variant use an unknown version everywhere. The 2026.x code solved the same situation with #if ROSLYN_5_0_0_OR_GREATER around Latest and All (commit 08d065a9), which the current doctrine forbids (testing.md:58, comment in Roslyn.5.10.0.props). Either the doctrine gets a documented exception for SupportedCSharpVersions.Latest and All, or Latest is derived at run time from RoslynApiVersion.Current.ToLanguageVersion(), which is a constant per variant without a preprocessor branch; the second form is recommended.

The design-time floor: Directory.Build.props:11-16 explains that the repository's own templates are bounded by RoslynApiMinVersion (5.0.0), so MetalamaTemplateLanguageVersion stays 14.0 for Metalama's own aspects. For user projects, mapping SDK 11 to C# 15 makes the default template language C# 15, and the compile-time assembly of such a project cannot be built inside Rider 2026.2 (Roslyn 5.0 host, PB-2027.0). This is a product decision: either keep the SDK 11 default at C# 14 and require MetalamaTemplateLanguageVersion=15.0 as an opt-in until RoslynApiMinVersion is 5.10, or accept the Rider limitation.

Tests to copy for C# 15: Tests/Aspects/CSharp14/ (one directory per feature; NullConditionalAssignment_Template.cs shows a C# 14 construct in a template, FieldKeyword_Template.cs shows one in an introduced accessor, ExtensionMembers_*.cs show target code); Tests/Aspects/LanguageVersion/ for LAMA0282; Standalone/TemplateLanguageVersion14 for LAMA0232 (copy as TemplateLanguageVersion15); Tests/Aspects/DesignTimeInvalidCode/UnknownAccessorInTemplate.cs:5-8 for @RequiredConstant(ROSLYN_5_10_0_OR_GREATER). Note that @LanguageVersion(15.0) is enough to skip a test on the 5.0.0 variant: an integral version that Roslyn does not recognise sets SkipReason instead of throwing (TestOptions.cs:681-699), so @RequiredConstant is only needed when the expected output differs. There is no CSharp14 directory in Metalama.Framework.Tests.TemplateTests/Tests (categories at Tests/: Dynamic, Syntax, UnsupportedSyntax, ...), so C# 15 template-compiler tests would be the first of their kind there; Tests/Syntax/ is the natural place.
findings.consequence_class: Build or restore error (ToDisplayStringSafe throw in LAMA0051/LAMA0052 paths, .t.cs mismatches) if the constants are raised piecemeal; no impact until then.
findings.proposed_change: Raise the six constants: (1) SupportedCSharpVersions.Latest => CSharp15 and All including CSharp15, through AllLanguageVersions.CSharp15 (AllLanguageVersions.cs:14-18) because Roslyn 5.0 has no LanguageVersion.CSharp15 member; (2) LanguageVersionProvider.cs:54-60: >= 11 => CSharp15, >= 10 => CSharp14; (3) ToLanguageVersion and GetMaxLanguageVersion (SupportedCSharpVersions.cs:52-62, :149-159) as in TP-2; (4) ToDisplayStringSafe (LanguageVersionExtensions.cs:33-39): (LanguageVersion) 1500 => "15.0"; (5) Metalama.Framework.targets:118: add '15.0' to the accepted implicit LangVersion values; (6) update the .t.cs expectations that list the supported versions. Resolve the variant problem either by a documented exception to the doctrine (testing.md:58, Roslyn.5.10.0.props) for SupportedCSharpVersions.Latest and All, or by deriving Latest at run time from RoslynApiVersion.Current.ToLanguageVersion(), which is a constant per variant without a preprocessor branch; the second form is recommended. Keep the repository-wide MetalamaTemplateLanguageVersion at 14.0 (Directory.Build.props:11-16) while RoslynApiMinVersion is 5.0.0. Take the product decision on the SDK 11 default: either keep it at C# 14 and require MetalamaTemplateLanguageVersion=15.0 as an opt-in until RoslynApiMinVersion is 5.10, or accept the Rider 2026.2 limitation. Copy tests from Tests/Aspects/CSharp14/, Tests/Aspects/LanguageVersion/ (LAMA0282), Standalone/TemplateLanguageVersion14 (as TemplateLanguageVersion15, LAMA0232) and Tests/Aspects/DesignTimeInvalidCode/UnknownAccessorInTemplate.cs:5-8 (@RequiredConstant(ROSLYN_5_10_0_OR_GREATER)); place C# 15 template-compiler tests under Metalama.Framework.Tests.TemplateTests/Tests/Syntax/.
findings.size: M (constants, tests, doctrine text); the product decision is separate.
open_questions: The Rider default: whether to keep the SDK 11 default template language at C# 14 with MetalamaTemplateLanguageVersion=15.0 as an opt-in until RoslynApiMinVersion is 5.10, or to accept that the compile-time assembly of such a project cannot be built inside Rider 2026.2 (Roslyn 5.0 host).
Whether CSharpParseOptions on Roslyn 5.0 rejects (LanguageVersion) 1500 with an error or accepts it silently, which decides how a C# 15 compile-time assembly fails in a Roslyn 5.0 host.

findings.title: The design-time hashers do not hash the stripped members
findings.what_happens_today: The generated VisitBreakStatement hashes only the fields of the stripped grammar and does not call the base walker, so a change of the label of a compile-time break in a template does not change the CompileTimeCodeHasher hash, and DiffStrategy treats the tree as unchanged (DiffStrategy.cs:78-83). For the three new node types there is no override, so CSharpSyntaxWalker.DefaultVisit walks child nodes but not tokens (BaseCodeHasher is created with SyntaxWalkerDepth.Node by default, SafeSyntaxWalker.cs:39); renaming a union, which changes only the identifier token, does not change either hash. RunTimeCodeHasher skips bodies anyway (Generator.cs:656-663), so for run-time code only the union identifier case applies.
findings.consequence_class: Silent wrong output at design time (stale compile-time assembly or stale generated partial classes until another edit), before regeneration; no impact after regeneration.
findings.proposed_change: None beyond TP-1; add the union rename case to Metalama.Framework.Tests.UnitTests/Utilities/HasherTests.cs once regeneration has happened.

findings.title: The closed modifier and patterns over union types need nothing from the template compiler
findings.what_happens_today: Modifiers are SyntaxList<SyntaxToken> and are transformed token by token through Transform(SyntaxToken), which emits Token(SyntaxKind.ClosedKeyword) by name (:274, :288-293); no grammar entry is involved. A switch or is over a union value uses existing pattern nodes, and the annotator derives the scope from the switched expression (:1533-1556, :2877-2945). In compile-time scope a closed compile-time class is copied verbatim into the compile-time compilation, whose parse options are C# 14 until TP-8; modifier feature checks are performed on source symbols in Roslyn (assumption), so this would surface as a CS error under CannotEmitCompileTimeAssembly.
findings.consequence_class: No impact (templating); diagnostic reported (compile-time compilation) until TP-8.
findings.proposed_change: None. Whether the code model exposes closed is a code-model theme.
findings.confidence: Verified for templating; plausible for the compile-time compilation.

non_findings: CompileTimeCodeFastDetector inspects only using directives and returns false from DefaultVisit (Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/CompileTime/CompileTimeCodeFastDetector.cs:45-83); new node kinds cannot affect it.

The fallback of the template annotator for an unknown node kind is DefaultVisitImpl (Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/Templating/TemplateAnnotator.cs:627-643), which visits the children and combines the scopes of expression children (TemplateAnnotator.cs:686-697); it neither throws nor reports. The fallback of the template compiler rewriter is the base CSharpSyntaxRewriter visitor; a crash occurs only where that base visitor casts a transformed child to a node type (TP-3, TP-4). The default: branch of MetaSyntaxRewriter.Transform<T> throws AssertionFailedException only for non-transformed nodes that are neither expressions, arguments nor statements (Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/Templating/MetaSyntaxRewriter.cs:131-132); a WithElementSyntax in compile-time scope inside a run-time collection expression would reach it, which is the same crash class as TP-4.

Metalama.Framework.Analyzers (shipped to users through Metalama.Framework.Package.csproj:76-80) registers only operation actions (ImmutableContractAnalyzer.WriteSites.cs:61-70, DurableContractAnalyzer.UseSites.cs:80-92) and has no switch over SyntaxKind or TypeKind with a throwing default (grep of _ => throw, default: followed by throw, and TypeKind in the project: no match).

Metalama.Framework.Engine.Analyzers is an internal-only package (Metalama.Framework.Engine.Analyzers.csproj, InternalOnlyPackage); its three throwing defaults (MetalamaAssertionAnalyzer.cs:83, MetalamaPerformanceAnalyzer.cs:80, MetalamaPerformanceAnalyzer.cs:157) switch over IOperation types that the registration restricts to Invocation and MethodReference (:67-70, :60, :71); KindCheckOptimizationAnalyzer registers syntax actions for IsPatternExpression, SwitchStatement and SwitchExpression (KindCheckOptimizationAnalyzer.cs:66-76) and its pattern helpers return false for unknown shapes (KindCheckOptimizationAnalyzer.cs:472-500).

AdditionalDiagnosticAnalyzer (Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/Analyzers/AdditionalDiagnosticAnalyzer.cs:31, :43-46) returns early for any TypeKind other than class, struct or interface.

RoslynApiVersion.g.cs and every file of the 5.0.0 generated directory are unchanged by the stable grammar (eng/src/GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter/GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter.cs:30-37, eng/src/GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter/Generator.cs:64-98).

The -stubs fallback include (Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/Metalama.Framework.Engine.csproj:38, Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.DesignTime/Metalama.Framework.DesignTime.csproj:35) and the PrepareStubs property (eng/src/Program.cs:168) are declared but nothing in eng/src produces a stubs directory; they are inert.

SyntaxTreeStructureVerifier.VerifyMetaSyntax (test support, Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Testing.AspectTesting/SyntaxTreeStructureVerifier.cs:26-46) and SyntaxFactoryDebugHelper (Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/SyntaxGeneration/SyntaxFactoryDebugHelper.cs:19-31) use MetaSyntaxRewriter with RoslynApiVersion.Current and DefaultParseOptions; they follow TP-1 and TP-8 automatically.

TextSpanClassifier.DefaultVisit (Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/Formatting/TextSpanClassifier.cs:278-295) and ReferenceIndexWalker.DefaultVisit (Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/ReferenceGraph/ReferenceIndexWalker.cs:97-101) walk children for unknown kinds and do not throw.

TemplatingCodeValidator.Visitor.VisitCore (Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/Templating/TemplatingCodeValidator.Visitor.cs:95-131) validates references after visiting children and has no per-kind switch that throws; its only throwing switch (TemplatingCodeValidator.Visitor.cs:1111-1128) is reached from ReportSuppressions (:1086) for declaration nodes that carry a well-known warning suppression, and the declaration kinds it lists are the ones the visitor's own Visit*Declaration overrides pass in (:478-813); a union declaration has no such override and does not reach it.

The aspect test infrastructure already supports C# 15 tests on a mixed-variant build: @LanguageVersion(15.0) skips the test on the 5.0.0 variant (Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Testing.AspectTesting/TestOptions.cs:681-699), and @RequiredConstant(ROSLYN_5_10_0_OR_GREATER) is available when the expected output differs (eng/RoslynVersions/Roslyn.5.10.0.props).

The compiler entry point does not stop on input errors (Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/Pipeline/SourceTransformer.cs:91-140, no diagnostic check), but the template compiler does (Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/Templating/TemplateCompiler.cs:159-217) and VerifyLanguageVersion rejects C# 15 and preview (Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/Pipeline/CompileTime/CompileTimeAspectPipeline.cs:62-90), so none of the template paths above is reachable in 2026.x without MetalamaAllowPreviewLanguageFeatures.

notes:
Wrote the reference document (544 lines). It carries no findings, so `included_ids` and `withdrawn_ids` are empty by construction.

Structure: an introduction that states the document is a reference and points to `platform-support.md`, `Directory.Packages.md`, `updating-roslyn.md` and to `analysis-reports/08-roslyn-api-delta.md`; then five sections. "The Roslyn versions" gives the snapshot table, the published-version table (5.0.0, 5.3.0, 5.6.0, 5.9.0 stable, the consumed 5.10.0-1.26365.3 prerelease, the non-existent 5.11 package, the expected 5.12 of November 2026), the three commits that separate the consumed build from `main` (dotnet/roslyn#84707, #84799 of 2026-08-11, #84738) and a comparison table of how C# 15 appears in each snapshot. "The public API delta" holds the two required tables, each row with a factual relevance cell, followed by the experimental markers, the grammar file and the list of what is unchanged. "The semantics of the C# 15 features" has one subsection per feature (unions, closed hierarchies, labeled break and continue, collection expression arguments, extension indexers, static members in interfaces) plus unsafe evolution, each with the proposal link, the syntax, the lowering, the restrictions and the diagnostics. Pre-compilation source outputs is a separate short section, marked as a generator API and not a language feature. "The local inventory" gives the per-enumeration switch counts (326 switches, 146 throwing default arms), the per-base-class visitor counts (118 classes) and the type-declaration kind sites that omit `UnionDeclaration`, pointing to the report for the per-file lists. The last section reproduces what could not be verified.

Reconciliations made against the addendum of FACTS.md: the timeline is presented with 5.12 as the expected November 2026 stable, the 5.11 label is used only as a state of `main` and never as a package, and `LanguageVersion.CSharp15` is stated as absent from every Roslyn that Metalama consumes today.

One correction to the research report: its API table cell says that seventeen visitors override `VisitClassDeclaration`, `VisitStructDeclaration` or `VisitRecordDeclaration`, while its own list names twenty production visitors and three test runners. I re-counted with a grep over `/home/user/Metalama/Metalama.Framework/src` on 2026-09-04, obtained exactly the twenty production files and three test runners of the report's list (plus one aspect test input, which the report's convention excludes), and the document states twenty and three with a sentence saying that the seventeen is superseded. I also re-verified the line numbers of `SyntaxKindExtensions.cs` (`IsTypeDeclaration` is at line 33, `IsBaseTypeDeclaration` at 41, `IsRecordDeclaration` at 100, where the report wrote 34-35) and spot-checked `SourceNamedTypeImpl.cs:173`, `SourceMethod.cs:174`, `BaseSourceGenerator.cs:28`, `MetalamaSourceGenerator.cs:14`, `TemplateAnnotator.cs:1375`, `TemplateExpansionContext.cs:827` and `CompileTimeCompilationBuilder.cs:520`.

No other file was created or modified; `git status` shows only the new document as untracked. No build and no test was run. The document contains no em dash, no contraction and no bold emphasis.

findings.title: Stable Roslyn 5.10 transition edits that remain after Premium#85

findings.title: `ChangeVisibilityCodeAction` silently skips union, interface and indexer declarations
findings.what_happens_today: `ChangeVisibilityCodeAction.cs:72-116` has overrides for class, record, struct, field, event, event field, property, enum, delegate, constructor, method, destructor, accessor, operator and conversion operator only; the public `ChangeAccessibility` in `CodeFixFactory.cs:101-117` accepts any `IMemberOrNamedType`. The rewriter derives from the core `SafeSyntaxRewriter`, which visits an unhandled node through the default visit. A `UnionDeclarationSyntax` (a `TypeDeclarationSyntax`, `/home/user/Metalama/eng/src/GenerateMetaSyntaxRewriter/Syntax-5.10.0.xml:1954-1978`), an `InterfaceDeclarationSyntax` and an `IndexerDeclarationSyntax` are visited but `ChangeModifiers` is never applied to them. `ExecuteAsync` then calls `context.UpdateTree` with an unchanged root (`ChangeVisibilityCodeAction.cs:46-48`), and `CodeActionContext.ToCodeActionResult` reports the file as changed (`CodeActionContext.cs:82-93`). The user sees the code fix succeed and nothing change. The interface and indexer cases exist today; C# 15 adds the union case.
findings.consequence_class: Silent wrong output.
findings.proposed_change: Replace the per-kind overrides on type declarations with one override of `Visit(SyntaxNode?)` that applies `TypeDeclarationSyntax.WithModifiers` to any `TypeDeclarationSyntax` (this covers interfaces, extension blocks, and unions without naming the union node, which is experimental in 5.10.0-1.26365.3 and absent from the 5.0 variant), add `VisitIndexerDeclaration`, and add aspect tests `ChangeVisibility_Interface` and `ChangeVisibility_Indexer`. A union test needs the stable Roslyn 5.10 grammar and `LangVersion` 15, and Premium defines no `ROSLYN_5_10_0_OR_GREATER`; if PR-2 adds the 5.0 test shims, the union test needs a `@RequiredConstant` and Premium must define the constant in `Roslyn.5.10.0.props` as core does.
findings.confidence: verified for the missing overrides; plausible for the union syntax shape, which the FACTS file records as experimental in the consumed build.

findings.title: `ReferenceValidationContext.GetInboundGranularity` throws for a validated extension block
findings.what_happens_today: The switch at `ReferenceValidationContext.cs:124-134` lists Constructor, Event, Method, Field, Property, Indexer, Compilation, AssemblyReference, Namespace, NamedType, Parameter, TypeParameter and Attribute, and throws `ArgumentOutOfRangeException` otherwise; it is called from the `Destination` property at line 56-57. The core repository treats an extension block as a valid validated declaration (`/home/user/Metalama/Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework.Engine/ReferenceGraph/ReferenceIndexerRequirements.cs:36,73`), exposes `DeclarationKind.ExtensionBlock` (`/home/user/Metalama/Metalama.Framework/src/Metalama.Framework/Code/DeclarationKind.cs:115-118`) and `INamedType.ExtensionBlocks` (`INamedType.cs:187`), and `IExtensionBlock` is an `INamedType` (`IExtensionBlock.cs:11`). A fabric can therefore write `.SelectMany(t => t.ExtensionBlocks).CanOnlyBeUsedFrom(...)`, which accepts `IQuery<IDeclaration>` (`ArchitectureExtensions.cs:34-39`). `ReferenceValidatorRunner` aggregates the references to the members of the validated symbol onto it (`ReferenceValidatorRunner.cs:111`, `ChildKinds.All`), so the validator runs, reads `context.Destination`, and throws. C# 15 extension indexers are declared inside extension blocks, which makes the block a more likely validation target than in C# 14.
findings.consequence_class: Assertion or crash. The exception is raised inside the user validator and reported by `UserCodeInvoker` as an error diagnostic; the rule reports nothing else.
findings.proposed_change: Map `DeclarationKind.ExtensionBlock` to `ReferenceGranularity.Type` and add a Validation aspect test that validates an extension block with an extension method, and on the latest variant an extension indexer.
findings.confidence: verified for the switch; plausible for the reachability, which the author traced through the query API without running it.
open_questions: Whether the core `DeclarationFactory` maps the indexer symbol of an extension type to an `IIndexer` whose `DeclaringType` is the `IExtensionBlock`; if it does not, the failure is in core before Premium is reached.

findings.title: Architecture rules under `closed` classes and unions
findings.what_happens_today: The core drops derived-type indexing only for `INamedType.IsSealed`. A `closed` class is not sealed, so `DerivedTypesMustRespectNamingConvention`, `ValidateDerivedTypes` and `InternalOnlyImplement` keep working; the compiler already confines derivation of a closed class to its assembly, so the transitive validator that Premium persists for other projects (`TransitiveValidatorInstance.cs`) becomes redundant for it but harmless. A union declares its case types in a `ParameterList` (`Syntax-5.10.0.xml:1965`), so a `CanOnlyBeUsedFrom` rule on a case type reports the union declaration as a `ParameterType` reference whose origin is the union type, and `pet is Cat c` in a switch is reported as `IsType`, as for any class. `DerivedTypesMustRespectNamingConvention` applied to a union validates nothing, because case types do not derive from it.
findings.consequence_class: No impact, subject to the open questions.
findings.proposed_change: None in Premium. Add two aspect tests on the latest variant once the union syntax is stable: `CanOnlyBeUsedFrom` on a case type referenced by a union, and `DerivedTypesMustRespectNamingConvention` on a `closed` class.
findings.confidence: plausible. The union symbol shape depends on the stable Roslyn 5.10, which the author could not read.
open_questions: The `TypeKind` that the core code model assigns to a union symbol; `TypeKind.cs` has no union member and the FACTS file states that the core knows nothing of `UnionDeclarationSyntax`.
Whether a `ReferenceKinds` member for a union case is wanted, so that users can filter it apart from `ParameterType`; that is a core API question.

findings.title: Variant set alignment (theme 1) is implemented by Premium#85
where: the pr85 diff against develop/2027.0, 47 files
findings.what_happens_today: The items requested by the coordinator, verified in the post-change tree: `eng/RoslynVersions/Roslyn.4.12.0.props` deleted; `Roslyn.5.0.0.props` with `ThisRoslynVersionProjectSuffix` `.5.0.0`, `System.Text.Json` and `System.IO.Pipelines` 9.0.0, `System.Memory` 4.6.3, `Unsafe` 6.1.2; `Roslyn.5.10.0.props` with `ThisRoslynVersion=$(RoslynApiMaxVersion)`, `NoPreview` 5.10.0, empty suffix, 10.0.11 pins; `Latest.props` importing 5.10.0; the three shim directories renamed to `.5.0.0` and the solution updated; `Directory.Packages.props` with `RoslynVersion`/`RoslynMaxVersion` 5.10.0-1.26365.3 and `Metalama.Framework.Implementation.5.10.0` and `.5.0.0` (4.12.0 removed); `nuget.base.config` with the roslyn-consolidated feed and the `Microsoft.CodeAnalysis.*` mapping (identical to core `nuget.base.config` apart from one comment word); `InternalsVisibleTo` for `Engine.5.10.0`, `DesignTime.5.10.0`, `Engine.5.0.0`, `DesignTime.5.0.0` in `Metalama.Extensions.CodeFixes.csproj:17-20` and `Engine.5.10.0`/`Engine.5.0.0` in `Metalama.Extensions.Validation.csproj:16-17`; the `Package.Resources` project references; the `_AddAssembliesToOutput` lists (`CodeFixes.Package.csproj:53-62`, `Validation.Package.csproj:46-51`) and the build props with `TargetRoslynVersion` 5.10.0 and 5.0.0 and `TargetFramework` `net472`/`net10.0`; no `DefineConstants` in either variant; no `@RequiredConstant`, `@ForbiddenConstant` or `RequiredConstants` anywhere in `src/tests` (grep), and the two `metalamaTests.json` files carry only `FormatOutput` and `RemoveOutputCode`. `develop/2027.0` without #85 fails restore with `NU1101` on `Metalama.Framework.Implementation.4.12.0` and `NU1701` on the `net8.0` projects, as #1913 records.
findings.consequence_class: Build or restore error until #85 merges.
findings.proposed_change: Merge #85. The residuals are PR-1 (stable transition), PR-2 (5.0 variant tests) and PR-13 (comment).

non_findings: Premium production and test source contains no `#if ROSLYN_*` block, no `@RequiredConstant` or `@ForbiddenConstant` directive and no `RequiredConstants` entry (grep over `/home/user/metalama.premium/src` and `eng`; the only `ROSLYN_` hits are the two props files and the two csproj comments of PR-13).

No Premium source duplicates `SupportedCSharpVersions`, `LanguageVersionProvider`, `RoslynApiVersion` or `ResourceExtractor`: a grep for `LanguageVersion`, `RoslynVersion`, `GetManifestResourceStream`, `AssemblyLoadContext` and `AssemblyResolve` over `src` finds only `src/tests/Metalama.Patterns.Caching.Backends.UnitTests/RedisServer/RedisTestInstance.cs:49`, which extracts the embedded `redis-server.exe` for the tests.

The Roslyn API surface used by the Premium design-time code is `CodeAction`, `ApplyChangesOperation`, `Document`, `Solution`, `SyntaxFactory.Comment` and `SyntaxNode.FindNode` (`LamaCodeAction.cs`, `CodeActionDescriptorExtensions.cs`, `PremiumCodeFixProviderExtension.cs:73-91`, `CodeFixService.cs:191-231`). The tests implement the Metalama abstractions `ICodeFixContext` and `ICodeRefactoringContext` (`TestCodeFixContext.cs`, `TestCodeRefactoringContext.cs`), not the Roslyn `CodeFixContext` constructors. No Roslyn 5.10 API break was found.

`AddAttributeCodeAction` (`AddAttributeCodeAction.cs:44-56`) special-cases only `VariableDeclarator` and delegates to the core `SyntaxGenerator.AddAttribute`; `RemoveAttributeRewriter` (`RemoveAttributeCodeAction.RemoveAttributeRewriter.cs:27-54`) visits `AttributeSyntax` and `AttributeListSyntax` only. Both are independent of the declaration kind, so unions and extension indexers add no case there. The `switch` statements with a throwing default in Premium are over `Accessibility` (`ChangeVisibilityCodeAction.cs:142-178`, `CodeFixFactory.cs:103-112`), `ReferenceGranularity` (`ReferenceEnd.cs:91-108`), `DeclarationValidationTime` (`ValidationReferenceValidationQueryService.cs:16-23`) and a menu item kind (`CodeActionMenuBuilder.cs:62`); none of them is over `SyntaxKind`, and the only one over `DeclarationKind` is PR-11.

Extension indexers as referenced members: `ReferenceValidatorQuerySource.cs:54-74` and `DynamicReferenceValidatorQuerySource.cs:51-67` map accessor validators to `DeclaringMember`, `ReferenceValidationContext.cs:127-128` maps `Indexer` to `Member`, `ReferenceEnd.cs:97-99` resolves the type through `GetClosestNamedType`, and the core walker enters indexer declarations wherever they appear (`ReferenceIndexWalker.cs:590-600`) and supports `Default`, `Assignment`, `InterfaceMemberImplementation` and `OverrideMember` for indexers (`ReferenceIndexerRequirements.cs:82-83`). Nothing in Premium depends on the indexer being declared in a class rather than in an extension block.

`ExperimentalAttribute` (`ExperimentalAttribute.cs:37-56`), `InternalsCanOnlyBeUsedFrom` (`ArchitectureExtensions.cs:130-175`), `NamespacePredicate`, `AssemblyNamePredicate` and `TypeNamePredicate` reason about accessibility, namespaces and names only and are unaffected by `closed`, unions or extension indexers.

notes:
Scope of the review: the consistency lens only. I did not check duplication against GitHub issues, and I did not review the copywriting rules except where a sentence was factually inconsistent.

Identifier audit. Every identifier of the required list appears in the draft, and each of the 89 identifiers is assigned exactly once, either to the Findings line of a story or to a bullet of "Findings not turned into a story". The repeated occurrences (CM-7 three times, CM-4, LK-5, LV-9, PR-4, PR-8, PR-15, UT-1, UT-2, UT-5, UT-6, UT-7 and UT-8 twice each) are cross-references in the decision sections and in "Already in progress", not second assignments. The introduction nevertheless claims that each identifier occurs once, which is corrected above. The assignment of CM-4 and LK-5 changes if the closed writer story is added, and the count "Thirteen" then becomes "Eleven".

Blocked-by audit against /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-Metalama/ccf204f4-b0b3-5fe6-a8de-fe20f6791d2c/scratchpad/FACTS.md. The rule "Roslyn 5.12 before the C# 15 language version" holds: S-11 is blocked by S-09, and S-09 by S-01. The rule "the variant gating decision before union and closed code" holds for S-12 and S-18 directly and for S-13, S-14, S-15, S-17 and S-22 through S-12, and fails for S-19 only, which names the `Name` field of `BreakStatementSyntax` and `ContinueStatementSyntax` without depending on S-02. The rule "Premium#85 before further Premium work" fails for S-10, S-23 and S-24, all three of which declare no dependency on it while `FACTS.md` and the pull request survey both record #85 as open.

Largest single defect: the draft contradicts section 5f of `DECISIONS.md` and question Q4 of `OPEN-QUESTIONS.md` in six places by stating that closed type introduction is out of scope, and it withdraws findings CM-4 and LK-5 on that basis. That is a decision reversed after the draft was written, and it costs one story of size M.

Second largest: five stories are not deliverable by one pull request. S-07, S-22 and S-25 each list two repositories, S-23 states in its own scope that part of the work "belong[s] in a second pull request", and S-17 names a deliverable in `metalama/Metalama.Documentation`, which its metadata does not list, and makes half of its scope conditional on the open question Q1.
